questions.q: A long straight wire of radius a carries a steady current I. The current is uniformly distributed across its cross section. The ratio of the magnetic field at \(\frac a2\) and 2a from axis of the wire is :
questions.sol: Inside: \(B = \dfrac{\mu_0Ir}{2\pi a^2}\), at \(\dfrac a2\): \(\dfrac{\mu_0I}{4\pi a}\). Outside at 2a: \(\dfrac{\mu_0I}{4\pi a}\). Ratio 1 : 1.

questions.q: A block is simply released from the top of an inclined plane as shown in the figure above. The maximum compression in the spring when the block hits the spring is :
questions.sol: Drop along the smooth incline: \(10\sin30^\circ = 5\) m, energy \(5\times10\times5 = 250\) J. Rough 2 m: loses \(0.5\times50\times2 = 50\) J. \(\tfrac12(100)x^2 = 200 \Rightarrow x = 2\) m.

questions.q: The position of the image formed by the combination of lenses is :
questions.sol: Lens 1: \(u = -30\), \(f = 10\): \(v = 15\) cm, i.e. 10 cm beyond lens 2 (virtual object). Lens 2 (\(f = -10\)): \(\dfrac1v = \dfrac1{10} - \dfrac1{10} = 0\), parallel beam. Lens 3 focuses it at 30 cm to its right.

questions.q: If \(\epsilon_0\) is the permittivity of free space and E is the electric field, then \(\epsilon_0E^2\) has the dimensions :
questions.sol: \(\epsilon_0E^2\) is (twice) an energy density: \([ML^{-1}T^{-2}]\).

questions.q: Two satellite A and B go round a planet in circular orbits having radii 4R and R respectively. If the speed of A is 3v, the speed of B will be :
questions.sol: \(v \propto \dfrac{1}{\sqrt r}\): \(v_B = 3v\times\sqrt4 = 6v\).

questions.q: Water boils in an electric kettle in 20 minutes after being switched on. Using the same main supply, the length of the heating element should be ____ to ____ times of its initial length if the water is to be boiled in 15 minutes.
questions.sol: Same heat, \(t \propto R \propto l\) at fixed V. 15 min needs \(\dfrac34\) of the length: decreased.

questions.q: A diatomic gas (\(\gamma\) = 1.4) does 100 J of work in an isobaric expansion. The heat given to the gas is :
questions.sol: \(Q = \dfrac{\gamma}{\gamma - 1}W = 3.5\times100 = 350\) J.

questions.q: If \(M_0\) is the mass of isotope \({}^{12}_5B\), \(M_p\) and \(M_n\) are the masses of proton and neutron, then nuclear binding energy of isotope is:
questions.sol: Mass defect \(= 5M_p + 7M_n - M_0\); B.E. \(= (5M_p + 7M_n - M_0)c^2\).

questions.q: A given object takes n times the time to slide down 45° rough inclined plane as it takes the time to slide down an identical perfectly smooth 45° inclined plane. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the object and the surface of inclined plane is :
questions.sol: \(t \propto \dfrac{1}{\sqrt a}\): \(a_{rough} = \dfrac{a_{smooth}}{n^2}\). \(g(\sin45^\circ - \mu\cos45^\circ) = \dfrac{g\sin45^\circ}{n^2} \Rightarrow \mu = 1 - \dfrac{1}{n^2}\).

questions.q: There are 100 divisions on the circular scale of a screw gauge of pitch 1 mm. With no measuring quantity in between the jaws, the zero of the circular scale lies 5 divisions below the reference line. The diameter of a wire is then measured using this screw gauge. It is found that 4 linear scale divisions are clearly visible while 60 divisions on circular scale coincide with the reference line. The diameter of the wire is :
questions.sol: Zero error \(+5\times0.01 = +0.05\) mm. Reading \(= 4 + 0.60 = 4.60\) mm; corrected \(4.60 - 0.05 = 4.55\) mm.

questions.q: A capacitor has air as dielectric medium and two conducting plates of area 12 cm² and they are 0.6 cm apart. When a slab of dielectric having area 12 cm² and 0.6 cm thickness is inserted between the plates, one of the conducting plates has to be moved by 0.2 cm to keep the capacitance same as in previous case. The dielectric constant of the slab is : (Given \(\epsilon_0 = 8.834\times10^{-12}\) F/m)
questions.sol: Gap becomes 0.8 cm with 0.6 cm of dielectric: \(0.2 + \dfrac{0.6}{K} = 0.6 \Rightarrow K = 1.5\).

questions.q: Least count of a vernier caliper is \(\frac{1}{20N}\) cm. The value of one division on the main scale is 1 mm. Then the number of divisions of main scale that coincide with N divisions of vernier scale is :
questions.sol: LC \(= \dfrac{1}{2N}\) mm \(= 1\text{ MSD} - 1\text{ VSD}\). N VSD \(= N\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{2N}\right) = \dfrac{2N - 1}{2}\) MSD.

questions.q: A cube of ice floats partly in water and partly in kerosene oil. The ratio of volume of ice immersed in water to that in kerosene oil (specific gravity of Kerosene oil = 0.8, specific gravity of ice = 0.9):
questions.sol: Fraction x in water: \(0.9 = x(1) + (1 - x)(0.8) \Rightarrow x = 0.5\). Ratio 1 : 1.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I): The mean free path of gas molecules is inversely proportional to square of molecular diameter.
Statement (II): Average kinetic energy of gas molecules is directly proportional to absolute temperature of gas.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
o: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.sol: \(\lambda = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt2\pi d^2n}\) (I true); average KE \(= \tfrac32kT\) (II true).

questions.q: The angle of projection for a projectile to have same horizontal range and maximum height is :
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{u^2\sin2\theta}{g} = \dfrac{u^2\sin^2\theta}{2g} \Rightarrow \tan\theta = 4\).

questions.q: A proton and an electron have the same de Broglie wavelength. If \(K_p\) and \(K_e\) be the kinetic energies of proton and electron respectively, then choose the correct relation :
questions.sol: Same momentum: \(K = \dfrac{p^2}{2m}\), so the heavier proton has less KE.

questions.q: In a hypothetical fission reaction \({}^{236}_{92}X \rightarrow {}^{141}_{56}Y + {}^{92}_{36}Z + 3R\). The identity of emitted particles (R) is :
questions.sol: Mass numbers: \(236 - 141 - 92 = 3\), so A = 1 each; charges \(92 - 56 - 36 = 0\): neutrons.

questions.q: A thin circular disc of mass M and radius R is rotating in a horizontal plane about an axis passing through its centre and perpendicular to its plane with angular velocity \(\omega\). If another disc of same dimensions but of mass M/2 is placed gently on the first disc co-axially, then the new angular velocity of the system is :
questions.sol: \(\tfrac12MR^2\omega = \left(\tfrac12MR^2 + \tfrac14MR^2\right)\omega' \Rightarrow \omega' = \dfrac23\omega\).

questions.q: A coil of negligible resistance is connected in series with 90 Ω resistor across 120 V, 60 Hz supply. A voltmeter reads 36 V across resistance. Inductance of the coil is :
A plane progressive wave is given by \(y = 2\cos2\pi(330t - x)\) m. The frequency of the wave is :
questions.sol: \(y = 2\cos(2\pi\times330t - 2\pi x)\): f = 330 Hz.

questions.q: An alternating emf \(E = 110\sqrt2\sin100t\) volt is applied to a capacitor of 2 µF, the rms value of current in the circuit is ____ mA.
questions.sol: \(I_{rms} = V_{rms}\omega C = 110\times100\times2\times10^{-6} = 22\) mA.

questions.q: If the net electric field at point P along Y axis is zero, then the ratio of \(\left|\frac{q_3}{q_2}\right|\) is \(\frac{5\sqrt x}{8}\), where x = ____ .
questions.sol: \(q_2\) at \(\sqrt{20}\) cm from P, \(q_3\) at 5 cm. Equal y-components: \(\dfrac{q_2\cdot4}{20^{3/2}} = \dfrac{q_3\cdot4}{125} \Rightarrow \dfrac{q_3}{q_2} = \dfrac{125}{40\sqrt5} = \dfrac{5\sqrt5}{8}\).

questions.q: Two slits are 1 mm apart and the screen is located 1 m away from the slits. A light of wavelength 500 nm is used. The width of each slit to obtain 10 maxima of the double slit pattern within the central maximum of the single slit pattern is ____ \(\times10^{-4}\) m.
questions.sol: Fringe width \(= \dfrac{\lambda D}{d} = 0.5\) mm. Ten fringes in the central maximum: \(\dfrac{2\lambda D}{a} = 5\) mm \(\Rightarrow a = \dfrac{2\times5\times10^{-7}}{5\times10^{-3}} = 2\times10^{-4}\) m.

questions.q: A potential divider circuit is connected with a dc source of 20 V, a light emitting diode of glow in voltage 1.8 V and a zener diode of breakdown voltage of 3.2 V. The length (PR) of the resistive wire is 20 cm. The minimum length of PQ to just glow the LED is ____ cm.
questions.sol: LED + Zener need \(1.8 + 3.2 = 5\) V. The wire drops 1 V/cm, so PQ = 5 cm.

questions.q: An object of mass 0.2 kg executes simple harmonic motion along x axis with frequency of \(\left(\frac{25}{\pi}\right)\) Hz. At the position x = 0.04 m the object has kinetic energy 0.5 J and potential energy 0.4 J. The amplitude of oscillation is ____ cm.

A circular table is rotating with an angular velocity of \(\omega\) rad/s about its axis (see figure). There is a smooth groove along a radial direction on the table. A steel ball is gently placed at a distance of 1 m on the groove. All the surfaces are smooth. If the radius of the table is 3 m, the radial velocity of the ball w.r.t. the table at the time ball leaves the table is \(x\sqrt2\omega\) m/s, where the value of x is ____ .
questions.sol: In the groove \(\ddot r = \omega^2r\), so \(v_r^2 = \omega^2(r^2 - r_0^2) = 8\omega^2\): \(v_r = 2\sqrt2\omega\).

questions.q: A heater is designed to operate with a power of 1000 W in a 100 V line. It is connected in combination with a resistance of 10 Ω and a resistance R, to a 100 V mains as shown in figure. For the heater to operate at 62.5 W, the value of R should be ____ Ω.
questions.sol: Heater \(R_h = \dfrac{100^2}{1000} = 10\ \Omega\). At 62.5 W: \(V_h = 25\) V, \(I_h = 2.5\) A. The 10 Ω takes 75 V, so 7.5 A total; R carries 5 A at 25 V: \(R = 5\ \Omega\).

questions.q: Small water droplets of radius 0.01 mm are formed in the upper atmosphere and falling with a terminal velocity of 10 cm/s. Due to condensation, if 8 such droplets are coalesced and formed a larger drop, the new terminal velocity will be ____ cm/s.
questions.sol: 8 drops give radius ×2; \(v_t \propto r^2\): \(10\times4 = 40\) cm/s.

questions.q: The coercivity of a magnet is \(5\times10^3\) A/m. The amount of current required to be passed in a solenoid of length 30 cm and the number of turns 150, so that the magnet gets demagnetised when inside the solenoid is ____ A.
questions.sol: \(H = nI \Rightarrow I = \dfrac{5\times10^3\times0.3}{150} = 10\) A.

questions.q: A body of mass M thrown horizontally with velocity v from the top of the tower of height H touches the ground at a distance of 100 m from the foot of the tower. A body of mass 2M thrown at a velocity \(\frac v2\) from the top of the tower of height 4H will touch the ground at a distance of ____ m.
questions.sol: \(R = v\sqrt{\dfrac{2H}{g}}\). New: \(\dfrac v2\sqrt{\dfrac{8H}{g}} = v\sqrt{\dfrac{2H}{g}}\): still 100 m (mass doesn't matter).

questions.q: A stationary particle breaks into two parts of masses \(m_A\) and \(m_B\) which move with velocities \(v_A\) and \(v_B\) respectively. The ratio of their kinetic energies (\(K_B : K_A\)) is :
questions.sol: Equal and opposite momenta: \(K = \dfrac{p^2}{2m}\), so \(\dfrac{K_B}{K_A} = \dfrac{m_A}{m_B} = \dfrac{v_B}{v_A}\).

questions.q: Two charged conducting spheres of radii a and b are connected to each other by a conducting wire. The ratio of charges of the two spheres respectively is:
questions.sol: Same potential: \(\dfrac{q_1}{a} = \dfrac{q_2}{b}\), so \(q_1 : q_2 = a : b\).

questions.q: Two planets A and B having masses \(m_1\) and \(m_2\) move around the sun in circular orbits of \(r_1\) and \(r_2\) radii respectively. If angular momentum of A is L and that of B is 3L, the ratio of time period \(\left(\frac{T_A}{T_B}\right)\) is:
questions.sol: \(L = m\sqrt{GMr}\): \(3 = \dfrac{m_2}{m_1}\sqrt{\dfrac{r_2}{r_1}} \Rightarrow \dfrac{r_1}{r_2} = \dfrac{m_2^2}{9m_1^2}\). \(\dfrac{T_A}{T_B} = \left(\dfrac{r_1}{r_2}\right)^{3/2} = \dfrac{1}{27}\left(\dfrac{m_2}{m_1}\right)^3\).

questions.q: Average force exerted on a non-reflecting surface at normal incidence is \(2.4\times10^{-4}\) N. If 360 W/cm² is the light energy flux during span of 1 hour 30 minutes, then the area of the surface is:
questions.sol: Absorbing surface: \(F = \dfrac{IA}{c} \Rightarrow A = \dfrac{2.4\times10^{-4}\times3\times10^8}{3.6\times10^6} = 0.02\) m².

questions.q: In an expression \(a\times10^b\) :
o: a is order of magnitude for b ≤ 5
b is order of magnitude for a ≤ 5
b is order of magnitude for a ≥ 5
b is order of magnitude for 5 < a ≤ 10
questions.sol: Writing a number as \(a\times10^b\), b is its order of magnitude when \(a \le 5\) (otherwise it is b + 1).

questions.q: A clock has 75 cm, 60 cm long second hand and minute hand respectively. In 30 minutes duration the tip of second hand will travel x distance more than the tip of minute hand. The value of x in meter is nearly (Take \(\pi\) = 3.14) :
questions.sol: Second hand: 30 turns, \(30\times2\pi\times0.75 = 141.3\) m. Minute hand: half a turn, \(\pi\times0.6 = 1.88\) m. Difference ≈ 139.4 m.

questions.q: The output Y of following circuit for given inputs is :
questions.sol: Upper OR: \(A + \bar B\). Lower AND: \(\bar A B\). \(Y = (A + \bar B)\bar AB = A\bar AB + \bar AB\bar B = 0\).

questions.q: A player caught a cricket ball of mass 150 g moving at a speed of 20 m/s. If the catching process is completed in 0.1 s, the magnitude of force exerted by the ball on the hand of the player is:
Three bodies A, B and C have equal kinetic energies and their masses are 400 g, 1.2 kg and 1.6 kg respectively. The ratio of their linear momenta is :
questions.sol: \(p = \sqrt{2mK} \propto \sqrt m\): \(\sqrt{0.4} : \sqrt{1.2} : \sqrt{1.6} = 1 : \sqrt3 : 2\).

questions.q: Young's modulus is determined by the equation given by \(Y = 49000\frac Ml\) dyne/cm² where M is the mass and l is the extension of wire used in the experiment. Now error in Young modulus (Y) is estimated by taking data from M − l plot in graph paper. The smallest scale divisions are 5 g and 0.02 cm along load axis and extension axis respectively. If the value of M and l are 500 g and 2 cm respectively then percentage error of Y is :

Paramagnetic substances:
A. align themselves along the directions of external magnetic field.
B. attract strongly towards external magnetic field.
C. has susceptibility little more than zero.
D. move from a region of strong magnetic field to weak magnetic field.
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.sol: Paramagnets align weakly with the field (A) and have small positive susceptibility (C). They are attracted only weakly and move towards stronger fields, so B and D are wrong.

questions.q: A mixture of one mole of monoatomic gas and one mole of a diatomic gas (rigid) are kept at room temperature (27°C). The ratio of specific heat of gases at constant volume respectively is:
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{\frac32R}{\frac52R} = \dfrac35\).

questions.q: A LCR circuit is at resonance for a capacitor C, inductance L and resistance R. Now the value of resistance is halved keeping all other parameters same. The current amplitude at resonance will be now:
questions.sol: At resonance \(I_0 = \dfrac{V_0}{R}\): halving R doubles it.

questions.q: The diameter of a sphere is measured using a vernier caliper whose 9 divisions of main scale are equal to 10 divisions of vernier scale. The shortest division on the main scale is equal to 1 mm. The main scale reading is 2 cm and second division of vernier scale coincides with a division on main scale. If mass of the sphere is 8.635 g, the density of the sphere is:
Critical angle of incidence for a pair of optical media is 45°. The refractive indices of first and second media are in the ratio:

A proton and an electron are associated with same de-Broglie wavelength. The ratio of their kinetic energies is: (Assume h = \(6.63\times10^{-34}\) J s, \(m_e = 9.0\times10^{-31}\) kg and \(m_p\) = 1836 times \(m_e\))
questions.sol: Same \(\lambda\), same momentum; \(K = \dfrac{p^2}{2m}\): \(K_p : K_e = m_e : m_p = 1 : 1836\).

questions.q: Correct Bernoulli's equation is (symbols have their usual meaning) :
questions.sol: Per unit volume: \(P + \rho gh + \tfrac12\rho v^2\) = constant.

questions.q: Binding energy of a certain nucleus is \(18\times10^8\) J. How much is the difference between total mass of all the nucleons and nuclear mass of the given nucleus:
questions.sol: \(\Delta m = \dfrac{E}{c^2} = \dfrac{18\times10^8}{9\times10^{16}} = 2\times10^{-8}\) kg = 20 µg.

questions.q: In the given circuit, the terminal potential difference of the cell is :
questions.sol: \(4\,\|\,4 = 2\ \Omega\). \(I = \dfrac{3}{2 + 1} = 1\) A. Terminal voltage \(= 1\times2 = 2\) V.

questions.q: Two different adiabatic paths for the same gas intersect two isothermal curves as shown in P-V diagram. The relation between the ratio \(\frac{V_a}{V_d}\) and the ratio \(\frac{V_b}{V_c}\) is:
questions.sol: On adiabats \(TV^{\gamma - 1}\) is constant: \(\dfrac{V_a}{V_d} = \left(\dfrac{T_2}{T_1}\right)^{1/(\gamma-1)} = \dfrac{V_b}{V_c}\).

questions.q: A closed and an open organ pipe have same lengths. If the ratio of frequencies of their seventh overtones is \(\left(\frac{a - 1}{a}\right)\) then the value of a is ____ .
questions.sol: Closed pipe 7th overtone = 15th harmonic: \(\dfrac{15v}{4L}\). Open pipe 7th overtone = 8th harmonic: \(\dfrac{16v}{4L}\). Ratio \(\dfrac{15}{16}\), so a = 16.

questions.q: An electric field, \(\vec E = \frac{2\hat i + 6\hat j + 8\hat k}{\sqrt6}\) passes through the surface of 4 m² area having unit vector \(\hat n = \left(\frac{2\hat i + \hat j + \hat k}{\sqrt6}\right)\). The electric flux for that surface is ____ V m.
questions.sol: \(\vec E\cdot\hat n = \dfrac{4 + 6 + 8}{6} = 3\). Flux \(= 3\times4 = 12\) V m.

questions.q: Three vectors \(\vec{OP}\), \(\vec{OQ}\) and \(\vec{OR}\) each of magnitude A are acting as shown in figure. The resultant of the three vectors is \(A\sqrt x\). The value of x is ____ .
questions.sol: \(\vec R = A\left(1 + \tfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\right)\hat i + A\left(1 - \tfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\right)\hat j\). \(|\vec R|^2 = A^2[(1.707)^2 + (0.293)^2] = 3A^2\).

questions.q: A square loop PQRS having 10 turns, area \(3.6\times10^{-3}\) m² and resistance 100 Ω is slowly and uniformly being pulled out of a uniform magnetic field of magnitude B = 0.5 T as shown. Work done in pulling the loop out of the field in 1.0 s is ____ \(\times10^{-6}\) J.
questions.sol: Side 6 cm, pulled out in 1 s: \(v = 0.06\) m/s. \(\varepsilon = NBlv = 10\times0.5\times0.06\times0.06 = 0.018\) V. \(W = \dfrac{\varepsilon^2}{R}t = 3.24\times10^{-6}\) J ≈ \(3\times10^{-6}\) J.

questions.q: A liquid column of height 0.04 cm balances excess pressure of a soap bubble of certain radius. If density of liquid is \(8\times10^3\) kg m\(^{-3}\) and surface tension of soap solution is 0.28 N m\(^{-1}\), then diameter of the soap bubble is ____ cm. (if g = 10 m s\(^{-2}\))
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{4T}{r} = \rho gh \Rightarrow r = \dfrac{4\times0.28}{8\times10^3\times10\times4\times10^{-4}} = 0.035\) m. Diameter 7 cm.

questions.q: A uniform thin metal plate of mass 10 kg with dimensions is shown. The ratio of x and y coordinates of center of mass of plate is \(\frac n9\). The value of n is ____ .
Resistance of a wire at 0°C, 100°C and t°C is found to be 10 Ω, 10.2 Ω and 10.95 Ω respectively. The temperature t in Kelvin scale is ____ .
questions.sol: \(\alpha = \dfrac{0.2}{10\times100} = 2\times10^{-4}\). \(10.95 = 10(1 + \alpha t) \Rightarrow t = 475^\circ\)C = 748 K.

questions.q: A parallel beam of monochromatic light of wavelength 600 nm passes through single slit of 0.4 mm width. Angular divergence corresponding to second order minima would be ____ \(\times10^{-3}\) rad.
questions.sol: Second minimum: \(\sin\theta = \dfrac{2\lambda}{a} = 3\times10^{-3}\). Angular divergence (both sides) \(= 2\theta = 6\times10^{-3}\) rad.

questions.q: An electron with kinetic energy 5 eV enters a region of uniform magnetic field of 3 µT perpendicular to its direction. An electric field E is applied perpendicular to the direction of velocity and magnetic field. The value of E, so that electron moves along the same path, is ____ N C\(^{-1}\). (Given, mass of electron = \(9\times10^{-31}\) kg, electric charge = \(1.6\times10^{-19}\) C)
questions.sol: \(v = \sqrt{\dfrac{2\times5\times1.6\times10^{-19}}{9\times10^{-31}}} = 1.33\times10^6\) m/s. \(E = vB = 1.33\times10^6\times3\times10^{-6} = 4\) N/C.

questions.q: In an alpha particle scattering experiment distance of closest approach for the \(\alpha\) particle is \(4.5\times10^{-14}\) m. If target nucleus has atomic number 80, then maximum velocity of \(\alpha\)-particle is ____ \(\times10^5\) m/s approximately. (\(\frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} = 9\times10^9\) SI unit, mass of \(\alpha\) particle = \(6.72\times10^{-27}\) kg)
questions.sol: \(\tfrac12mv^2 = \dfrac{k(2e)(80e)}{r} = \dfrac{9\times10^9\times160\times(1.6\times10^{-19})^2}{4.5\times10^{-14}} = 8.19\times10^{-13}\) J. \(v = \sqrt{\dfrac{2\times8.19\times10^{-13}}{6.72\times10^{-27}}} \approx 1.56\times10^7\) m/s.

questions.q: A car of 800 kg is taking turn on a banked road of radius 300 m and angle of banking 30°. If coefficient of static friction is 0.2 then the maximum speed with which car can negotiate the turn safely: (g = 10 m/s², \(\sqrt3\) = 1.73)
questions.sol: \(v^2 = rg\dfrac{\mu + \tan\theta}{1 - \mu\tan\theta} = 3000\times\dfrac{0.2 + 0.577}{1 - 0.115} \approx 2635\), \(v \approx 51.4\) m/s.

questions.q: A body projected vertically upwards with a certain speed from the top of a tower reaches the ground in \(t_1\). If it is projected vertically downwards from the same point with the same speed, it reaches the ground in \(t_2\). Time required to reach the ground, if it is dropped from the top of the tower, is :
questions.sol: With \(h = -ut_1 + \tfrac12gt_1^2 = ut_2 + \tfrac12gt_2^2\), eliminating u gives \(h = \tfrac12gt_1t_2\). Dropped: \(t = \sqrt{t_1t_2}\).

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement (I): Dimensions of specific heat is \([L^2T^{-2}K^{-1}]\).
Statement (II): Dimensions of gas constant is \([ML^2T^{-1}K^{-1}]\).
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
o: Statement (I) is incorrect but statement (II) is correct
Both statement (I) and statement (II) are incorrect
Both statement (I) and statement (II) are correct
Statement (I) is correct but statement (II) is incorrect

questions.q: A body of weight 200 N is suspended from a tree branch through a chain of mass 10 kg. The branch pulls the chain by a force equal to (if g = 10 m/s²) :
questions.sol: The branch holds the body and the chain: \(200 + 10\times10 = 300\) N.

questions.q: The number of electrons flowing per second in the filament of a 110 W bulb operating at 220 V is : (Given e = \(1.6\times10^{-19}\) C)
The acceptor level of a p-type semiconductor is 6 eV. The maximum wavelength of light which can create a hole would be : Given hc = 1242 eV nm.
questions.sol: \(\lambda_{max} = \dfrac{1242}{6} = 207\) nm.

questions.q: In a vernier calliper, when both jaws touch each other, zero of the vernier scale shifts towards left and its 4<sup>th</sup> division coincides exactly with a certain division on main scale. If 50 vernier scale divisions equal to 49 main scale divisions and zero error in the instrument is 0.04 mm then how many main scale divisions are there in 1 cm ?
questions.sol: Negative zero error of 4 divisions: \(4\times LC = 0.04\) mm, so LC = 0.01 mm \(= \dfrac{1}{50}\) MSD. 1 MSD = 0.5 mm: 20 divisions per cm.

questions.q: In a coil, the current changes from −2 A to +2 A in 0.2 s and induces an emf of 0.1 V. The self inductance of the coil is :
questions.sol: \(L = \dfrac{\varepsilon\,\Delta t}{\Delta I} = \dfrac{0.1\times0.2}{4} = 5\) mH.

questions.q: Energy of 10 non rigid diatomic molecules at temperature T is :
questions.sol: Non-rigid diatomic: 7 degrees of freedom, \(\tfrac72k_BT\) each molecule. Ten molecules: \(35k_BT\).

questions.q: When UV light of wavelength 300 nm is incident on the metal surface having work function 2.13 eV, electron emission takes place. The stopping potential is : (Given hc = 1240 eV nm)

Match List I with List II (the graphs of List II are shown in the figure):
A. Y = magnetic susceptibility, X = magnetising field
B. Y = magnetic field, X = distance from centre of a current carrying wire for x < a (where a = radius of wire)
C. Y = magnetic field, X = distance from centre of a current carrying wire for x > a (where a = radius of wire)
D. Y = magnetic field inside solenoid, X = distance from centre
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: Susceptibility is constant (III). Inside a wire \(B \propto x\) (I); outside \(B \propto \dfrac1x\) (IV). Inside a solenoid B is uniform, falling near the ends (II).

questions.q: For the thin convex lens, the radii of curvature are at 15 cm and 30 cm respectively. The focal length of the lens is 20 cm. The refractive index of the material is :
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{1}{20} = (\mu - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{15} + \dfrac{1}{30}\right) = \dfrac{\mu - 1}{10} \Rightarrow \mu = 1.5\).

questions.q: Two identical conducting spheres P and S with charge Q on each, repel each other with a force 16 N. A third identical uncharged conducting sphere R is successively brought in contact with the two spheres. The new force of repulsion between P and S is :
questions.sol: After R touches P: P has \(\dfrac Q2\). Then R \(\left(\dfrac Q2\right)\) touches S: S has \(\dfrac{3Q}{4}\). \(F' = 16\times\dfrac12\times\dfrac34 = 6\) N.

questions.q: The longest wavelength associated with Paschen series is : (Given \(R_H = 1.097\times10^7\) SI unit)
questions.sol: 4 → 3: \(\dfrac1\lambda = R\left(\dfrac19 - \dfrac{1}{16}\right) = \dfrac{7R}{144}\), \(\lambda = \dfrac{144}{7\times1.097\times10^7} = 1.876\times10^{-6}\) m.

questions.q: A total of 48 J heat is given to one mole of helium kept in a cylinder. The temperature of helium increases by 2°C. The work done by the gas is: Given, R = 8.3 J K\(^{-1}\) mol\(^{-1}\).
questions.sol: \(\Delta U = \tfrac32R\Delta T = 1.5\times8.3\times2 = 24.9\) J. \(W = 48 - 24.9 = 23.1\) J.

questions.q: When kinetic energy of a body becomes 36 times of its original value, the percentage increase in the momentum of the body will be :
questions.sol: \(p \propto \sqrt K\): ×6, a 500% increase.

questions.q: Pressure inside a soap bubble is greater than the pressure outside by an amount : (given : R = Radius of bubble, S = Surface tension of bubble)
questions.sol: Two surfaces: \(\Delta P = \dfrac{4S}{R}\).

questions.q: Assuming the earth to be a sphere of uniform mass density, a body weighed 300 N on the surface of earth. How much it would weigh at R/4 depth under surface of earth ?
questions.sol: \(g_d = g\left(1 - \dfrac dR\right) = \dfrac34g\): \(\dfrac34\times300 = 225\) N.

questions.q:
In finding out refractive index of glass slab the following observations were made through travelling microscope: 50 vernier scale division = 49 MSD; 20 divisions on main scale in each cm.
For mark on paper: MSR = 8.45 cm, VC = 26
For mark on paper seen through slab: MSR = 7.12 cm, VC = 41
For powder particle on the top surface of the glass slab: MSR = 4.05 cm, VC = 1
(MSR = Main Scale Reading, VC = Vernier Coincidence)
Refractive index of the glass slab is :

In the given electromagnetic wave \(E_y = 600\sin(\omega t - kx)\) V m\(^{-1}\), intensity of the associated light beam is (in W/m²) : (Given \(\epsilon_0 = 9\times10^{-12}\) C² N\(^{-1}\) m\(^{-2}\))
questions.sol: \(I = \tfrac12c\epsilon_0E_0^2 = 0.5\times3\times10^8\times9\times10^{-12}\times600^2 = 486\) W/m².

questions.q: For a given series LCR circuit it is found that maximum current is drawn when value of variable capacitance is 2.5 nF. If resistance of 200 Ω and 100 mH inductor is being used in the given circuit. The frequency of ac source is ____ \(\times10^3\) Hz (given \(\pi^2\) = 10)
questions.sol: Resonance: \(f = \dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}} = \dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{0.1\times2.5\times10^{-9}}} = \dfrac{1}{2\pi\times5\times10^{-6}\sqrt{10}} \approx 10\times10^3\) Hz.

questions.q: Three balls of masses 2 kg, 4 kg and 6 kg respectively are arranged at centre of the edges of an equilateral triangle of side 2 m. The moment of inertia of the system about an axis through the centroid and perpendicular to the plane of triangle, will be ____ kg m².
questions.sol: Mid-points of the sides are at the inradius \(\dfrac{a}{2\sqrt3} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}\) m from the centroid. \(I = (2 + 4 + 6)\times\dfrac13 = 4\) kg m².

questions.q: In the given figure an ammeter A consists of a 240 Ω coil connected in parallel to a 10 Ω shunt. The reading of the ammeter is ____ mA. (The 140.4 Ω resistor in the figure is external to the ammeter; the 240 Ω coil and its 10 Ω shunt are both inside A.)
questions.sol: Ammeter resistance \(= \dfrac{240\times10}{250} = 9.6\ \Omega\). \(I = \dfrac{24}{140.4 + 9.6} = 0.16\) A = 160 mA.

questions.q: A coil having 100 turns, area of \(5\times10^{-3}\) m², carrying current of 1 mA is placed in uniform magnetic field of 0.20 T such a way that plane of coil is perpendicular to the magnetic field. The work done in turning the coil through 90° is ____ µJ.
questions.sol: Plane ⟂ B means \(\vec m \parallel \vec B\). \(W = mB(1 - \cos90^\circ) = 100\times10^{-3}\times5\times10^{-3}\times0.2 = 10^{-4}\) J = 100 µJ.

questions.q: A capacitor of 10 µF capacitance whose plates are separated by 10 mm through air and each plate has area 4 cm² is now filled equally with two dielectric media of \(K_1\) = 2, \(K_2\) = 3 respectively as shown in figure. If new force between the plates is 8 N. The supply voltage is ____ V.
questions.sol: Side by side: \(C' = C\dfrac{K_1 + K_2}{2} = 25\ \mu\)F. Force between plates \(= \dfrac{C'V^2}{2d} = \dfrac{25\times10^{-6}V^2}{0.02} = 8 \Rightarrow V = 80\) V.

questions.q: A particle moves in a straight line so that its displacement x at any time t is given by \(x^2 = 1 + t^2\). Its acceleration at any time t is \(x^{-n}\) where n = ____ .
questions.sol: \(xv = t\), so \(v = \dfrac tx\). \(a = \dfrac{x - tv}{x^2} = \dfrac{x^2 - t^2}{x^3} = \dfrac{1}{x^3}\): n = 3.

questions.q: Two coherent monochromatic light beams of intensities I and 4I are superimposed. The difference between maximum and minimum possible intensities in the resulting beam is x I. The value of x is ____ .

Two open organ pipes of lengths 60 cm and 90 cm resonate at 6<sup>th</sup> and 5<sup>th</sup> harmonics respectively. The difference of frequencies for the given modes is ____ Hz. (Velocity of sound in air = 333 m/s)
questions.sol: \(f_1 = \dfrac{6\times333}{2\times0.6} = 1665\) Hz, \(f_2 = \dfrac{5\times333}{2\times0.9} = 925\) Hz. Difference 740 Hz.

questions.q: In Franck-Hertz experiment, the first dip in the current-voltage graph for hydrogen is observed at 10.2 V. The wavelength of light emitted by hydrogen atom when excited to the first excitation level is ____ nm. (Given hc = 1245 eV nm, e = \(1.6\times10^{-19}\) C).
questions.sol: \(\lambda = \dfrac{1245}{10.2} \approx 122\) nm.

questions.q: A wire of cross sectional area A, modulus of elasticity \(2\times10^{11}\) N m\(^{-2}\) and length 2 m is stretched between two vertical rigid supports. When a mass of 2 kg is suspended at the middle it sags lower from its original position making angle \(\theta = \frac{1}{100}\) radian on the points of support. The value of A is ____ \(\times10^{-4}\) m² (consider x << L). (given : g = 10 m/s²)
questions.sol: \(2T\sin\theta = mg \Rightarrow T = \dfrac{20}{0.02} = 1000\) N. Strain \(= \dfrac{1}{\cos\theta} - 1 \approx \dfrac{\theta^2}{2} = 5\times10^{-5}\). \(A = \dfrac{T}{Y\times\text{strain}} = \dfrac{1000}{2\times10^{11}\times5\times10^{-5}} = 10^{-4}\) m².

questions.q: A bullet of mass 50 g is fired with a speed 100 m/s on a plywood and emerges with 40 m/s. The percentage loss of kinetic energy is :
questions.sol: Remaining KE fraction \(= \left(\dfrac{40}{100}\right)^2 = 0.16\): 84% lost.

questions.q: The specific heat at constant pressure of a real gas obeying \(PV^2 = RT\) equation is:
questions.sol: At constant P: \(2PV\,dV = R\,dT \Rightarrow P\,dV = \dfrac{R}{2V}dT\). \(C_P = C_V + \dfrac{R}{2V}\).

questions.q: The correct truth table for the following logic circuit is :
questions.sol: \(Y = \bar A + AB = \bar A + B\): outputs 1, 1, 0, 1 for AB = 00, 01, 10, 11.

questions.q: Electromagnetic waves travel in a medium with speed of \(1.5\times10^8\) m s\(^{-1}\). The relative permeability of the medium is 2.0. The relative permittivity will be:
questions.sol: \(n = \dfrac{c}{v} = 2 = \sqrt{\mu_r\epsilon_r} \Rightarrow \epsilon_r = \dfrac42 = 2\).

questions.q: To find the spring constant (k) of a spring experimentally, a student commits 2% positive error in the measurement of time and 1% negative error in measurement of mass. The percentage error in determining value of k is :
questions.sol: \(k = \dfrac{4\pi^2m}{T^2}\): \(\dfrac{\Delta k}{k} = \dfrac{\Delta m}{m} - 2\dfrac{\Delta T}{T} = -1\% - 4\% = -5\%\). Magnitude 5%.

questions.q: The value of unknown resistance (x) for which the potential difference between B and D will be zero in the arrangement shown, is :

A light string passing over a smooth light pulley connects two blocks of masses \(m_1\) and \(m_2\) (where \(m_2 > m_1\)). If the acceleration of the system is \(\frac{g}{\sqrt2}\), then the ratio of the masses \(\frac{m_1}{m_2}\) is:
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{m_2 - m_1}{m_2 + m_1} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt2} \Rightarrow \dfrac{m_1}{m_2} = \dfrac{\sqrt2 - 1}{\sqrt2 + 1}\).

questions.q: To project a body of mass m from earth's surface to infinity, the required kinetic energy is (assume, the radius of earth is \(R_E\), g = acceleration due to gravity on the surface of earth):
questions.sol: \(K = \dfrac{GMm}{R_E} = mgR_E\).

List IList II

B. Magnetic fieldII. \([L^2A^1]\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Which of the following phenomena is not explained by wave nature of light?
A. reflection
B. diffraction
C. photoelectric effect
D. interference
E. polarization
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.sol: Only the photoelectric effect needs photons.

questions.q: Four particles A, B, C, D of mass \(\frac m2\), m, 2m, 4m, have same momentum, respectively. The particle with maximum kinetic energy is :
questions.sol: \(K = \dfrac{p^2}{2m}\): same p, so the lightest (A, mass \(\frac m2\)) has the most KE.

questions.q: In photoelectric experiment energy of 2.48 eV irradiates a photo sensitive material. The stopping potential was measured to be 0.5 V. Work function of the photo sensitive material is :

While measuring diameter of wire using screw gauge the following readings were noted. Main scale reading is 1 mm and circular scale reading is equal to 42 divisions. Pitch of screw gauge is 1 mm and it has 100 divisions on circular scale. The diameter of the wire is \(\frac{x}{50}\) mm. The value of x is :

Given below are two statements :
Statement I: In an LCR series circuit, current is maximum at resonance.
Statement II: Current in a purely resistive circuit can never be less than that in a series LCR circuit when connected to same voltage source.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
o: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.sol: At resonance \(Z = R\) (minimum), so current is maximum (I true). \(Z \ge R\) always, so the pure-R current is never less (II true).

questions.q: \(\sigma\) is the uniform surface charge density of a thin spherical shell of radius R. The electric field at any point on the surface of the spherical shell is :
questions.sol: Just outside the shell \(E = \dfrac{Q}{4\pi\epsilon_0R^2} = \dfrac{\sigma}{\epsilon_0}\) (the key's answer).
questions.note: The official key gives (B), the field just outside the shell. Exactly on the surface itself the field is the average of inside (0) and outside, \(\sigma/2\epsilon_0\).

questions.q: An element \(\Delta\vec l = \Delta x\hat i\) is placed at the origin and carries a large current I = 10 A. The magnetic field on the y-axis at a distance of 0.5 m from the element \(\Delta x\) of 1 cm length is:
questions.sol: Biot–Savart, \(\theta = 90^\circ\): \(B = \dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\dfrac{I\Delta x}{r^2} = 10^{-7}\times\dfrac{10\times0.01}{0.25} = 4\times10^{-8}\) T.

questions.q: A small ball of mass m and density \(\rho\) is dropped in a viscous liquid of density \(\rho_0\). After sometime, the ball falls with constant velocity. The viscous force on the ball is :
questions.sol: At terminal speed: \(F_v = mg - \text{buoyancy} = mg - \dfrac{m}{\rho}\rho_0g = mg\left(1 - \dfrac{\rho_0}{\rho}\right)\).

questions.q: A train starting from rest first accelerates uniformly up to a speed of 80 km/h for time t, then it moves with a constant speed for time 3t. The average speed of the train for this duration of journey will be (in km/h) :
questions.sol: Distance \(= \tfrac12(80)t + 80(3t) = 280t\) in time 4t: average 70 km/h.

questions.q: A sample contains mixture of helium and oxygen gas. The ratio of root mean square speed of helium and oxygen in the sample, is :
questions.sol: \(v_{rms} \propto \dfrac{1}{\sqrt M}\): \(\sqrt{\dfrac{32}{4}} = 2\sqrt2\).

questions.q: The ratio of the shortest wavelength of Balmer series to the shortest wavelength of Lyman series for hydrogen atom is :
questions.sol: Shortest Balmer \(= \dfrac{4}{R}\), shortest Lyman \(= \dfrac1R\): 4 : 1.

questions.q: A big drop is formed by coalescing 1000 small droplets of water. The ratio of surface energy of 1000 droplets to that of energy of big drop is \(\frac{10}{x}\). The value of x is ____ .
questions.sol: \(R = 10r\). Total area of droplets \(1000\times4\pi r^2\) vs \(4\pi(10r)^2 = 100\times4\pi r^2\): ratio \(10 = \dfrac{10}{1}\).

questions.q: If the radius of earth is reduced to three-fourth of its present value without change in its mass then value of duration of the day of earth will be ____ hours 30 minutes.
questions.sol: Angular momentum conserved: \(T \propto I \propto R^2\). \(24\times\dfrac{9}{16} = 13.5\) h = 13 h 30 min.

questions.q: A particle is doing simple harmonic motion of amplitude 0.06 m and time period 3.14 s. The maximum velocity of the particle is ____ cm/s.
questions.sol: \(\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{3.14} = 2\) rad/s. \(v_{max} = A\omega = 0.12\) m/s = 12 cm/s.

questions.q: Three infinitely long charged thin sheets are placed as shown in figure. The magnitude of electric field at the point P is \(\frac{x\sigma}{\epsilon_0}\). The value of x is ____ (all quantities are measured in SI units).
questions.sol: P lies between \(x = a\) and \(x = 3a\). Each sheet gives \(\dfrac{|\sigma'|}{2\epsilon_0}\): \(-\sigma\) (left, pulls left) \(\dfrac{\sigma}{2\epsilon_0}\); \(-2\sigma\) (left, pulls left) \(\dfrac{\sigma}{\epsilon_0}\); \(+\sigma\) (right, pushes left) \(\dfrac{\sigma}{2\epsilon_0}\). Total \(\dfrac{2\sigma}{\epsilon_0}\) along −x.

questions.q: Radius of a certain orbit of hydrogen atom is 8.48 Å. If energy of electron in this orbit is E/x, then x = ____ . (Given \(a_0\) = 0.529 Å, E = energy of electron in ground state).
questions.sol: \(n^2 = \dfrac{8.48}{0.529} = 16\), so \(n = 4\) and the energy is \(\dfrac{E}{16}\).

questions.q: For three vectors \(\vec A = (-x\hat i - 6\hat j - 2\hat k)\), \(\vec B = (-\hat i + 4\hat j + 3\hat k)\) and \(\vec C = (-8\hat i - \hat j + 3\hat k)\), if \(\vec A\cdot(\vec B\times\vec C) = 0\), then value of x is ____ .
questions.sol: \(\begin{vmatrix}-x & -6 & -2\\ -1 & 4 & 3\\ -8 & -1 & 3\end{vmatrix} = -15x + 126 - 66 = 0 \Rightarrow x = 4\).

questions.q: The refractive index of prism is \(\mu = \sqrt3\) and the ratio of the angle of minimum deviation to the angle of prism is one. The value of angle of prism is ____ °.
questions.sol: \(\delta_m = A\): \(\mu = \dfrac{\sin A}{\sin(A/2)} = 2\cos\dfrac A2 = \sqrt3 \Rightarrow A = 60^\circ\).

questions.q: A wire of resistance R and radius r is stretched till its radius became r/2. If new resistance of the stretched wire is x R, then value of x is ____ .
questions.sol: Radius halves: area \(\dfrac14\), length ×4 (same volume). \(R' = 16R\).

questions.q: When a dc voltage of 100 V is applied to an inductor, a dc current of 5 A flows through it. When an ac voltage of 200 V peak value is connected to inductor, its inductive reactance is found to be \(20\sqrt3\) Ω. The power dissipated in the circuit is ____ W.

A circular coil having 200 turns, \(2.5\times10^{-4}\) m² area and carrying 100 µA current is placed in a uniform magnetic field of 1 T. Initially the magnetic dipole moment (\(\vec M\)) was directed along \(\vec B\). Amount of work, required to rotate the coil through 90° from its initial orientation such that \(\vec M\) becomes perpendicular to \(\vec B\), is ____ µJ.
questions.sol: \(W = MB(1 - \cos90^\circ) = NIAB = 200\times10^{-4}\times2.5\times10^{-4}\times1 = 5\times10^{-6}\) J = 5 µJ.

questions.q: A body is moving unidirectionally under the influence of a constant power source. Its displacement in time t is proportional to :
questions.sol: \(\tfrac12mv^2 = Pt \Rightarrow v \propto t^{1/2} \Rightarrow x \propto t^{3/2}\).

questions.q: What is the dimensional formula of \(ab^{-1}\) in the equation \(\left(P + \frac{a}{V^2}\right)(V - b) = RT\), where letters have their usual meaning.
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{a}{V^2}\) is a pressure, so \(a = PV^2\); \(b\) is a volume. \(\dfrac ab = PV\): energy, \([ML^2T^{-2}]\).

questions.q: A particle moves in x-y plane under the influence of a force \(\vec F\) such that its linear momentum is \(\vec p(t) = \hat i\cos(kt) - \hat j\sin(kt)\). If k is constant, the angle between \(\vec F\) and \(\vec p\) will be :
questions.sol: \(\vec F = \dfrac{d\vec p}{dt} = -k(\hat i\sin kt + \hat j\cos kt)\). \(\vec F\cdot\vec p = -k(\sin kt\cos kt - \cos kt\sin kt) = 0\): 90°.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II :
List I (EM-Wave)List II (Wavelength Range)
A. Infra-redI. < \(10^{-3}\) nm
B. UltravioletII. 400 nm to 1 nm
C. X-raysIII. 1 mm to 700 nm
D. Gamma raysIV. 1 nm to \(10^{-3}\) nm
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: IR: 1 mm–700 nm; UV: 400 nm–1 nm; X-rays: 1 nm–\(10^{-3}\) nm; gamma: below \(10^{-3}\) nm.

questions.q: During an adiabatic process, if the pressure of a gas is found to be proportional to the cube of its absolute temperature, then the ratio of \(\frac{C_P}{C_V}\) for the gas is :
questions.sol: Adiabatic: \(P \propto T^{\gamma/(\gamma - 1)}\). \(\dfrac{\gamma}{\gamma - 1} = 3 \Rightarrow \gamma = \dfrac32\).

questions.q: A heavy box of mass 50 kg is moving on a horizontal surface. If co-efficient of kinetic friction between the box and horizontal surface is 0.3 then force of kinetic friction is :
questions.sol: \(f = \mu mg = 0.3\times50\times9.8 = 147\) N.

questions.q: A man carrying a monkey on his shoulder does cycling smoothly on a circular track of radius 9 m and completes 120 revolutions in 3 minutes. The magnitude of centripetal acceleration of monkey is (in m/s²) :
questions.sol: \(\omega = 2\pi\times\dfrac{120}{180} = \dfrac{4\pi}{3}\) rad/s. \(a = \omega^2r = \dfrac{16\pi^2}{9}\times9 = 16\pi^2\) m/s².

questions.q: A series LCR circuit is subjected to an ac signal of 200 V, 50 Hz. If the voltage across the inductor (L = 10 mH) is 31.4 V, then the current in this circuit is ____ .
Which of the following statement is not true about stopping potential (\(V_0\)) ?
o: It depends upon frequency of the incident light.
It is 1/e times the maximum kinetic energy of electrons emitted.
It increases with increase in intensity of the incident light.
It depends on the nature of emitter material.
questions.sol: Stopping potential depends on frequency and the material, not on intensity.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I: When the white light passed through a prism, the red light bends lesser than yellow and violet.
Statement II: The refractive indices are different for different wavelengths in dispersive medium.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.sol: Refractive index depends on wavelength; red has the smallest index and bends least. Both true.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II :
List IList II
A. A force that restores an elastic body of unit area to its original stateI. Bulk modulus
B. Two equal and opposite forces parallel to opposite facesII. Young's modulus
C. Forces perpendicular everywhere to the surface per unit area same everywhereIII. Stress
D. Two equal and opposite forces perpendicular to opposite facesIV. Shear modulus
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: Restoring force per unit area is stress (III); tangential forces → shear modulus (IV); uniform normal pressure → bulk modulus (I); normal forces on opposite faces → Young's modulus (II).

questions.q: A satellite revolving around a planet in stationary orbit has time period 6 hours. The mass of planet is one-fourth the mass of earth. The radius of orbit of the satellite is : (Given: Radius of geo-stationary orbit for earth is \(4.2\times10^4\) km)
questions.sol: \(r^3 \propto MT^2\): \(r = 4.2\times10^4\times\left(\dfrac14\times\dfrac{1}{16}\right)^{1/3} = \dfrac{4.2\times10^4}{4} = 1.05\times10^4\) km.

questions.q: A vernier callipers has 20 divisions on the vernier scale, which coincides with 19<sup>th</sup> division on the main scale. The least count of the instrument is 0.1 mm. One main scale division is equal to ____ mm.
questions.sol: \(LC = 1\text{ MSD} - 1\text{ VSD} = \dfrac{1}{20}\) MSD \(= 0.1\) mm, so 1 MSD = 2 mm.

questions.q: The ratio of heat dissipated per second through the resistance 5 Ω and 10 Ω in the circuit given below is:
questions.sol: Same voltage across the parallel pair: \(P \propto \dfrac1R\), so \(5\ \Omega : 10\ \Omega = 2 : 1\).

questions.q: The output (Y) of logic circuit given below is 0 only when :
questions.sol: \(Y = (A + B) + B\cdot1 = A + B\), which is 0 only for A = B = 0.

questions.q: The angular momentum of an electron in a hydrogen atom is proportional to : (Where r is the radius of orbit of electron)
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{mv^2}{r} = \dfrac{ke^2}{r^2} \Rightarrow v \propto \dfrac{1}{\sqrt r}\). \(L = mvr \propto \sqrt r\).

questions.q: The vehicles carrying inflammable fluids usually have metallic chains touching the ground:
o: To protect tyres from catching dirt from ground
To conduct excess charge due to air friction to ground and prevent sparking
questions.sol: The chain earths the static charge built up by friction with air, so no spark can ignite the fuel.

questions.q: A galvanometer of resistance 100 Ω when connected in series with 400 Ω measures a voltage of upto 10 V. The value of resistance required to convert the galvanometer into ammeter to read upto 10 A is \(x\times10^{-2}\) Ω. The value of x is :
questions.sol: \(I_g = \dfrac{10}{500} = 0.02\) A. \(S = \dfrac{I_gG}{I - I_g} = \dfrac{0.02\times100}{9.98} \approx 0.2\ \Omega = 20\times10^{-2}\ \Omega\).

questions.q: The electrostatic force (\(\vec F_1\)) and magnetic force (\(\vec F_2\)) acting on a charge q moving with velocity v can be written :
o: \(\vec F_1 = q\vec B\), \(\vec F_2 = q(\vec B\times\vec v)\)
\(\vec F_1 = q\vec V\cdot\vec E\), \(\vec F_2 = q(\vec B\cdot\vec V)\)
\(\vec F_1 = q\vec E\), \(\vec F_2 = q(\vec V\times\vec B)\)
\(\vec F_1 = q\vec E\), \(\vec F_2 = q(\vec B\times\vec V)\)
questions.sol: \(\vec F_1 = q\vec E\), \(\vec F_2 = q\vec v\times\vec B\).

questions.q: If n is the number density and d is the diameter of the molecule, then the average distance covered by a molecule between two successive collisions (i.e. mean free path) is represented by :
questions.sol: \(\lambda = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt2n\pi d^2}\).

questions.q: The electric field at point P due to an electric dipole is E. The electric field at point R on equatorial line will be \(\frac Ex\). The value of x :
questions.sol: P is on the axis at distance r: \(E = \dfrac{2kp}{r^3}\). R is on the equatorial line at 2r: \(\dfrac{kp}{(2r)^3} = \dfrac{kp}{8r^3} = \dfrac{E}{16}\).

questions.q: A sonometer wire of resonating length 90 cm has a fundamental frequency of 400 Hz when kept under some tension. The resonating length of the wire with fundamental frequency of 600 Hz under same tension ____ cm.
questions.sol: \(f \propto \dfrac1L\): \(L = 90\times\dfrac{400}{600} = 60\) cm.

questions.q: In a single slit experiment, a parallel beam of green light of wavelength 550 nm passes through a slit of width 0.20 mm. The transmitted light is collected on a screen 100 cm away. The distance of first order minima from the central maximum will be \(x\times10^{-5}\) m. The value of x is :
questions.sol: \(y = \dfrac{\lambda D}{a} = \dfrac{550\times10^{-9}\times1}{2\times10^{-4}} = 275\times10^{-5}\) m.

questions.q: A hollow sphere is rolling on a plane surface about its axis of symmetry. The ratio of rotational kinetic energy to its total kinetic energy is \(\frac x5\). The value of x is ____ .
questions.sol: Hollow sphere: \(K_{rot} = \tfrac12\cdot\tfrac23mv^2 = \tfrac13mv^2\); total \(= \tfrac56mv^2\). Ratio \(= \dfrac25\).

questions.q: A wire of resistance 20 Ω is divided into 10 equal parts, resulting pairs. A combination of two parts are connected in parallel and so on. Now resulting pairs of parallel combination are connected in series. The equivalent resistance of final combination is ____ Ω.
questions.sol: Each part 2 Ω; each pair in parallel is 1 Ω; five pairs in series: 5 Ω.

questions.q: The maximum height reached by a projectile is 64 m. If the initial velocity is halved, the new maximum height of the projectile is ____ m.
The shortest wavelength of the spectral lines in the Lyman series of hydrogen spectrum is 915 Å. The longest wavelength of spectral lines in the Balmer series will be ____ Å.
questions.sol: Lyman limit: \(\dfrac{1}{915} = R\). Balmer longest (3 → 2): \(\dfrac1\lambda = R\cdot\dfrac{5}{36}\), \(\lambda = \dfrac{36\times915}{5} = 6588\) Å.

questions.q: The current in an inductor is given by I = (3t + 8) where t is in second. The magnitude of induced emf produced in the inductor is 12 mV. The self-inductance of the inductor ____ mH.
questions.sol: \(\varepsilon = L\dfrac{dI}{dt} = 3L = 12\) mV, so \(L = 4\) mH.

questions.q: A hydraulic press containing water has two arms with diameters as mentioned in the figure. A force of 10 N is applied on the surface of water in the thinner arm. The force required to be applied on the surface of water in the thicker arm to maintain equilibrium of water is ____ N.
questions.sol: Pascal: \(\dfrac{F_1}{A_1} = \dfrac{F_2}{A_2}\). \(F = 10\times\left(\dfrac{14}{1.4}\right)^2 = 1000\) N.

questions.q: A solenoid of length 0.5 m has a radius of 1 cm and is made up of 'm' number of turns. It carries a current of 5 A. If the magnitude of the magnetic field inside the solenoid is \(6.28\times10^{-3}\) T then the value of m is ____ .
questions.sol: \(B = \dfrac{\mu_0mI}{L} \Rightarrow m = \dfrac{6.28\times10^{-3}\times0.5}{4\pi\times10^{-7}\times5} = 500\).

questions.q: A body of mass 50 kg is lifted to a height of 20 m from the ground in the two different ways as shown in the figures. The ratio of work done against the gravity in both the respective cases, will be :
questions.sol: Work against gravity is \(mgh\) either way, whatever the path: 1 : 1.

questions.q: If G be the gravitational constant and u be the energy density then which of the following quantity have the dimensions as that of the \(\sqrt{uG}\) :
An alternating voltage of amplitude 40 V and frequency 4 kHz is applied directly across the capacitor of 12 µF. The maximum displacement current between the plates of the capacitor is nearly :
questions.sol: \(I_0 = V_0\omega C = 40\times2\pi\times4000\times12\times10^{-6} \approx 12\) A.

questions.q: Ratio of radius of gyration of a hollow sphere to that of a solid cylinder of equal mass, for moment of Inertia about their diameter axis AB as shown in figure is \(\sqrt{8/x}\). The value of x is :
questions.sol: Hollow sphere: \(k_1^2 = \dfrac23R^2\). Solid cylinder (radius R, length 4R) about a diameter of its end face: \(k_2^2 = \dfrac{R^2}{4} + \dfrac{(4R)^2}{3} = \dfrac{67}{12}R^2\). \(\dfrac{k_1}{k_2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{8}{67}}\).

questions.q: In hydrogen like system the ratio of coulombian force and gravitational force between an electron and a proton is in the order of :
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{F_e}{F_g} = \dfrac{ke^2}{Gm_em_p} = \dfrac{9\times10^9\times(1.6\times10^{-19})^2}{6.67\times10^{-11}\times9.1\times10^{-31}\times1.67\times10^{-27}} \approx 2\times10^{39}\).

questions.q: A simple pendulum doing small oscillations at a place R height above earth surface has time period of \(T_1\) = 4 s. \(T_2\) would be its time period if it is brought to a point which is at a height 2R from earth surface. Choose the correct relation [R = radius of earth] :
questions.sol: \(T \propto \dfrac{1}{\sqrt g} \propto (R + h)\): \(\dfrac{T_1}{T_2} = \dfrac{2R}{3R}\), so \(3T_1 = 2T_2\).

questions.q:
Match List I with List II :
List IList II
A. Kinetic energy of planetI. \(-GMm/a\)
B. Gravitation Potential energy of sun-planet systemII. \(GMm/2a\)
C. Total mechanical energy of planetIII. \(\frac{Gm}{r}\)
D. Escape energy at the surface of planet for unit mass objectIV. \(-GMm/2a\)
(Where a = radius of planet orbit, r = radius of planet, M = mass of Sun, m = mass of planet)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: KE \(= \dfrac{GMm}{2a}\) (II); PE \(= -\dfrac{GMm}{a}\) (I); total \(= -\dfrac{GMm}{2a}\) (IV); escape energy per unit mass \(= \dfrac{Gm}{r}\) (III).

questions.q: The heat absorbed by a system in going through the given cyclic process is :
questions.sol: Heat in a cycle = work = enclosed area, a circle of diameter 280 units: \(\pi(140)^2 \approx 61600\) kPa·cc \(= 61600\times10^{-3}\) J \(= 61.6\) J.

questions.q: In the given figure \(R_1\) = 10 Ω, \(R_2\) = 8 Ω, \(R_3\) = 4 Ω and \(R_4\) = 8 Ω. Battery is ideal with emf 12 V. Equivalent resistance of the circuit and current supplied by battery are respectively :
questions.sol: \(R_2\), \(R_4\) and \(R_3\) all join the same two nodes: \(8\,\|\,8\,\|\,4 = 2\ \Omega\). Total \(10 + 2 = 12\ \Omega\), \(I = 1\) A.

questions.q: Two conducting circular loops A and B are placed in the same plane with their centres coinciding as shown in figure. The mutual inductance between them is:
questions.sol: Current \(I\) in B gives \(\dfrac{\mu_0I}{2b}\) at the centre, nearly uniform over the small loop A: \(\phi = \dfrac{\mu_0I}{2b}\pi a^2\), so \(M = \dfrac{\mu_0\pi a^2}{2b}\).

questions.q: If the collision frequency of hydrogen molecules in a closed chamber at 27°C is Z, then the collision frequency of the same system at 127°C is :
questions.sol: Collision frequency \(\propto v_{rms} \propto \sqrt T\): \(Z\sqrt{\dfrac{400}{300}} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt3}Z\).

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I: Figure shows the variation of stopping potential with frequency (\(\nu\)) for the two photosensitive materials \(M_1\) and \(M_2\). The slope gives value of \(\frac he\), where h is Planck's constant, e is the charge of electron.
Statement II: \(M_2\) will emit photoelectrons of greater kinetic energy for the incident radiation having same frequency.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
o: Statement I is correct and Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.sol: \(eV_0 = h\nu - \phi\): slope \(\dfrac he\) (I correct). \(M_2\) has the larger threshold, so at the same frequency its electrons have less KE (II wrong).

questions.q: Following gates section is connected in a complete suitable circuit. For which of the following combination, bulb will glow (ON) :
questions.sol: The A gate gives \(\bar A\) and the B, C gate gives BC; the final NOR outputs 1 only when \(\bar A = 0\) and \(BC = 0\), i.e. A = 1 with B, C not both 1. Of the options only (B) does this, so only then does current flow through R and the bulb.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I: When a capillary tube is dipped into a liquid, the liquid neither rises nor falls in the capillary. The contact angle may be 0°.
Statement II: The contact angle between a solid and a liquid is a property of the material of the solid and liquid as well.
In the light of the above statement, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
o: Statement I is true and Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.sol: No rise or fall means a contact angle of 90°, not 0° (I false). Contact angle depends on both materials (II true).

questions.q: Light emerges out of a convex lens when a source of light is kept at its focus. The shape of wavefront of the light is :
questions.sol: A point source at the focus gives a parallel beam: plane wavefronts.

questions.q: An electron rotates in a circle around a nucleus having positive charge Ze. Correct relation between total energy (E) of electron to its potential energy (U) is :
questions.sol: \(E = -K = \dfrac U2\), so \(2E = U\).

questions.q: Time periods of oscillation of the same simple pendulum measured using four different measuring clocks were recorded as 4.62 s, 4.632 s, 4.6 s and 4.64 s. The arithmetic mean of these readings in correct significant figure is :
questions.sol: Mean \(= \dfrac{18.492}{4} = 4.623\) s, but 4.6 s has only one decimal place, so the mean is quoted as 4.6 s.

questions.q: The angle between vector \(\vec Q\) and the resultant of \((2\vec Q + 2\vec P)\) and \((2\vec Q - 2\vec P)\) is :
questions.sol: Resultant \(= 4\vec Q\), parallel to \(\vec Q\): 0°.

questions.q: In a co-axial straight cable, the central conductor and the outer conductor carry equal currents in opposite directions. The magnetic field is zero :
questions.sol: Outside the cable the enclosed current is zero, so B = 0 there.

questions.q: A wooden block of mass 5 kg rests on a soft horizontal floor. When an iron cylinder of mass 25 kg is placed on the top of the block, the floor yields and the block and the cylinder together go down with an acceleration of 0.1 m s\(^{-2}\). The action force of the system on the floor is equal to :

The electric field between the two parallel plates of a capacitor of 1.5 µF capacitance drops to one third of its initial value in 6.6 µs when the plates are connected by a thin wire. The resistance of this wire is ____ Ω. (Given, \(\log_e3\) = 1.1)
questions.sol: \(E \propto q = q_0e^{-t/RC}\): \(t = RC\ln3 \Rightarrow R = \dfrac{6.6\times10^{-6}}{1.5\times10^{-6}\times1.1} = 4\ \Omega\).

questions.q: If three helium nuclei combine to form a carbon nucleus then the energy released in this reaction is ____ \(\times10^{-2}\) MeV. (Given 1 u = 931 MeV/c², atomic mass of helium = 4.002603 u)

Three blocks \(M_1, M_2, M_3\) having masses 4 kg, 6 kg and 10 kg respectively are hanging from a smooth pulley using rope 1, 2 and 3 as shown in figure. The tension in the rope 1, \(T_1\) when they are moving upward with acceleration of 2 m s\(^{-2}\) is ____ N (if g = 10 m/s²).
questions.sol: Rope 1 carries all three blocks: \(T_1 = 20(10 + 2) = 240\) N.

questions.q: Three capacitors of capacitances 25 µF, 30 µF and 45 µF are connected in parallel to a supply of 100 V. Energy stored in the above combination is E. When these capacitors are connected in series to the same supply, the stored energy is \(\frac9xE\). The value of x is ____ .
questions.sol: Parallel: 100 µF. Series: \(\dfrac1C = \dfrac1{25} + \dfrac1{30} + \dfrac1{45} = \dfrac{86}{900}\). Energy ratio at the same voltage \(= \dfrac{900/86}{100} = \dfrac{9}{86}\).

questions.q: In the experiment to determine the galvanometer resistance by half-deflection method, the plot of 1/\(\theta\) vs the resistance (R) of the resistance box is shown in the figure. The figure of merit of the galvanometer is ____ \(\times10^{-1}\) A/division. [The source has emf 2 V]
questions.sol: \(k\theta = \dfrac{E}{R + G} \Rightarrow \dfrac1\theta = \dfrac kE(R + G)\). Slope \(= \dfrac14 = \dfrac k2\), so \(k = 0.5 = 5\times10^{-1}\) A/div.

questions.q: The density and breaking stress of a wire are \(6\times10^4\) kg/m³ and \(1.2\times10^8\) N/m² respectively. The wire is suspended from a rigid support on a planet where acceleration due to gravity is \(\frac13\)<sup>rd</sup> of the value on the surface of earth. The maximum length of the wire without breaking is ____ m (take, g = 10 m/s²).
questions.sol: \(L = \dfrac{\sigma}{\rho g'} = \dfrac{1.2\times10^8}{6\times10^4\times10/3} = 600\) m.

questions.q: An ac source is connected in given series LCR circuit. The rms potential difference across the capacitor of 20 µF is ____ V.

A body moves on a frictionless plane starting from rest. If \(S_n\) is distance moved between t = n − 1 and t = n and \(S_{n-1}\) is distance moved between t = n − 2 and t = n − 1, then the ratio \(\frac{S_{n-1}}{S_n}\) is \(\left(1 - \frac2x\right)\) for n = 10. The value of x is ____ .

In Young's double slit experiment, carried out with light of wavelength 5000 Å, the distance between the slits is 0.3 mm and the screen is at 200 cm from the slits. The central maximum is at x = 0 cm. The value of x for third maxima is ____ mm.
questions.sol: \(x = \dfrac{3\lambda D}{d} = \dfrac{3\times5\times10^{-7}\times2}{3\times10^{-4}} = 10\) mm.

questions.q: A 2 A current carrying straight metal wire of resistance 1 Ω, resistivity \(2\times10^{-6}\) Ω m, area of cross-section 10 mm² and mass 500 g is suspended horizontally in mid air by applying a uniform magnetic field \(\vec B\). The magnitude of B is ____ \(\times10^{-1}\) T (given, g = 10 m/s²).
questions.sol: \(L = \dfrac{RA}{\rho} = \dfrac{1\times10^{-5}}{2\times10^{-6}} = 5\) m. \(BIL = mg \Rightarrow B = \dfrac{5}{2\times5} = 0.5\) T.

questions.q: Applying the principle of homogeneity of dimensions, determine which one is correct, where T is time period, G is gravitational constant, M is mass, r is radius of orbit.
questions.sol: \([GM] = [L^3T^{-2}]\), so \(\dfrac{r^3}{GM}\) has dimensions \([T^2]\): \(T^2 = \dfrac{4\pi^2r^3}{GM}\).

questions.q: A 2 kg brick begins to slide over a surface which is inclined at an angle of 45° with respect to horizontal axis. The co-efficient of static friction between their surfaces is:
questions.sol: It just begins to slide at the angle of repose: \(\mu = \tan45^\circ = 1\).

questions.q:
Match List I with List II (the phasor diagrams of List II are shown in the figure).
List I: A. Purely capacitive circuit   B. Purely inductive circuit   C. LCR series at resonance   D. LCR series circuit
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol: Capacitive: current leads voltage by 90° (I). Inductive: voltage leads by 90° (IV). Resonance: in phase (II). General LCR: phase angle \(\theta\) (III).

questions.q: Which of the diode circuits shows correct biasing used for the measurement of dynamic resistance of p-n junction diode :
questions.sol: Dynamic resistance is measured in forward bias. In (D) the long (positive) plate of the 5 V cell drives current through R into the anode of \(D_2\); in (B) the cell is reversed.

questions.q: A sample of gas at temperature T is adiabatically expanded to double its volume. Adiabatic constant for the gas is \(\gamma = 3/2\). The work done by the gas in the process is: (\(\mu\) = 1 mole)
questions.sol: \(T_2 = T\left(\tfrac12\right)^{1/2} = \dfrac{T}{\sqrt2}\). \(W = \dfrac{R(T_1 - T_2)}{\gamma - 1} = 2RT\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\right) = RT(2 - \sqrt2)\).

questions.q: The magnetic moment of a bar magnet is 0.5 A m². It is suspended in a uniform magnetic field of \(8\times10^{-2}\) T. The work done in rotating it from its most stable to most unstable position is:
questions.sol: \(W = 2mB = 2\times0.5\times8\times10^{-2} = 8\times10^{-2}\) J.

questions.q: In simple harmonic motion, the total mechanical energy of given system is E. If mass of oscillating particle P is doubled then the new energy of the system for same amplitude is:
questions.sol: \(E = \tfrac12kA^2\) does not depend on the mass: still E.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion A: Number of photons increases with increase in frequency of light.
Reason R: Maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons increases with the frequency of incident radiation.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
o: A is not correct but R is correct.
A is correct but R is not correct.
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct and R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
questions.sol: The number of photons depends on intensity, not frequency, so A is wrong; R (Einstein's equation) is right.

questions.q: A 90 kg body placed at 2R distance from surface of earth experiences gravitational pull of : (R = Radius of earth, g = 10 m s\(^{-2}\))
questions.sol: At \(r = 3R\): \(g' = \dfrac g9\). Pull \(= \dfrac{90\times10}{9} = 100\) N.

questions.q: According to Bohr's theory, the moment of momentum of an electron revolving in 4<sup>th</sup> orbit of hydrogen atom is:
questions.sol: \(L = \dfrac{nh}{2\pi} = \dfrac{4h}{2\pi} = \dfrac{2h}{\pi}\).

questions.q: A cyclist starts from the point P of a circular ground of radius 2 km and travels along its circumference to the point S. The displacement of a cyclist is:
questions.sol: P → Q → R → S is three quarters of the circle. Displacement = chord PS \(= \sqrt2\times2 = \sqrt8\) km.

questions.q: A body of m kg slides from rest along the curve of vertical circle from point A to B in frictionless path. The velocity of the body at B is: (given, R = 14 m, g = 10 m/s² and \(\sqrt2\) = 1.4)
questions.sol: Drop from A to B: \(R\sin45^\circ + R = 14(0.7 + 1) = 23.8\) m. \(v = \sqrt{2\times10\times23.8} \approx 21.8\) m/s, option (D).

questions.q: The width of one of the two slits in a Young's double slit experiment is 4 times that of the other slit. The ratio of the maximum to the minimum intensity in the interference pattern is:
questions.sol: Intensity \(\propto\) width: amplitudes in ratio 2 : 1. \(\dfrac{I_{max}}{I_{min}} = \left(\dfrac{2 + 1}{2 - 1}\right)^2 = 9\).

questions.q: The translational degrees of freedom (\(f_t\)) and rotational degrees of freedom (\(f_r\)) of CH\(_4\) molecule are:
questions.sol: CH\(_4\) is non-linear: 3 translational, 3 rotational.

questions.q: A charge q is placed at the center of one of the surfaces of a cube. The flux linked with the cube is:
questions.sol: A cube and its mirror image would enclose q; by symmetry this cube gets half: \(\dfrac{q}{2\epsilon_0}\).

questions.q: Correct formula for height of a satellite from earth's surface is :
questions.sol: \(T^2 = \dfrac{4\pi^2(R + h)^3}{gR^2} \Rightarrow h = \left(\dfrac{T^2R^2g}{4\pi^2}\right)^{1/3} - R\).

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I: The contact angle between a solid and a liquid is a property of the material of the solid and liquid as well.
Statement II: The rise of a liquid in a capillary tube does not depend on the inner radius of the tube.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
questions.sol: Contact angle depends on both materials (I true). Capillary rise \(h = \dfrac{2T\cos\theta}{r\rho g}\) depends on radius (II false).

questions.q: An electric bulb rated 50 W − 200 V is connected across a 100 V supply. The power dissipation of the bulb is:
questions.sol: \(P = 50\times\left(\dfrac{100}{200}\right)^2 = 12.5\) W.

questions.q:
Arrange the following in the ascending order of wavelength:
A. Gamma rays (\(\lambda_1\))
B. x - rays (\(\lambda_2\))
C. Infrared waves (\(\lambda_3\))
D. Microwaves (\(\lambda_4\))
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
questions.sol: Gamma < X-rays < infrared < microwaves.

questions.q: Identify the logic gate given in the circuit :
questions.sol: \(Y = \overline{\bar A\cdot\bar B} = A + B\): an OR gate.

questions.q: In a system two particles of masses \(m_1\) = 3 kg and \(m_2\) = 2 kg are placed at certain distance from each other. The particle of mass \(m_1\) is moved towards the center of mass of the system through a distance 2 cm. In order to keep the center of mass of the system at the original position, the particle of mass \(m_2\) should move towards the center of mass by the distance ____ cm.
questions.sol: \(m_1d_1 = m_2d_2\): \(3\times2 = 2d_2 \Rightarrow d_2 = 3\) cm.

questions.q: Two parallel long current carrying wires separated by a distance 2r are shown in the figure. The ratio of magnetic field at A to the magnetic field produced at C is \(\frac x7\). The value of x is ____ .
questions.sol: Both currents are upward. At A (distance r and 3r): \(B \propto \dfrac Ir + \dfrac{2I}{3r} = \dfrac{5I}{3r}\). At C (3r and r): \(\dfrac{I}{3r} + \dfrac{2I}{r} = \dfrac{7I}{3r}\). Ratio \(\dfrac57\).

questions.q: A bus moving along a straight highway with speed of 72 km/h is brought to a halt within 4 s after applying the brakes. The distance travelled by the bus during this time (Assume the retardation is uniform) is ____ m.
questions.sol: \(s = \dfrac{u + 0}{2}t = \dfrac{20}{2}\times4 = 40\) m.

questions.q: A rod of length 60 cm rotates with a uniform angular velocity 20 rad s\(^{-1}\) about its perpendicular bisector, in a uniform magnetic field 0.5 T. The direction of magnetic field is parallel to the axis of rotation. The potential difference between the two ends of the rod is ____ V.
questions.sol: Each half develops \(\tfrac12B\omega(l/2)^2\) from the centre outwards; the two ends are at the same potential: 0 V.

questions.q: The disintegration energy Q for the nuclear fission of \({}^{235}\)U → \({}^{140}\)Ce + \({}^{94}\)Zr + n is ____ MeV. Given atomic masses of \({}^{235}\)U : 235.0439 u; \({}^{140}\)Ce : 139.9054 u, \({}^{94}\)Zr : 93.9063 u; n : 1.0086 u, Value of c² = 931 MeV/u.

Mercury is filled in a tube of radius 2 cm up to a height of 30 cm. The force exerted by mercury on the bottom of the tube is ____ N. (Given, atmospheric pressure = \(10^5\) N m\(^{-2}\), density of mercury = \(1.36\times10^4\) kg m\(^{-3}\), g = 10 m s\(^{-2}\), \(\pi = \frac{22}{7}\))
questions.sol: \(P = 10^5 + 1.36\times10^4\times10\times0.3 = 1.408\times10^5\) Pa. \(F = PA = 1.408\times10^5\times\dfrac{22}{7}\times4\times10^{-4} \approx 177\) N.

questions.q: A light ray is incident on a glass slab of thickness \(4\sqrt3\) cm and refractive index \(\sqrt2\). The angle of incidence is equal to the critical angle for the glass slab with air. The lateral displacement of ray after passing through glass slab is ____ cm. (Given sin 15° = 0.25)
questions.sol: Critical angle 45° = i. \(\sin r = \dfrac{\sin45^\circ}{\sqrt2} = \dfrac12\), r = 30°. \(d = \dfrac{t\sin(i - r)}{\cos r} = \dfrac{4\sqrt3\times0.25}{\sqrt3/2} = 2\) cm.

questions.q: Two wires A and B are made up of the same material and have the same mass. Wire A has radius of 2.0 mm and wire B has radius of 4.0 mm. The resistance of wire B is 2 Ω. The resistance of wire A is ____ Ω.
questions.sol: Same mass and material: same volume, \(R \propto \dfrac{l}{A} \propto \dfrac{1}{r^4}\). \(R_A = 2\times2^4 = 32\ \Omega\).

questions.q: The displacement of a particle executing SHM is given by \(x = 10\sin\left(\omega t + \frac\pi3\right)\) m. The time period of motion is 3.14 s. The velocity of the particle at t = 0 is ____ m/s.
questions.sol: \(\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{3.14} = 2\) rad/s. \(v = A\omega\cos\dfrac\pi3 = 10\times2\times\dfrac12 = 10\) m/s.

questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor of capacitance 12.5 pF is charged by a battery connected between its plates to potential difference of 12.0 V. The battery is now disconnected and a dielectric slab (\(\epsilon_r\) = 6) is inserted between the plates. The change in its potential energy after inserting the dielectric slab is ____ \(\times10^{-12}\) J.
questions.sol: \(U_1 = \tfrac12CV^2 = 900\times10^{-12}\) J. With charge fixed, \(U_2 = \dfrac{U_1}{6} = 150\times10^{-12}\) J. Change \(= 750\times10^{-12}\) J.

questions.q: An infinitely long positively charged straight thread has a linear charge density \(\lambda\) C m\(^{-1}\). An electron revolves along a circular path having axis along the length of the wire. The graph that correctly represents the variation of the kinetic energy of electron as a function of radius of circular path from the wire is :
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{mv^2}{r} = eE = \dfrac{e\lambda}{2\pi\epsilon_0r}\), so \(\tfrac12mv^2 = \dfrac{e\lambda}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\): the KE is the same at every radius.

questions.q: An electron is projected with uniform velocity along the axis inside a current carrying long solenoid. Then :
o: the electron will experience a force at 45° to the axis and execute a helical path.
the electron will be accelerated along the axis.
the electron path will be circular about the axis.
the electron will continue to move with uniform velocity along the axis of the solenoid.
questions.sol: Inside a long solenoid \(\vec B\) is along the axis, parallel to \(\vec v\): \(\vec F = q\vec v\times\vec B = 0\). Uniform velocity.

questions.q: A metal wire of uniform mass density having length L and mass M is bent to form a semicircular arc and a particle of mass m is placed at the centre of the arc. The gravitational force on the particle by the wire is :
questions.sol: Radius \(R = \dfrac L\pi\). The arc gives \(F = \dfrac{2GMm}{\pi R^2} = \dfrac{2GMm\pi}{L^2}\).

questions.q: An effective power of a combination of 5 identical convex lenses which are kept in contact along the principal axis is 25 D. Focal length of each of the convex lens is:

Given below are two statements :
Statement I: When speed of liquid is zero everywhere, pressure difference at any two points depends on equation \(P_1 - P_2 = \rho g(h_2 - h_1)\).
Statement II: In venturi tube shown \(2gh = v_1^2 - v_2^2\)
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
o: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.sol: Statement I is hydrostatics. In the venturi \(P_1 - P_2 = \rho gh = \tfrac12\rho(v_2^2 - v_1^2)\), so \(2gh = v_2^2 - v_1^2\): Statement II has the sign wrong.

questions.q: If a rubber ball falls from a height h and rebounds upto the height of h/2. The percentage loss of total energy of the initial system as well as velocity of ball before it strikes the ground, respectively, are :
questions.sol: Energy goes from \(mgh\) to \(mg\dfrac h2\): 50% lost. Speed before impact \(\sqrt{2gh}\).

questions.q:
In an ac circuit, the instantaneous current is zero, when the instantaneous voltage is maximum. In this case, the source may be connected to :
A. pure inductor.
B. pure capacitor.
C. pure resistor.
D. combination of an inductor and capacitor.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: Current is zero at peak voltage when they are 90° apart: pure L, pure C, or an LC combination.

questions.q: Which of the following nuclear fragments corresponding to nuclear fission between neutron \(({}^1_0n)\) and uranium isotope \(({}^{235}_{92}U)\) is correct :
questions.sol: Conserve A and Z: \(236 = 144 + 89 + 3\) and \(92 = 56 + 36\). Only (D) balances.

questions.q: A body travels 102.5 m in n<sup>th</sup> second and 115.0 m in (n + 2)<sup>th</sup> second. The acceleration is :
questions.sol: \(S_{n+2} - S_n = 2a = 12.5 \Rightarrow a = 6.25\) m/s².

questions.q: In an experiment to measure focal length (f) of convex lens, the least counts of the measuring scales for the position of object (u) and for the position of image (v) are \(\Delta u\) and \(\Delta v\), respectively. The error in the measurement of the focal length of the convex lens will be:
questions.sol: \(\dfrac1f = \dfrac1v - \dfrac1u \Rightarrow \dfrac{\Delta f}{f^2} = \dfrac{\Delta u}{u^2} + \dfrac{\Delta v}{v^2}\).

questions.q: The co-ordinates of a particle moving in x-y plane are given by : \(x = 2 + 4t\), \(y = 3t + 8t^2\). The motion of the particle is :
o: uniform motion along a straight line.
uniformly accelerated having motion along a straight line.
uniformly accelerated having motion along a parabolic path.
questions.sol: \(\vec a = 16\hat j\) (constant) while \(\vec u = 4\hat i + 3\hat j\) is not along it: a parabola.

questions.q: The equation of stationary wave is : \(y = 2a\sin\left(\frac{2\pi nt}{\lambda}\right)\cos\left(\frac{2\pi x}{\lambda}\right)\). Which of the following is NOT correct :
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{nt}{\lambda}\) is dimensionless, so \(nt\) is [L], \(n\) is \([LT^{-1}]\), and \(\dfrac n\lambda\) is \([T^{-1}]\), not [T].

questions.q: Which figure shows the correct variation of applied potential difference (V) with photoelectric current (I) at two different intensities of light (\(I_1 < I_2\)) of same wavelengths :
questions.sol: Same wavelength, same stopping potential \(-V_0\) for both; the higher intensity \(I_2\) gives the larger saturation current: (C).

questions.q: P-T diagram of an ideal gas having three different densities \(\rho_1, \rho_2, \rho_3\) (in three different cases) is shown in the figure. Which of the following is correct :
questions.sol: \(P = \dfrac{\rho RT}{M}\): slope of P–T \(\propto\rho\). Steepest line \(\rho_1\), so \(\rho_1 > \rho_2 > \rho_3\).

questions.q: The electric field in an electromagnetic wave is given by \(\vec E = \hat i\,40\cos\omega(t - z/c)\) N C\(^{-1}\). The magnetic field induction of this wave is (in SI unit) :
questions.sol: \(\vec E\) along \(\hat i\), travel along \(\hat k\): \(\vec B\) along \(\hat j\) with \(B_0 = \dfrac{E_0}{c} = \dfrac{40}{c}\).

questions.q: The resistances of the platinum wire of a platinum resistance thermometer at the ice point and steam point are 8 Ω and 10 Ω respectively. After inserting in a hot bath of temperature 400°C, the resistance of platinum wire is :
The value of net resistance of the network as shown in the given figure is :
questions.sol: Current flows from −6 V to −8 V (left to right). The diode in the 10 Ω arm is forward biased; the one in the 5 Ω arm is reversed. \(15\,\|\,10 = 6\ \Omega\).

questions.q: A wooden block, initially at rest on the ground, is pushed by a force which increases linearly with time t. Which of the following curve best describes acceleration of the block with time :
questions.sol: Taking friction as negligible, \(a = \dfrac{F}{m} = \dfrac{kt}{m}\): a straight line through the origin.

questions.q: To measure the internal resistance of a battery, potentiometer is used. For R = 10 Ω, the balance point is observed at l = 500 cm and for R = 1 Ω the balance point is observed at l = 400 cm. The internal resistance of the battery is approximately :
