questions.sol: The potentiometer reads the terminal voltage \(\dfrac{\varepsilon R}{R + r}\). \(\dfrac{500}{400} = \dfrac{10(1 + r)}{10 + r} \Rightarrow r \approx 0.29 \approx 0.3\ \Omega\).

questions.q: On Celsius scale the temperature of body increases by 40°C. The increase in temperature on Fahrenheit scale is :
questions.sol: \(\Delta F = \dfrac95\times40 = 72^\circ\)F.

questions.q: A solid sphere and a hollow cylinder roll up without slipping on same inclined plane with same initial speed v. The sphere and the cylinder reach upto maximum heights \(h_1\) and \(h_2\) respectively, above the initial level. The ratio \(h_1 : h_2\) is \(\frac{n}{10}\). The value of n is ____ .
questions.sol: \(h = \dfrac{v^2}{2g}\left(1 + \dfrac{k^2}{R^2}\right)\): sphere 1.4, hollow cylinder 2. \(h_1 : h_2 = 0.7 = \dfrac{7}{10}\).

questions.q: An infinite plane sheet of charge having uniform surface charge density \(+\sigma_s\) C/m² is placed on x-y plane. Another infinitely long line charge having uniform linear charge density \(+\lambda_e\) C/m is placed at z = 4 m plane and parallel to y-axis. If the magnitude values \(|\sigma_s| = 2|\lambda_e|\) then at point (0, 0, 2), the ratio of magnitudes of electric field values due to sheet charge to that of line charge is \(\pi\sqrt n : 1\). The value of n is ____ .
questions.sol: \(E_s = \dfrac{\sigma}{2\epsilon_0}\); line at distance 2 m: \(E_l = \dfrac{\lambda}{2\pi\epsilon_0\cdot2}\). Ratio \(= \dfrac{2\pi\sigma}{\lambda} = 4\pi = \pi\sqrt{16}\).

questions.q: A hydrogen atom changes its state from n = 3 to n = 2. Due to recoil, the percentage change in the wavelength of emitted light is approximately \(1\times10^{-n}\). The value of n is ____ . [Given Rhc = 13.6 eV, hc = 1242 eV nm, h = \(6.6\times10^{-34}\) J s, mass of the hydrogen atom = \(1.6\times10^{-27}\) kg]
questions.sol: \(E = 13.6\left(\dfrac14 - \dfrac19\right) = 1.89\) eV. Recoil gives \(\dfrac{\Delta\lambda}{\lambda} \approx \dfrac{E}{2Mc^2} = \dfrac{1.89\times1.6\times10^{-19}}{2\times1.6\times10^{-27}\times9\times10^{16}} \approx 10^{-9}\), i.e. \(10^{-7}\)%.

questions.q: A soap bubble is blown to a diameter of 7 cm. 36960 erg of work is done in blowing it further. If surface tension of soap solution is 40 dyne/cm then the new radius is ____ cm. Take \(\left(\pi = \frac{22}{7}\right)\).
questions.sol: Two surfaces: \(W = 2T\cdot4\pi(R^2 - r^2)\). \(36960 = 8\times\dfrac{22}{7}\times40(R^2 - 12.25) \Rightarrow R^2 = 49\), \(R = 7\) cm.

questions.q: An elastic spring under tension of 3 N has a length a. Its length is b under tension 2 N. For its length (3a − 2b), the value of tension will be ____ N.
questions.sol: \(3 = k(a - l_0)\), \(2 = k(b - l_0)\). \(3a - 2b - l_0 = 2(a - b) + (a - l_0) = \dfrac2k + \dfrac3k = \dfrac5k\): tension 5 N.

questions.q: The magnetic field existing in a region is given by \(\vec B = 0.2(1 + 2x)\hat k\) T. A square loop of edge 50 cm carrying 0.5 A current is placed in x-y plane with its edges parallel to the x-y axes, as shown in figure. The magnitude of the net magnetic force experienced by the loop is ____ mN.
questions.sol: Forces on the horizontal sides cancel. The vertical sides differ in field by \(0.2\times2\times0.5 = 0.2\) T: \(F = IL\Delta B = 0.5\times0.5\times0.2 = 0.05\) N = 50 mN.

questions.q: Two forces \(\vec F_1\) and \(\vec F_2\) are acting on a body. One force has magnitude thrice that of the other force and the resultant of the two forces is equal to the force of larger magnitude. The angle between \(\vec F_1\) and \(\vec F_2\) is \(\cos^{-1}\left(\frac1n\right)\). The value of |n| is ____ .
questions.sol: \((3F)^2 = F^2 + 9F^2 + 6F^2\cos\theta \Rightarrow \cos\theta = -\dfrac16\), \(|n| = 6\).

questions.q: An alternating current at any instant is given by \(i = [6 + \sqrt{56}\sin(100\pi t + \pi/3)]\) A. The rms value of the current is ____ A.
Twelve wires each having resistance 2 Ω are joined to form a cube. A battery of 6 V emf is joined across point a and c. The voltage difference between e and f is ____ V.
questions.sol: Solving the cube (a at 6 V, c at 0): by symmetry b, d, e and g sit at 3 V, h at 4 V and f at 2 V. \(V_e - V_f = 1\) V.

questions.q: Two wavelengths \(\lambda_1\) and \(\lambda_2\) are used in Young's double slit experiment. \(\lambda_1\) = 450 nm and \(\lambda_2\) = 650 nm. The minimum order of fringe produced by \(\lambda_2\) which overlaps with the fringe produced by \(\lambda_1\) is n. The value of n is ____ .
questions.sol: \(n_1\times450 = n_2\times650 \Rightarrow 9n_1 = 13n_2\): smallest \(n_2 = 9\).

questions.q:
From the statements given below :
(A) The angular momentum of an electron in nth orbit is an integral multiple of \(\hbar\).
(B) Nuclear forces do not obey inverse square law.
(C) Nuclear forces are spin dependent.
(D) Nuclear forces are central and charge independent.
(E) Stability of nucleus is inversely proportional to the value of packing fraction.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: (A) is Bohr's postulate. Nuclear forces are short-range (not inverse-square) and spin dependent, and a lower packing fraction means a more stable nucleus. Nuclear forces are not central, so (D) is wrong: (A), (B), (C), (E).

questions.q: A body of mass 4 kg experiences two forces \(\vec F_1 = 5\hat i + 8\hat j + 7\hat k\) and \(\vec F_2 = 3\hat i - 4\hat j - 3\hat k\). The acceleration acting on the body is :
questions.sol: \(\vec F = 8\hat i + 4\hat j + 4\hat k\); \(\vec a = \dfrac{\vec F}{4} = 2\hat i + \hat j + \hat k\).

questions.q: Monochromatic light of frequency \(6\times10^{14}\) Hz is produced by a laser. The power emitted is \(2\times10^{-3}\) W. How many photons per second on an average, are emitted by the source ? (Given h = \(6.63\times10^{-34}\) J s)
questions.sol: \(n = \dfrac{P}{h\nu} = \dfrac{2\times10^{-3}}{6.63\times10^{-34}\times6\times10^{14}} \approx 5\times10^{15}\) per second.

questions.q: \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) are two hollow concentric cubes enclosing charges 2Q and 3Q respectively as shown in figure. The ratio of electric flux passing through \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) is :
questions.sol: \(C_1\) encloses \(2Q\); \(C_2\) encloses \(2Q + 3Q = 5Q\). Flux ratio \(2 : 5\).

questions.q: A galvanometer (G) of 2 Ω resistance is connected in the given circuit. The ratio of charge stored in \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) is :
questions.sol: In steady state current flows through 4 Ω, G (2 Ω) and 6 Ω: \(I = \dfrac{6}{12} = 0.5\) A. Taking the left node at 6 V: top node 4 V, bottom node 3 V, right node 0. \(C_1\) has 3 V (12 µC), \(C_2\) has 4 V (24 µC): ratio \(\dfrac12\).

questions.q:
Match List - I with List - II.
List I (Number)List II (Significant figure)
(A) 1001(I) 3
(B) 010.1(II) 4
(C) 100.100(III) 5
(D) 0.0010010(IV) 6
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
A big drop is formed by coalescing 1000 small droplets of water. The surface energy will become :
questions.sol: \(R = 10r\). Total area goes from \(1000\times4\pi r^2\) to \(4\pi(10r)^2 = 100\times4\pi r^2\): one-tenth.

questions.q: A cricket player catches a ball of mass 120 g moving with 25 m/s speed. If the catching process is completed in 0.1 s then the magnitude of force exerted by the ball on the hand of player will be (in SI unit) :
questions.sol: \(F = \dfrac{\Delta p}{\Delta t} = \dfrac{0.12\times25}{0.1} = 30\) N.

questions.q: In a metre-bridge when a resistance in the left gap is 2 Ω and unknown resistance in the right gap, the balance length is found to be 40 cm. On shunting the unknown resistance with 2 Ω, the balance length changes by :
questions.sol: \(\dfrac2X = \dfrac{40}{60} \Rightarrow X = 3\ \Omega\). Shunted: \(3\,\|\,2 = 1.2\ \Omega\); \(\dfrac{2}{1.2} = \dfrac{l}{100 - l} \Rightarrow l = 62.5\) cm. Change \(= 22.5\) cm.

questions.q: A diatomic gas (\(\gamma\) = 1.4) does 200 J of work when it is expanded isobarically. The heat given to the gas in the process is :
questions.sol: Isobaric: \(Q = \dfrac{\gamma}{\gamma - 1}W = 3.5\times200 = 700\) J.

questions.q: Train A is moving along two parallel rail tracks towards north with speed 72 km/h and train B is moving towards south with speed 108 km/h. Velocity of train B with respect to A and velocity of ground with respect to B are (in m s\(^{-1}\)):
questions.sol: North positive: \(v_A = 20\), \(v_B = -30\) m/s. \(v_{BA} = -50\); ground relative to B \(= 0 - (-30) = 30\) m/s.

questions.q: A light planet is revolving around a massive star in a circular orbit of radius R with a period of revolution T. If the force of attraction between planet and star is proportional to \(R^{-3/2}\) then choose the correct option :
questions.sol: \(m\omega^2R \propto R^{-3/2} \Rightarrow \omega^2 \propto R^{-5/2} \Rightarrow T^2 \propto R^{5/2}\).

questions.q: A microwave of wavelength 2.0 cm falls normally on a slit of width 4.0 cm. The angular spread of the central maxima of the diffraction pattern obtained on a screen 1.5 m away from the slit, will be :
questions.sol: First minimum: \(\sin\theta = \dfrac{\lambda}{a} = 0.5 \Rightarrow \theta = 30^\circ\). Angular spread \(2\theta = 60^\circ\).

questions.q: If the root mean square velocity of hydrogen molecule at a given temperature and pressure is 2 km/s, the root mean square velocity of oxygen at the same condition in km/s is :
questions.sol: \(v_{rms} \propto \dfrac{1}{\sqrt M}\): \(2\times\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{32}} = 0.5\) km/s.

questions.q: If frequency of electromagnetic wave is 60 MHz and it travels in air along z direction then the corresponding electric and magnetic field vectors will be mutually perpendicular to each other and the wavelength of the wave (in m) is :
questions.sol: \(\lambda = \dfrac{c}{f} = \dfrac{3\times10^8}{6\times10^7} = 5\) m.

questions.q: To measure the temperature coefficient of resistivity \(\alpha\) of a semiconductor, an electrical arrangement shown in the figure is prepared. The arm BC is made up of the semiconductor. The experiment is being conducted at 25°C and resistance of the semiconductor arm is 3 mΩ. Arm BC is cooled at a constant rate of 2°C/s. If the galvanometer G shows no deflection after 10 s, then \(\alpha\) is :
questions.sol: Balance: \(\dfrac{0.8}{R_{BC}} = \dfrac13 \Rightarrow R_{BC} = 2.4\) mΩ after cooling by 20°C. \(2.4 = 3(1 - 20\alpha)\) gives \(|\alpha| = 1\times10^{-2}\ ^\circ\)C\(^{-1}\).
questions.note: The official key gives (A). Working it out gives a magnitude of \(1\times10^{-2}\ ^\circ\)C\(^{-1}\), but the arm's resistance falls on cooling (3 → 2.4 mΩ), which strictly means a positive \(\alpha\). The question intends the semiconductor's (negative) coefficient, so (A) is the expected answer.

questions.q: Conductivity of a photodiode starts changing only if the wavelength of incident light is less than 660 nm. The band gap of photodiode is found to be \(\left(\frac X8\right)\) eV. The value of X is : (Given, h = \(6.6\times10^{-34}\) J s, e = \(1.6\times10^{-19}\) C)
questions.sol: \(E_g = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda e} = \dfrac{6.6\times10^{-34}\times3\times10^8}{660\times10^{-9}\times1.6\times10^{-19}} = 1.875 = \dfrac{15}{8}\) eV.

questions.q: A transformer has an efficiency of 80% and works at 10 V and 4 kW. If the secondary voltage is 240 V, then the current in the secondary coil is :
In an ammeter, 5% of the main current passes through the galvanometer. If resistance of the galvanometer is G, the resistance of ammeter will be :
questions.sol: Shunt \(S = \dfrac{0.05}{0.95}G = \dfrac{G}{19}\). Ammeter resistance \(G\,\|\,S = \dfrac{G}{20}\).

questions.q: A disc of radius R and mass M is rolling horizontally without slipping with speed v. It then moves up an inclined smooth surface as shown in figure. The maximum height that the disc can go up the incline is :
questions.sol: On a smooth incline friction cannot change the spin, so only the translational KE becomes height: \(h = \dfrac{v^2}{2g}\).

questions.q: A mass m is suspended from a spring of negligible mass and the system oscillates with a frequency \(f_1\). The frequency of oscillations if a mass 9m is suspended from the same spring is \(f_2\). The value of \(\frac{f_1}{f_2}\) is ____ .
questions.sol: \(f \propto \dfrac{1}{\sqrt m}\): \(\dfrac{f_1}{f_2} = \sqrt9 = 3\).

questions.q: In an electrical circuit drawn below the amount of charge stored in the capacitor is ____ µC.
questions.sol: No steady current through the capacitor branch. Current \(= \dfrac{10}{4 + 6} = 1\) A, so the capacitor has the 6 V across \(R_3\): \(Q = 10\times6 = 60\ \mu\)C.

questions.q: A particle initially at rest starts moving from reference point x = 0 along x-axis, with velocity v that varies as \(v = 4\sqrt x\) m/s. The acceleration of the particle is ____ m s\(^{-2}\).
questions.sol: \(a = v\dfrac{dv}{dx} = 4\sqrt x\times\dfrac{2}{\sqrt x} = 8\) m/s².

questions.q: Suppose a uniformly charged wall provides a uniform electric field of \(2\times10^4\) N/C normally. A charged particle of mass 2 g being suspended through a silk thread of length 20 cm and remain stayed at a distance of 10 cm from the wall. Then the charge on the particle will be \(\frac{1}{\sqrt x}\) µC where \(x\) = ____ . [use g = 10 m/s²]
questions.sol: \(\sin\theta = \dfrac{10}{20} \Rightarrow \theta = 30^\circ\). \(qE = mg\tan30^\circ \Rightarrow q = \dfrac{0.02}{\sqrt3\times2\times10^4} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}\ \mu\)C.

questions.q: A moving coil galvanometer has 100 turns and each turn has an area of 2.0 cm². The magnetic field produced by the magnet is 0.01 T and the deflection in the coil is 0.05 radian when a current of 10 mA is passed through it. The torsional constant of the suspension wire is \(x\times10^{-5}\) N m/rad. The value of \(x\) is ____ .
questions.sol: \(k = \dfrac{NIAB}{\theta} = \dfrac{100\times0.01\times2\times10^{-4}\times0.01}{0.05} = 4\times10^{-5}\) N m/rad.

questions.q: One end of a metal wire is fixed to a ceiling and a load of 2 kg hangs from the other end. A similar wire is attached to the bottom of the load and another load of 1 kg hangs from this lower wire. Then the ratio of longitudinal strain of upper wire to that of the lower wire will be ____ . [Area of cross section of wire = 0.005 cm², Y = \(2\times10^{11}\) N m\(^{-2}\) and g = 10 m s\(^{-2}\)]
questions.sol: The upper wire holds 3 kg, the lower 1 kg; identical wires, so strain ratio \(= 3\).

questions.q: In Young's double slit experiment, monochromatic light of wavelength 5000 Å is used. The slits are 1.0 mm apart and screen is placed at 1.0 m away from slits. The distance from the centre of the screen where intensity becomes half of the maximum intensity for the first time is ____ \(\times10^{-6}\) m.
questions.sol: Half intensity: \(\cos^2\dfrac\phi2 = \dfrac12 \Rightarrow \phi = \dfrac\pi2\), path difference \(\dfrac\lambda4\). \(y = \dfrac{\lambda D}{4d} = \dfrac{5\times10^{-7}}{4\times10^{-3}} = 125\times10^{-6}\) m.

questions.q: A coil of 200 turns and area 0.20 m² is rotated at half a revolution per second and is placed in uniform magnetic field of 0.01 T perpendicular to axis of rotation of the coil. The maximum voltage generated in the coil is \(\frac{2\pi}{\beta}\) volt. The value of \(\beta\) is ____ .
questions.sol: \(\omega = \pi\) rad/s. \(\varepsilon_0 = NBA\omega = 200\times0.01\times0.2\times\pi = 0.4\pi = \dfrac{2\pi}{5}\) V.

questions.q: A uniform rod AB of mass 2 kg and length 30 cm is at rest on a smooth horizontal surface. An impulse of force 0.2 N s is applied to end B. The time taken by the rod to turn through at right angles will be \(\frac{\pi}{x}\) s, where \(x\) = ____ .
questions.sol: \(\omega = \dfrac{J(L/2)}{I} = \dfrac{0.2\times0.15}{2\times0.09/12} = 2\) rad/s. Turning \(\dfrac\pi2\): \(t = \dfrac\pi4\) s.

questions.q: A particular hydrogen-like ion emits the radiation of frequency \(3\times10^{15}\) Hz when it makes transition from n = 2 to n = 1. The frequency of radiation emitted in transition from n = 3 to n = 1 is \(\frac{x}{9}\times10^{15}\) Hz, when \(x\) = ____ .

Consider a block and trolley system as shown in figure. If the coefficient of kinetic friction between the trolley and the surface is 0.04, the acceleration of the system in m s\(^{-2}\) is :
(Consider that the string is massless and unstretchable and the pulley is also massless and frictionless)

If R is the radius of the earth and the acceleration due to gravity on the surface of earth is \(g = \pi^2\) m/s², then the length of the second's pendulum at a height h = 2R from the surface of earth will be :
questions.sol: At \(h = 2R\): \(g' = \dfrac{g}{9} = \dfrac{\pi^2}{9}\). Seconds pendulum \(T = 2\) s: \(l = \dfrac{g'T^2}{4\pi^2} = \dfrac19\) m.

questions.q: 10 divisions on the main scale of a Vernier calliper coincide with 11 divisions on the Vernier scale. If each division on the main scale is of 5 units, the least count of the instrument is :
questions.sol: 1 VSD \(= \dfrac{10}{11}\) MSD. LC \(= \left(1 - \dfrac{10}{11}\right)\times5 = \dfrac{5}{11}\).

questions.q: Two moles of a monoatomic gas is mixed with six moles of a diatomic gas. The molar specific heat of the mixture at constant volume is :
questions.sol: \(C_V = \dfrac{2\times\frac32R + 6\times\frac52R}{8} = \dfrac{18R}{8} = \dfrac94R\).

questions.q: The dimensional formula of angular impulse is :
questions.sol: Angular impulse = change in angular momentum: \([ML^2T^{-1}]\).

questions.q: A monochromatic light of wavelength 6000 Å is incident on the single slit of width 0.01 mm. If the diffraction pattern is formed at the focus of the convex lens of focal length 20 cm, the linear width of the central maximum is :
questions.sol: Width \(= \dfrac{2\lambda f}{a} = \dfrac{2\times6\times10^{-7}\times0.2}{10^{-5}} = 0.024\) m = 24 mm.

questions.q: A ball of mass 0.5 kg is attached to a string of length 50 cm. The ball is rotated on a horizontal circular path about its vertical axis. The maximum tension that the string can bear is 400 N. The maximum possible value of angular velocity of the ball in rad/s is :
questions.sol: \(T = m\omega^2l \Rightarrow 400 = 0.5\times\omega^2\times0.5 \Rightarrow \omega = 40\) rad/s.

questions.q: The reading in the ideal voltmeter (V) shown in the given circuit diagram is :
questions.sol: All eight 5 V, 0.2 Ω cells are in one series loop: \(I = \dfrac{40}{1.6} = 25\) A. The voltmeter is across one cell: \(V = 5 - 25\times0.2 = 0\).

questions.q: A galvanometer has a resistance of 50 Ω and it allows maximum current of 5 mA. It can be converted into voltmeter to measure up to 100 V by connecting in series a resistor of resistance :
The minimum energy required by a hydrogen atom in ground state to emit radiation in Balmer series is nearly :
questions.sol: Balmer lines end on \(n = 2\) and start from \(n \ge 3\). Lifting the atom to \(n = 3\) needs \(13.6\left(1 - \dfrac19\right) = 12.1\) eV.

questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor has a capacitance C = 200 pF. It is connected to 230 V ac supply with an angular frequency 300 rad/s. The rms value of conduction current in the circuit and displacement current in the capacitor respectively are :
questions.sol: \(I = V\omega C = 230\times300\times200\times10^{-12} = 13.8\ \mu\)A. Displacement current equals conduction current.

questions.q: The de Broglie wavelengths of a proton and an \(\alpha\) particle are \(\lambda\) and \(2\lambda\) respectively. The ratio of the velocities of proton and \(\alpha\) particle will be :
questions.sol: \(v = \dfrac{h}{m\lambda}\): \(\dfrac{v_p}{v_\alpha} = \dfrac{m_\alpha\lambda_\alpha}{m_p\lambda_p} = 4\times2 = 8\).

questions.q:
The radius (r), length (l) and resistance (R) of a metal wire was measured in the laboratory as
r = (0.35 ± 0.05) cm
R = (100 ± 10) ohm
l = (15 ± 0.2) cm
The percentage error in resistivity of the material of the wire is :

Two identical capacitors have same capacitance C. One of them is charged to the potential V and other to the potential 2V. The negative ends of both are connected together. When the positive ends are also joined together, the decrease in energy of the combined system is :
questions.sol: \(\Delta U = \dfrac12\dfrac{C_1C_2}{C_1 + C_2}(V_1 - V_2)^2 = \dfrac12\cdot\dfrac C2\cdot V^2 = \dfrac14CV^2\).

questions.q: A simple pendulum of length 1 m has a wooden bob of mass 1 kg. It is struck by a bullet of mass \(10^{-2}\) kg moving with a speed of \(2\times10^2\) m s\(^{-1}\). The bullet gets embedded into the bob. The height to which the bob rises before swinging back is. (use g = 10 m/s²)
questions.sol: \(v = \dfrac{0.01\times200}{1.01} \approx 1.98\) m/s. \(h = \dfrac{v^2}{2g} \approx 0.20\) m.

questions.q: The pressure and volume of an ideal gas are related as \(PV^{3/2} = K\) (Constant). The work done when the gas is taken from state A(\(P_1, V_1, T_1\)) to state B(\(P_2, V_2, T_2\)) is :
questions.sol: Polytropic with \(n = \tfrac32\): \(W = \dfrac{P_1V_1 - P_2V_2}{n - 1} = 2(P_1V_1 - P_2V_2)\).

questions.q: In series LCR circuit, the capacitance is changed from C to 4C. To keep the resonance frequency unchanged, the new inductance should be:
questions.sol: \(LC\) must stay constant: \(L' = \dfrac L4\), a reduction of \(\dfrac34L\).

questions.q: A particle moving in a circle of radius R with uniform speed takes time T to complete one revolution. If this particle is projected with the same speed at an angle \(\theta\) to the horizontal, the maximum height attained by it is equal to 4R. The angle of projection \(\theta\) is then given by :
questions.sol: \(v = \dfrac{2\pi R}{T}\). \(\dfrac{v^2\sin^2\theta}{2g} = 4R \Rightarrow \sin^2\theta = \dfrac{8gR}{v^2} = \dfrac{2gT^2}{\pi^2R}\).

questions.q: With rise in temperature, the Young's modulus of elasticity :
questions.sol: Interatomic bonds weaken with temperature, so Young's modulus decreases.

questions.q: In the given circuit if the power rating of Zener diode is 10 mW, the value of series resistance \(R_s\) to regulate the input unregulated supply is :
questions.sol: \(I_L = \dfrac{5}{1000} = 5\) mA; \(I_{Z,\max} = \dfrac{10\text{ mW}}{5\text{ V}} = 2\) mA. Total current between 5 and 7 mA through 3 V: \(\dfrac37\) kΩ \(< R_s < \dfrac35\) kΩ.

questions.q: A rectangular loop of sides 12 cm and 5 cm, with its sides parallel to the x-axis and y-axis respectively, moves with a velocity of 5 cm/s in the positive x axis direction, in a space containing a variable magnetic field in the positive z direction. The field has a gradient of \(10^{-3}\) T/cm along the negative x direction and it is decreasing with time at the rate of \(10^{-3}\) T/s. If the resistance of the loop is 6 mΩ, the power dissipated by the loop as heat is ____ \(\times10^{-9}\) W.
questions.sol: Following the loop: \(\dfrac{dB}{dt} = \dfrac{\partial B}{\partial t} + v\dfrac{\partial B}{\partial x} = -10^{-3} + 0.05\times(-0.1) = -6\times10^{-3}\) T/s. \(\varepsilon = 6\times10^{-3}\times60\times10^{-4} = 3.6\times10^{-5}\) V. \(P = \dfrac{\varepsilon^2}{R} = \dfrac{1.296\times10^{-9}}{6\times10^{-3}} = 216\times10^{-9}\) W.

questions.q: A plane is in level flight at constant speed and each of its two wings has an area of 40 m². If the speed of the air is 180 km/h over the lower wing surface and 252 km/h over the upper wing surface, the mass of the plane is ____ kg. (Take air density to be 1 kg m\(^{-3}\) and g = 10 m s\(^{-2}\))

Two identical charged spheres are suspended by strings of equal lengths. The strings make an angle \(\theta\) with each other. When suspended in water the angle remains the same. If density of the material of the sphere is 1.5 g/cc, the dielectric constant of water will be ____ . (Take density of water = 1 g/cc)
questions.sol: The angle is unchanged if \(\dfrac{F}{mg}\) is unchanged: \(\dfrac{F/K}{mg(1 - \sigma/\rho)}\). So \(K = \dfrac{\rho}{\rho - \sigma} = \dfrac{1.5}{0.5} = 3\).

questions.q: A particle is moving in one dimension (along x axis) under the action of a variable force. Its initial position was 16 m right of origin. The variation of its position (x) with time (t) is given as \(x = -3t^3 + 18t^2 + 16t\), where x is in m and t is in s. The velocity of the particle when its acceleration becomes zero is ____ m/s.
The radius of a nucleus of mass number 64 is 4.8 fermi. Then the mass number of another nucleus having radius of 4 fermi is \(\frac{1000}{x}\), where \(x\) is ____ .

A regular polygon of 6 sides is formed by bending a wire of length \(4\pi\) meter. If an electric current of \(4\pi\sqrt3\) A is flowing through the sides of the polygon, the magnetic field at the centre of the polygon would be \(x\times10^{-7}\) T. The value of \(x\) is ____ .
questions.sol: Side \(a = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}\), distance to each side \(d = \dfrac{\sqrt3a}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{\sqrt3}\). \(B = 6\times\dfrac{\mu_0I}{4\pi d}(2\sin30^\circ) = \dfrac{6\times10^{-7}\times4\pi\sqrt3}{\pi/\sqrt3} = 72\times10^{-7}\) T.

questions.q: The distance between object and its 3 times magnified virtual image as produced by a convex lens is 20 cm. The focal length of the lens used is ____ cm.
questions.sol: Virtual image 3× on the same side: \(3u - u = 20 \Rightarrow u = 10\) cm, \(v = 30\) cm. \(\dfrac1f = \dfrac{1}{-30} - \dfrac{1}{-10} \Rightarrow f = 15\) cm.

questions.q: Three identical spheres each of mass 2M are placed at the corners of a right angled triangle with mutually perpendicular sides equal to 4 m each. Taking point of intersection of these two sides as origin, the magnitude of position vector of the centre of mass of the system is \(\frac{4\sqrt2}{x}\), where the value of \(x\) is ____ .
questions.sol: Masses at (0,0), (4,0), (0,4): CM \(= \left(\dfrac43, \dfrac43\right)\), \(|\vec r| = \dfrac{4\sqrt2}{3}\).

questions.q: A tuning fork resonates with a sonometer wire of length 1 m stretched with a tension of 6 N. When the tension in the wire is changed to 54 N, the same tuning fork produces 12 beats per second with it. The frequency of the tuning fork is ____ Hz.
questions.sol: Frequency \(\propto\sqrt T\): tension ×9 makes the wire's frequency \(3f\). Beats \(3f - f = 12 \Rightarrow f = 6\) Hz.

questions.q: The current in a conductor is expressed as \(I = 3t^2 + 4t^3\), where I is in Ampere and t is in second. The amount of electric charge that flows through a section of the conductor during t = 1 s to t = 2 s is ____ C.

Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Electromagnetic waves carry energy as they travel through space and this energy is equally shared by the electric and magnetic fields.
Statement II: When electromagnetic waves strike a surface, a pressure is exerted on the surface.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
o: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
questions.sol: The energy of an EM wave is shared equally between E and B, and the wave carries momentum, so it exerts pressure. Both are correct.

questions.q: Consider two physical quantities A and B related to each other as \(E = \frac{B - x^2}{At}\) where E, x and t have dimensions of energy, length and time respectively. The dimension of AB is
questions.sol: \(B\) has the dimensions of \(x^2\): \([L^2]\). \(A = \dfrac{B}{Et} = \dfrac{L^2}{ML^2T^{-2}\cdot T} = [M^{-1}T]\). \(AB = [L^2M^{-1}T]\).

questions.q: In a photoelectric effect experiment a light of frequency 1.5 times the threshold frequency is made to fall on the surface of photosensitive material. Now if the frequency is halved and intensity is doubled, the number of photo electrons emitted will be:
questions.sol: Halving gives \(0.75\nu_0\), below threshold: no electrons, whatever the intensity.

questions.q: The mass number of nucleus having radius equal to half of the radius of nucleus with mass number 192 is :
questions.sol: \(R \propto A^{1/3}\): half the radius means \(\dfrac18\) of the mass number, \(\dfrac{192}{8} = 24\).

questions.q: A uniform magnetic field of \(2\times10^{-3}\) T acts along positive Y-direction. A rectangular loop of sides 20 cm and 10 cm with current of 5 A is in Y − Z plane. The current is in anticlockwise sense with reference to negative X axis. Magnitude and direction of the torque is:
questions.sol: \(m = 5\times0.02 = 0.1\) A m², along \(-\hat i\). \(\vec\tau = \vec m\times\vec B = 0.1(-\hat i)\times2\times10^{-3}\hat j = -2\times10^{-4}\hat k\) N m.

questions.q: A block of mass 5 kg is placed on a rough inclined surface as shown in the figure. If \(\vec F_1\) is the force required to just move the block up the inclined plane and \(\vec F_2\) is the force required to just prevent the block from sliding down, then the value of \(|\vec F_1| - |\vec F_2|\) is : [Use \(g\) = 10 m/s²]
questions.sol: \(F_1 = mg\sin30^\circ + \mu mg\cos30^\circ\), \(F_2 = mg\sin30^\circ - \mu mg\cos30^\circ\). Difference \(= 2\mu mg\cos30^\circ = 2\times0.1\times50\times\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2} = 5\sqrt3\) N.

questions.q: If two vectors \(\vec A\) and \(\vec B\) having equal magnitude R are inclined at angle \(\theta\), then
questions.sol: \(|\vec A + \vec B| = \sqrt{2R^2(1 + \cos\theta)} = 2R\cos\dfrac\theta2\).

questions.q: By what percentage will the illumination of the lamp decrease if the current drops by 20%?
The speed of sound in oxygen at S.T.P. will be approximately: (given, R = 8.3 J K\(^{-1}\), \(\gamma\) = 1.4)
questions.sol: \(v = \sqrt{\dfrac{\gamma RT}{M}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1.4\times8.3\times273}{0.032}} \approx 315\) m/s.

questions.q: A light string passing over a smooth light fixed pulley connects two blocks of masses \(m_1\) and \(m_2\). If the acceleration of the system is \(g/8\), then the ratio of masses is:
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{m_1 - m_2}{m_1 + m_2} = \dfrac18 \Rightarrow \dfrac{m_1}{m_2} = \dfrac97\).

questions.q: A gas mixture consists of 8 moles of argon and 6 moles of oxygen at temperature T. Neglecting all vibrational modes, the total internal energy of the system is:
questions.sol: \(U = 8\times\dfrac32RT + 6\times\dfrac52RT = 12RT + 15RT = 27RT\).

questions.q: A small spherical ball of radius r, falling through a viscous medium of negligible density has terminal velocity 'v'. Another ball of the same mass but of radius 2r, falling through the same viscous medium will have terminal velocity:
questions.sol: Terminal speed: \(mg = 6\pi\eta rv\), so for the same mass \(v \propto \dfrac1r\): \(\dfrac v2\).

questions.q: The measured value of the length of a simple pendulum is 20 cm with 2 mm accuracy. The time for 50 oscillations was measured to be 40 seconds with 1 second resolution. From these measurements, the accuracy in the measurement of acceleration due to gravity is N%. The value of N is:
When unpolarized light is incident at an angle of 60° on a transparent medium from air, the reflected ray is completely polarized. The angle of refraction in the medium is:
questions.sol: At Brewster's angle the reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular: \(r = 90^\circ - 60^\circ = 30^\circ\).

questions.q: The resistance per centimeter of a meter bridge wire is r, with X Ω resistance in left gap. Balancing length from left end is at 40 cm with 25 Ω resistance in right gap. Now the wire is replaced by another wire of 2r resistance per centimeter. The new balancing length for same settings will be at
questions.sol: The balance point depends only on the ratio of the gap resistances, not on the wire's resistance per cm: still 40 cm.

questions.q: Force between two point charges \(q_1\) and \(q_2\) placed in vacuum at 'r' cm apart is F. Force between them when placed in a medium having dielectric constant K = 5 at 'r/5' cm apart will be:
questions.sol: \(F' = \dfrac{F}{K}\times\left(\dfrac{r}{r/5}\right)^2 = \dfrac{25F}{5} = 5F\).

questions.q: A body of mass 2 kg begins to move under the action of a time dependent force given by \(\vec F = (6t\hat i + 6t^2\hat j)\) N. The power developed by the force at the time t is given by:
questions.sol: \(\vec a = 3t\hat i + 3t^2\hat j\), \(\vec v = 1.5t^2\hat i + t^3\hat j\). \(P = \vec F\cdot\vec v = 9t^3 + 6t^5\) W.

questions.q: An AC voltage \(V = 20\sin200\pi t\) is applied to a series LCR circuit which drives a current \(I = 10\sin\left(200\pi t + \frac\pi3\right)\). The average power dissipated is:
questions.sol: \(P = \tfrac12V_0I_0\cos60^\circ = \tfrac12\times20\times10\times\tfrac12 = 50\) W.

questions.q: The mass of the moon is \(\frac{1}{144}\) times the mass of a planet and its diameter is \(\frac{1}{16}\) times the diameter of a planet. If the escape velocity on the planet is v, the escape velocity on the moon will be :
questions.sol: \(v_e \propto \sqrt{\dfrac MR}\): \(\sqrt{\dfrac{1/144}{1/16}} = \dfrac13\).

questions.q: The output of the given circuit diagram is -
questions.sol: The gates give \(Y = \overline{(A + \bar B) + (\bar A + B)}\), and \((A + \bar B) + (\bar A + B) = 1\) always, so \(Y = 0\) for every input.

questions.q: Two blocks of mass 2 kg and 4 kg are connected by a metal wire going over a smooth pulley as shown in figure. The radius of wire is \(4.0\times10^{-5}\) m and Young's modulus of the metal is \(2.0\times10^{11}\) N/m². The longitudinal strain developed in the wire is \(\frac{1}{\alpha\pi}\). The value of \(\alpha\) is ____ . [Use \(g\) = 10 m/s²]
questions.sol: \(T = \dfrac{2m_1m_2g}{m_1 + m_2} = \dfrac{80}{3}\) N. Strain \(= \dfrac{T}{\pi r^2Y} = \dfrac{80/3}{\pi\times1.6\times10^{-9}\times2\times10^{11}} = \dfrac{1}{12\pi}\).

questions.q: A body of mass 'm' is projected with a speed 'u' making an angle of 45° with the ground. The angular momentum of the body about the point of projection, at the highest point is expressed as \(\frac{\sqrt2mu^3}{Xg}\). The value of 'X' is ____ .
questions.sol: At the top \(v = \dfrac{u}{\sqrt2}\) at height \(H = \dfrac{u^2}{4g}\). \(L = mvH = \dfrac{mu^3}{4\sqrt2g} = \dfrac{\sqrt2mu^3}{8g}\).

questions.q: In the following circuit, the battery has an emf of 2 V and an internal resistance of \(\frac23\) Ω. The power consumption in the entire circuit is ____ W.
questions.sol: Between the two side wires: the top and bottom 2 Ω, and the diagonal network (2 Ω ‖ 2 Ω to the centre, then 2 Ω ‖ 2 Ω out) = 2 Ω. Three 2 Ω in parallel: \(\dfrac23\ \Omega\). \(I = \dfrac{2}{4/3} = 1.5\) A; \(P = EI = 3\) W.

questions.q: Two circular coils P and Q of 100 turns each have same radius of \(\pi\) cm. The currents in P and Q are 1 A and 2 A respectively. P and Q are placed with their planes mutually perpendicular with their centers coincide. The resultant magnetic field induction at the center of the coils is \(\sqrt x\) mT, where \(x\) = ____ . [Use \(\mu_0 = 4\pi\times10^{-7}\) T m A\(^{-1}\)]
questions.sol: Each coil: \(B = \dfrac{\mu_0NI}{2R}\): \(2\) mT (P) and \(4\) mT (Q), at right angles. \(B = \sqrt{4 + 16} = \sqrt{20}\) mT.

questions.q: Two identical spheres each of mass 2 kg and radius 50 cm are fixed at the ends of a light rod so that the separation between the centers is 150 cm. Then, moment of inertia of the system about an axis perpendicular to the rod and passing through its middle point is \(\frac{x}{20}\) kg m², where the value of \(x\) is ____ .

Light from a point source in air falls on a convex curved surface of radius 20 cm and refractive index 1.5. If the source is located at 100 cm from the convex surface, the image will be formed at ____ cm from the object.
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{1.5}{v} - \dfrac{1}{-100} = \dfrac{0.5}{20} \Rightarrow \dfrac{1.5}{v} = 0.015 \Rightarrow v = 100\) cm inside, i.e. 200 cm from the object.

questions.q: A nucleus has mass number \(A_1\) and volume \(V_1\). Another nucleus has mass number \(A_2\) and Volume \(V_2\). If relation between mass number is \(A_2 = 4A_1\), then \(\frac{V_2}{V_1}\) = ____ .
questions.sol: Nuclear volume \(\propto A\): \(\dfrac{V_2}{V_1} = 4\).

questions.q: The distance between charges +q and −q is 2l and between +2q and −2q is 4l. The electrostatic potential at point P at a distance r from center O is \(-\alpha\left[\frac{ql}{r^2}\right]\times10^9\) V, where the value of \(\alpha\) is ____ . (Use \(\frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} = 9\times10^9\) N m² C\(^{-2}\))
questions.sol: Inner pair: \(p_1 = 2ql\) towards \(+q\); outer pair: \(p_2 = 8ql\) the other way. Net \(6ql\) pointing away from the side of P. \(V = -\dfrac{k(6ql)\cos60^\circ}{r^2} = -27\dfrac{ql}{r^2}\times10^9\) V.

questions.q: The magnetic flux \(\phi\) (in weber) linked with a closed circuit of resistance 8 Ω varies with time (in seconds) as \(\phi = 5t^2 - 36t + 1\). The induced current in the circuit at t = 2 s is ____ A.
questions.sol: \(\varepsilon = -\dfrac{d\phi}{dt} = -(10t - 36) = 16\) V at \(t = 2\) s. \(I = \dfrac{16}{8} = 2\) A.

questions.q: The time period of simple harmonic motion of mass M in the given figure is \(\pi\sqrt{\frac{\alpha M}{5k}}\), where the value of \(\alpha\) is ____ .
questions.sol: Two \(k\) in parallel (\(2k\)) in series with \(k\): \(\dfrac{2k}{3}\); parallel with the single \(k\): \(\dfrac{5k}{3}\). \(T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{3M}{5k}} = \pi\sqrt{\dfrac{12M}{5k}}\).

questions.q: Four identical particles of mass m are kept at the four corners of a square. If the gravitational force exerted on one of the masses by the other masses is \(\left(\frac{2\sqrt2 + 1}{32}\right)\frac{Gm^2}{L^2}\), the length of the sides of the square is
questions.sol: Net force on a corner: \(\dfrac{Gm^2}{a^2}\left(\sqrt2 + \dfrac12\right) = \dfrac{(2\sqrt2 + 1)Gm^2}{2a^2}\). Matching \(\dfrac{2\sqrt2 + 1}{32}\dfrac{Gm^2}{L^2}\) gives \(a^2 = 16L^2\), \(a = 4L\).

questions.q: Two charges q and 3q are separated by a distance 'r' in air. At a distance x from charge q, the resultant electric field is zero. The value of x is :
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{q}{x^2} = \dfrac{3q}{(r - x)^2} \Rightarrow r - x = \sqrt3x \Rightarrow x = \dfrac{r}{1 + \sqrt3}\).

questions.q: The given figure represents two isobaric processes for the same mass of an ideal gas, then
questions.sol: On a V–T graph the slope is \(\dfrac{nR}{P}\): the steeper line (\(P_2\)) has the lower pressure, so \(P_1 > P_2\).

questions.q: In the given arrangement of a doubly inclined plane two blocks of masses M and m are placed. The blocks are connected by a light string passing over an ideal pulley as shown. The coefficient of friction between the surface of the plane and the blocks is 0.25. The value of m, for which M = 10 kg will move down with an acceleration of 2 m/s², is: (take \(g\) = 10 m/s² and \(\tan37^\circ = 3/4\))
The relation between time 't' and distance 'x' is \(t = \alpha x^2 + \beta x\), where \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are constants. The relation between acceleration (a) and velocity (v) is :
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{dt}{dx} = 2\alpha x + \beta = \dfrac1v\). Then \(\dfrac{dv}{dx} = -2\alpha v^2\) and \(a = v\dfrac{dv}{dx} = -2\alpha v^3\).

questions.q: An artillery piece of mass \(M_1\) fires a shell of mass \(M_2\) horizontally. Instantaneously after the firing, the ratio of kinetic energy of the artillery and that of the shell is:
questions.sol: Equal momenta: \(K = \dfrac{p^2}{2M}\), so \(\dfrac{K_1}{K_2} = \dfrac{M_2}{M_1}\).

questions.q: The parameter that remains the same for molecules of all gases at a given temperature is :
questions.sol: Average kinetic energy per molecule, \(\dfrac32kT\), depends only on temperature.

questions.q: A rigid wire consists of a semicircular portion of radius R and two straight sections. The wire is partially immersed in a perpendicular magnetic field \(B = B_0\hat k\) as shown in figure. The magnetic force on the wire if it has a current \(i\) is:
questions.sol: The part in the field acts like a straight wire from one leg to the other, \(2R\hat i\). \(\vec F = i(2R\hat i)\times B\hat k = -2iBR\hat j\).

questions.q: When a metal surface is illuminated by light of wavelength \(\lambda\), the stopping potential is 8 V. When the same surface is illuminated by light of wavelength \(3\lambda\), stopping potential is 2 V. The threshold wavelength for this surface is:
questions.sol: \(8e = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - \phi\), \(2e = \dfrac{hc}{3\lambda} - \phi\). Subtracting: \(\dfrac{hc}{\lambda} = 9\) eV, \(\phi = 1\) eV. Threshold \(\lambda_0 = 9\lambda\).

questions.q: The refractive index of a prism with apex angle A is \(\cot A/2\). The angle of minimum deviation is :
questions.sol: \(\cot\dfrac A2 = \dfrac{\sin\frac{A + \delta}{2}}{\sin\frac A2} \Rightarrow \dfrac{A + \delta}{2} = 90^\circ - \dfrac A2 \Rightarrow \delta = 180^\circ - 2A\).

questions.q: The fundamental frequency of a closed organ pipe is equal to the first overtone frequency of an open organ pipe. If length of the open pipe is 60 cm, the length of the closed pipe will be:
questions.sol: Open pipe first overtone \(= \dfrac{v}{0.6}\); closed fundamental \(\dfrac{v}{4L}\). Equal: \(L = 0.15\) m = 15 cm.

questions.q: If the wavelength of the first member of Lyman series of hydrogen is \(\lambda\). The wavelength of the second member will be
questions.sol: \(\dfrac1{\lambda_1} \propto \dfrac34\), \(\dfrac1{\lambda_2} \propto \dfrac89\): \(\lambda_2 = \dfrac{3/4}{8/9}\lambda = \dfrac{27}{32}\lambda\).

questions.q: A coil is placed perpendicular to a magnetic field of 5000 T. When the field is changed to 3000 T in 2 s, an induced emf of 22 V is produced in the coil. If the diameter of the coil is 0.02 m, then the number of turns in the coil is:
questions.sol: \(\varepsilon = N\pi r^2\dfrac{\Delta B}{\Delta t} = N\pi(10^{-4})(1000) = 0.314N = 22 \Rightarrow N = 70\).

questions.q: A coin is placed on a disc. The coefficient of friction between the coin and the disc is \(\mu\). If the distance of the coin from the center of the disc is r, the maximum angular velocity which can be given to the disc, so that the coin does not slip away, is :
questions.sol: \(\mu mg = m\omega^2r \Rightarrow \omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{\mu g}{r}}\).

questions.q: Two conductors have the same resistances at 0°C but their temperature coefficients of resistance are \(\alpha_1\) and \(\alpha_2\). The respective temperature coefficients for their series and parallel combinations are :
questions.sol: Series: \(R_0(1 + \alpha_1t) + R_0(1 + \alpha_2t) = 2R_0\left(1 + \dfrac{\alpha_1 + \alpha_2}{2}t\right)\). Parallel, to first order, gives the same mean: \(\dfrac{\alpha_1 + \alpha_2}{2}\) for both.

questions.q: If the percentage errors in measuring the length and the diameter of a wire are 0.1% each. The percentage error in measuring its resistance will be:
A small steel ball is dropped into a long cylinder containing glycerine. Which one of the following is the correct representation of the velocity time graph for the transit of the ball?
questions.sol: The ball speeds up and approaches its terminal velocity: graph (B).

questions.q: A force is represented by \(F = ax^2 + bt^{\frac12}\) where x = distance and t = time. The dimensions of \(b^2/a\) are:

In a plane EM wave, the electric field oscillates sinusoidally at a frequency of \(5\times10^{10}\) Hz and an amplitude of 50 V m\(^{-1}\). The total average energy density of the electromagnetic field of the wave is : [Use \(\epsilon_0 = 8.85\times10^{-12}\) C²/N m²]
questions.sol: \(u = \tfrac12\epsilon_0E_0^2 = 0.5\times8.85\times10^{-12}\times2500 \approx 1.106\times10^{-8}\) J/m³.

questions.q: Identify the logic operation performed by the given circuit.
questions.sol: Both inputs are inverted and fed to a NAND: \(\overline{\bar A\bar B} = A + B\), an OR gate.

questions.q: A solid circular disc of mass 50 kg rolls along a horizontal floor so that its center of mass has a speed of 0.4 m/s. The absolute value of work done on the disc to stop it is ____ J.
questions.sol: Rolling disc: \(K = \dfrac34mv^2 = 0.75\times50\times0.16 = 6\) J must be removed.

questions.q: An electron moves through a uniform magnetic field \(\vec B = B_0\hat i + 2B_0\hat j\) T. At a particular instant of time, the velocity of electron is \(\vec u = 3\hat i + 5\hat j\) m/s. If the magnetic force acting on electron is \(\vec F = 5e\hat k\) N, where e is the charge of electron, then the value of \(B_0\) is ____ T.
questions.sol: \(\vec F = -e(\vec u\times\vec B) = -e(6B_0 - 5B_0)\hat k = -eB_0\hat k\). \(|B_0| = 5\) T.

questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor with plate separation 5 mm is charged up by a battery. It is found that on introducing a dielectric sheet of thickness 2 mm, while keeping the battery connections intact, the capacitor draws 25% more charge from the battery than before. The dielectric constant of the sheet is ____ .
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{C'}{C} = \dfrac{5}{3 + 2/K} = 1.25 \Rightarrow 3 + \dfrac2K = 4 \Rightarrow K = 2\).

questions.q: The depth below the surface of sea to which a rubber ball be taken so as to decrease its volume by 0.02% is ____ m. (Take density of sea water = \(10^3\) kg m\(^{-3}\), Bulk modulus of rubber = \(9\times10^8\) N m\(^{-2}\), and \(g\) = 10 m s\(^{-2}\))
questions.sol: \(\rho gh = B\dfrac{\Delta V}{V} \Rightarrow h = \dfrac{9\times10^8\times2\times10^{-4}}{10^4} = 18\) m.

questions.q: A body starts falling freely from height H hits an inclined plane in its path at height h. As a result of this perfectly elastic impact, the direction of the velocity of the body becomes horizontal. The value of \(\frac Hh\) for which the body will take the maximum time to reach the ground is ____ .
questions.sol: Time \(= \sqrt{\dfrac{2(H - h)}{g}} + \sqrt{\dfrac{2h}{g}}\), largest when \(H - h = h\): \(\dfrac Hh = 2\).

questions.q: A particle performs simple harmonic motion with amplitude A. Its speed is increased to three times at an instant when its displacement is \(\frac{2A}{3}\). The new amplitude of motion is \(\frac{nA}{3}\). The value of n is ____ .
questions.sol: At \(x = \dfrac{2A}{3}\): \(v = \omega\dfrac{\sqrt5A}{3}\). New speed \(\sqrt5\omega A\): \(A'^2 = \dfrac{4A^2}{9} + 5A^2 = \dfrac{49A^2}{9}\), \(A' = \dfrac{7A}{3}\).

questions.q: The mass defect in a particular reaction is 0.4 g. The amount of energy liberated is \(n\times10^7\) kWh, where n = ____ . (speed of light = \(3\times10^8\) m/s)

A small square loop of wire of side \(l\) is placed inside a large square loop of wire of side L (\(L = l^2\)). The loops are coplanar and their centers coincide. The value of the mutual inductance of the system is \(\sqrt x\times10^{-7}\) H, where \(x\) = ____ .
questions.sol: Field at the centre of the large square \(= \dfrac{2\sqrt2\mu_0I}{\pi L}\); flux through the small loop \(= Bl^2\). \(M = \dfrac{2\sqrt2\mu_0l^2}{\pi L} = 2\sqrt2\times4\times10^{-7} = \sqrt{128}\times10^{-7}\) H (with \(L = l^2\)).

questions.q: Equivalent resistance of the following network is ____ Ω.
questions.sol: From the far end: \(6 + 2 = 8\ \Omega\), in parallel with 2 Ω: 1.6 Ω; plus 2 Ω: 3.6 Ω; in parallel with 3 Ω and 3 Ω (1.5 Ω): \(\approx 1\ \Omega\).

questions.q: Two waves of intensity ratio 1 : 9 cross each other at a point. The resultant intensities at that point, when (a) Waves are incoherent is \(I_1\) (b) Waves are coherent is \(I_2\) and differ in phase by 60°. If \(\frac{I_1}{I_2} = \frac{10}{x}\) then \(x\) = ____ .
questions.sol: Incoherent: \(I_1 = I + 9I = 10I\). Coherent at 60°: \(I_2 = 10I + 2\sqrt{9}I\cos60^\circ = 13I\). So \(x = 13\).

questions.q: If 50 Vernier divisions are equal to 49 main scale divisions of a traveling microscope and one smallest reading of main scale is 0.5 mm, the Vernier constant of traveling microscope is
An electron revolving in \(n^{th}\) Bohr orbit has magnetic moment \(\mu_n\). If \(\mu_n \propto n^x\), the value of \(x\) is
questions.sol: \(\mu = \dfrac{evr}{2}\) with \(v \propto \dfrac1n\), \(r \propto n^2\): \(\mu \propto n\).

questions.q: In the given circuit, the voltage across load resistance (\(R_L\)) is :
questions.sol: Diode drops: 0.3 V (Ge) + 0.7 V (Si). \(I = \dfrac{14}{4\ \text{k}\Omega} = 3.5\) mA; \(V_L = 3.5\times2.5 = 8.75\) V.

questions.q: An alternating voltage \(V(t) = 220\sin100\pi t\) volt is applied to a purely resistive load of 50 Ω. The time taken for the current to rise from half of the peak value to the peak value is:
questions.sol: From phase \(\dfrac\pi6\) to \(\dfrac\pi2\): \(\Delta t = \dfrac{\pi/3}{100\pi} = \dfrac{1}{300}\) s \(\approx 3.3\) ms.

questions.q: (One or more correct) Choose the correct statement for processes A & B shown in figure.
o: \(PV = k\) for process B and A.
\(\frac{P^{\gamma - 1}}{T^\gamma} = k\) for process B and \(T = k\) for process A.
\(\frac{T^\gamma}{P^{\gamma - 1}} = k\) for process A and \(PV = k\) for process B.
\(PV^\gamma = k\) for process B and \(PV = k\) for process A.
questions.sol: The flatter curve A is isothermal (\(T\), or \(PV\), constant); the steeper curve B is adiabatic (\(PV^\gamma\) constant, equivalently \(\dfrac{P^{\gamma - 1}}{T^\gamma}\) constant). Options (B) and (D) are correct.
questions.note: This is a multiple-correct question: (B) and (D) are both correct.

questions.q: A block of mass m is placed on a surface having vertical cross-section given by \(y = x^2/4\). If coefficient of friction is 0.5, the maximum height above the ground at which block can be placed without slipping is:
questions.sol: No slipping needs \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac x2 \le 0.5 \Rightarrow x \le 1\) m, so \(y_{max} = \dfrac14\) m.

questions.q: A block of ice at −10°C is slowly heated and converted to steam at 100°C. Which of the following curves represent the phenomenon qualitatively:
questions.sol: Temperature rises (ice), stays flat while melting, rises (water), then stays flat while boiling at 100°C: curve (A).

questions.q: When a potential difference V is applied across a wire of resistance R, it dissipates energy at a rate W. If the wire is cut into two halves and these halves are connected mutually parallel across the same supply, the energy dissipation rate will become:
questions.sol: Each half is \(\dfrac R2\); in parallel \(\dfrac R4\). \(P = \dfrac{V^2}{R/4} = 4W\).

questions.q:
Match List I with List II
List IList II
(A)Gauss's law of magnetostatics(I)\(\oint\vec E\cdot d\vec a = \frac{1}{\epsilon_0}\int\rho\,dV\)
(B)Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction(II)\(\oint\vec B\cdot d\vec a = 0\)
(C)Ampere's law(III)\(\oint\vec E\cdot d\vec l = -\frac{d}{dt}\int\vec B\cdot d\vec a\)
(D)Gauss's law of electrostatics(IV)\(\oint\vec B\cdot d\vec l = \mu_0I\)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol: Magnetostatics: \(\oint\vec B\cdot d\vec a = 0\) (II); Faraday: (III); Ampere: \(\oint\vec B\cdot d\vec l = \mu_0I\) (IV); electrostatics: (I).

questions.q: In a nuclear fission reaction of an isotope of mass M, three similar daughter nuclei of same mass are formed. The speed of a daughter nucleus in terms of mass defect \(\Delta M\) will be :
questions.sol: \(\Delta Mc^2 = 3\times\tfrac12\dfrac M3v^2 \Rightarrow v = c\sqrt{\dfrac{2\Delta M}{M}}\).

questions.q: For the photoelectric effect, the maximum kinetic energy (\(E_k\)) of the photoelectrons is plotted against the frequency (\(\nu\)) of the incident photons as shown in figure. The slope of the graph gives
o: Ratio of Planck's constant to electric charge
questions.sol: \(E_k = h\nu - \phi\): the slope is \(h\).

questions.q: A beam of unpolarised light of intensity \(I_0\) is passed through a polaroid A and then through another polaroid B which is oriented so that its principal plane makes an angle of 45° relative to that of A. The intensity of emergent light is:
questions.sol: After A: \(\dfrac{I_0}{2}\); after B: \(\dfrac{I_0}{2}\cos^245^\circ = \dfrac{I_0}{4}\).

questions.q: If three moles of monoatomic gas (\(\gamma = \frac53\)) is mixed with two moles of a diatomic gas (\(\gamma = \frac75\)), the value of adiabatic exponent \(\gamma\) for the mixture is
Three blocks A, B and C are pulled on a horizontal smooth surface by a force of 80 N as shown in figure. The tensions \(T_1\) and \(T_2\) in the string are respectively :

A particle of charge '\(-q\)' and mass '\(m\)' moves in a circle of radius '\(r\)' around an infinitely long line charge of linear charge density '\(+\lambda\)'. Then time period will be given as : (Consider \(k\) as Coulomb's constant)
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{2k\lambda q}{r} = \dfrac{mv^2}{r} \Rightarrow v = \sqrt{\dfrac{2k\lambda q}{m}}\). \(T = \dfrac{2\pi r}{v} = 2\pi r\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{2k\lambda q}}\).

questions.q: Escape velocity of a body from earth is 11.2 km/s. If the radius of a planet be one-third the radius of earth and mass be one-sixth that of earth, the escape velocity from the planet is :
questions.sol: \(v \propto \sqrt{\dfrac MR}\): \(11.2\sqrt{\dfrac{1/6}{1/3}} = \dfrac{11.2}{\sqrt2} \approx 7.9\) km/s.

questions.q: Projectiles A and B are thrown at angles of 45° and 60° with vertical respectively from top of a 400 m high tower. If their ranges and times of flight are same, the ratio of their speeds of projection \(v_A : v_B\) is : [Take \(g\) = 10 m s\(^{-2}\)]
questions.sol: Equal times of flight from the same height need equal vertical launch speeds, \(v_A\cos45^\circ = v_B\cos60^\circ\); equal ranges then need equal horizontal speeds too, \(v_A\sin45^\circ = v_B\sin60^\circ\). Both cannot hold, so the question was dropped.
questions.note: Bonus question: the official key dropped this question, so full marks are given to everyone. Two projectiles thrown at different angles from the same height cannot have both equal ranges and equal times of flight.
questions.val: Bonus (the data given cannot all hold together)

questions.q: If the total energy transferred to a surface in time t is \(6.48\times10^5\) J, then the magnitude of the total momentum delivered to this surface for complete absorption will be:
questions.sol: Full absorption: \(p = \dfrac Ec = \dfrac{6.48\times10^5}{3\times10^8} = 2.16\times10^{-3}\) kg m/s.

questions.q: If mass is written as \(m = kc^PG^{-1/2}h^{1/2}\) then the value of P will be : (Constants have their usual meaning with k a dimensionless constant)
questions.sol: The Planck mass is \(\sqrt{\dfrac{hc}{G}}\), so \(c\) appears to the power \(\dfrac12\).

questions.q: A block of mass 1 kg is pushed up a surface inclined to horizontal at an angle of 60° by a force of 10 N parallel to the inclined surface as shown in figure. When the block is pushed up by 10 m along inclined surface, the work done against frictional force is : [\(g\) = 10 m/s²]
questions.sol: Friction \(= \mu mg\cos60^\circ = 0.1\times10\times0.5 = 0.5\) N; work against it over 10 m \(= 5\) J.

questions.q: A big drop is formed by coalescing 1000 small identical drops of water. If \(E_1\) be the total surface energy of 1000 small drops of water and \(E_2\) be the surface energy of single big drop of water, then \(E_1 : E_2\) is \(x : 1\) where \(x\) = ____ .

A power transmission line feeds input power at 2.3 kV to a step down transformer with its primary winding having 3000 turns. The output power is delivered at 230 V by the transformer. The current in the primary of the transformer is 5 A and its efficiency is 90%. The winding of transformer is made of copper. The output current of transformer is ____ A.
A current of 5 A flows in a square loop of side 1 m placed in air. The magnetic field at the centre of the loop is \(X\sqrt2\times10^{-7}\) T. The value of X is ____ .
questions.sol: Square loop: \(B = \dfrac{2\sqrt2\mu_0I}{\pi a} = \dfrac{2\sqrt2\times4\pi\times10^{-7}\times5}{\pi\times1} = 40\sqrt2\times10^{-7}\) T.

questions.q: Two discs of moment of inertia \(I_1\) = 4 kg m² and \(I_2\) = 2 kg m², about their central axes & normal to their planes, rotating with angular speeds 10 rad/s & 4 rad/s respectively are brought into contact face to face with their axes of rotation coincident. The loss in kinetic energy of the system in the process is ____ J.
questions.sol: \(\omega = \dfrac{40 + 8}{6} = 8\) rad/s. \(KE_i = \tfrac12(4\times100 + 2\times16) = 216\) J, \(KE_f = \tfrac12\times6\times64 = 192\) J. Loss 24 J.

questions.q: A point source is emitting sound waves of intensity \(16\times10^{-8}\) W m\(^{-2}\) at the origin. The difference in intensity (magnitude only) at two points located at distances of 2 m and 4 m from the origin respectively will be ____ \(\times10^{-8}\) W m\(^{-2}\).
questions.sol: Intensity falls as \(\dfrac{1}{r^2}\), but a value 'at the origin' (the source itself) gives no finite reference, so the question was dropped.
questions.note: Bonus question: the official key dropped this question, so full marks are given to everyone. The intensity of a point source is not defined at the source itself, so the data cannot be used as given.
questions.val: Bonus (intensity at the source itself is not defined)

questions.q: Two resistances of 100 Ω and 200 Ω are connected in series with a battery of 4 V and negligible internal resistance. A voltmeter is used to measure voltage across 100 Ω resistance, which gives reading as 1 V. The resistance of voltmeter must be ____ Ω.
questions.sol: The voltmeter reads 1 V, so the 200 Ω has 3 V and the current is 15 mA. The parallel combination is \(\dfrac{1}{0.015} = 66.7\ \Omega = 100\,\|\,R_V \Rightarrow R_V = 200\ \Omega\).

questions.q: Two identical charged spheres are suspended by strings of equal lengths. The strings make an angle of 37° with each other. When suspended in a liquid of density 0.7 g/cm³, the angle remains same. If density of material of the sphere is 1.4 g/cm³, the dielectric constant of the liquid is ____ (\(\tan37^\circ = \frac34\))
questions.sol: Same angle in the liquid: \(K = \dfrac{\rho}{\rho - \sigma} = \dfrac{1.4}{1.4 - 0.7} = 2\).

questions.q: A simple pendulum is placed at a place where its distance from the earth's surface is equal to the radius of the earth. If the length of the string is 4 m, then the time period of small oscillations will be ____ s. [take \(g = \pi^2\) m s\(^{-2}\)]
questions.sol: At height R: \(g' = \dfrac g4 = \dfrac{\pi^2}{4}\). \(T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{4}{\pi^2/4}} = 8\) s.

questions.q: In an experiment to measure the focal length (\(f\)) of a convex lens, the magnitude of object distance (\(x\)) and the image distance (\(y\)) are measured with reference to the focal point of the lens. The \(y\)-\(x\) plot is shown in figure. The focal length of the lens is ____ cm.
questions.sol: Newton's form \(xy = f^2\); the curve crosses \(y = x\) at (20, 20) cm, so \(f = 20\) cm.

questions.q: A vector has magnitude same as that of \(\vec A = 3\hat i + 4\hat j\) and is parallel to \(\vec B = 4\hat i + 3\hat j\). The x and y components of this vector in first quadrant are \(x\) and 3 respectively where \(x\) = ____ .
questions.sol: Magnitude 5 along \(\dfrac{4\hat i + 3\hat j}{5}\): the vector is \(4\hat i + 3\hat j\), so \(x = 4\).

questions.q: The ratio of the magnitude of the kinetic energy to the potential energy of an electron in the 5\(^{th}\) excited state of a hydrogen atom is :
questions.sol: In any Bohr orbit \(K = -\dfrac U2\), so \(\dfrac{K}{|U|} = \dfrac12\).

questions.q: The work function of a substance is 3.0 eV. The longest wavelength of light that can cause the emission of photoelectrons from this substance is approximately;
questions.sol: \(\lambda_{max} = \dfrac{1240}{3.0} \approx 414\) nm.

questions.q: Primary coil of a transformer is connected to 220 V ac. Primary and secondary turns of the transformer are 100 and 10 respectively. Secondary coil of transformer is connected to two series resistances shown in figure. The output voltage (\(V_0\)) is :
questions.sol: Secondary: 22 V across 15 kΩ + 7 kΩ. \(V_0 = 22\times\dfrac{7}{22} = 7\) V.

questions.q: A particle of mass m is projected with a velocity 'u' making an angle of 30° with the horizontal. The magnitude of angular momentum of the projectile about the point of projection when the particle is at its maximum height h is :
questions.sol: At the top \(v = u\cos30^\circ\) horizontally at height \(h = \dfrac{u^2\sin^230^\circ}{2g} = \dfrac{u^2}{8g}\). \(L = mvh = m\dfrac{\sqrt3u}{2}\cdot\dfrac{u^2}{8g} = \dfrac{\sqrt3}{16}\dfrac{mu^3}{g}\).

questions.q: The diffraction pattern of a light of wavelength 400 nm diffracting from a slit of width 0.2 mm is focused on the focal plane of a convex lens of focal length 100 cm. The width of the 1\(^{st}\) secondary maxima will be :
questions.sol: Width of a secondary maximum \(= \dfrac{\lambda f}{a} = \dfrac{400\times10^{-9}\times1}{0.2\times10^{-3}} = 2\) mm.

questions.q: A series L.R circuit connected with an ac source \(E = (25\sin1000t)\) V has a power factor of \(\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\). If the source of emf is changed to \(E = (20\sin2000t)\) V, the new power factor of the circuit will be :
questions.sol: At \(\omega = 1000\): \(X_L = R\). Doubling \(\omega\) gives \(X_L = 2R\): \(\cos\phi = \dfrac{R}{\sqrt{R^2 + 4R^2}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt5}\).

questions.q: The electrostatic potential due to an electric dipole at a distance 'r' varies as :
questions.sol: Dipole potential \(\propto \dfrac{p\cos\theta}{r^2}\).

questions.q: A particle is placed at the point A of a frictionless track ABC as shown in figure. It is gently pushed towards right. The speed of the particle when it reaches the point B is : (Take \(g\) = 10 m/s²).
questions.sol: Drop from 1 m to 0.5 m: \(v = \sqrt{2\times10\times0.5} = \sqrt{10}\) m/s.

questions.q: Two thermodynamical processes are shown in the figure. The molar heat capacity for process A and B are \(C_A\) and \(C_B\). The molar heat capacity at constant pressure and constant volume are represented by \(C_P\) and \(C_V\), respectively. Choose the correct statement.
questions.sol: On a log P–log V plot, a line of slope \(x\) means \(PV^{-x}\) is constant, so \(C = C_V + \dfrac{R}{1 + x}\). B (slope 1): \(C_V + \dfrac R2\); A (slope \(\gamma\)): \(C_V + \dfrac{R}{1 + \gamma}\). So \(C_P > C_B > C_A > C_V\).

questions.q: The electric field of an electromagnetic wave in free space is represented as \(\vec E = E_0\cos(\omega t - kz)\hat i\). The corresponding magnetic induction vector will be :
questions.sol: \(B_0 = \dfrac{E_0}{c}\), same phase; with travel along \(+z\) and \(\vec E\) along \(\hat i\), \(\vec B\) is along \(\hat j\).

questions.q: At which temperature is the r.m.s. velocity of a hydrogen molecule equal to that of an oxygen molecule at 47°C ?
questions.sol: \(v_{rms} \propto \sqrt{T/M}\): \(\dfrac{T}{2} = \dfrac{320}{32} \Rightarrow T = 20\) K.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II.
List IList II
(A) Coefficient of viscosity(I) \([ML^2T^{-2}]\)
(B) Surface tension(II) \([ML^2T^{-1}]\)
(C) Angular momentum(III) \([ML^{-1}T^{-1}]\)
(D) Rotational kinetic energy(IV) \([ML^0T^{-2}]\)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: Viscosity \([ML^{-1}T^{-1}]\) (III); surface tension \([MT^{-2}]\) (IV); angular momentum \([ML^2T^{-1}]\) (II); rotational KE \([ML^2T^{-2}]\) (I).

questions.q: A potential divider circuit is shown in figure. The output voltage \(V_0\) is :
questions.sol: Total \(= 3300 + 7\times100 = 4000\ \Omega\), current 1 mA. \(V_0\) is across five 100 Ω resistors: \(1\text{ mA}\times500\ \Omega = 0.5\) V.

questions.q: A Zener diode of breakdown voltage 10 V is used as a voltage regulator as shown in the figure. The current through the Zener diode is :
questions.sol: Series current \(= \dfrac{20 - 10}{200} = 50\) mA; load current \(= \dfrac{10}{500} = 20\) mA; Zener current 30 mA.

questions.q: Two insulated circular loops A and B of radius 'a' carrying a current of 'I' in the anti clockwise direction as shown in the figure. The magnitude of the magnetic induction at the centre will be :
questions.sol: The two loops are perpendicular, each giving \(\dfrac{\mu_0I}{2a}\): \(B = \sqrt2\dfrac{\mu_0I}{2a} = \dfrac{\mu_0I}{\sqrt2a}\).

questions.q: All surfaces shown in figure are assumed to be frictionless and the pulleys and the string are light. The acceleration of the block of mass 2 kg is :
questions.sol: The 4 kg block hangs from a movable pulley, so \(a_{2} = 2a_{4}\). \(T - 2g\sin30^\circ = 2a\) and \(4g - 2T = 4\dfrac a2\). Solving: \(a = \dfrac g3\).

questions.q: An electric toaster has resistance of 60 Ω at room temperature (27°C). The toaster is connected to a 220 V supply. If the current flowing through it reaches 2.75 A, the temperature attained by toaster is around : (if \(\alpha = 2\times10^{-4}\)/°C)

A spherical body of mass 100 g is dropped from a height of 10 m from the ground. After hitting the ground, the body rebounds to a height of 5 m. The impulse of force imparted by the ground to the body is given by : (given, \(g\) = 9.8 m/s²)
Young's modulus of material of a wire of length 'L' and cross-sectional area A is Y. If the length of the wire is doubled and cross-sectional area is halved then Young's modulus will be :
questions.sol: Young's modulus is a property of the material, so it stays Y.

questions.q: The gravitational potential at a point above the surface of earth is \(-5.12\times10^7\) J/kg and the acceleration due to gravity at that point is 6.4 m/s². Assume that the mean radius of earth to be 6400 km. The height of this point above the earth's surface is :

The horizontal component of earth's magnetic field at a place is \(3.5\times10^{-5}\) T. A very long straight conductor carrying current of \(\sqrt2\) A in the direction from South east to North West is placed. The force per unit length experienced by the conductor is ____ \(\times10^{-6}\) N/m.
questions.sol: The wire makes 45° with the horizontal field (along N). \(\dfrac FL = IB\sin45^\circ = \sqrt2\times3.5\times10^{-5}\times\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2} = 35\times10^{-6}\) N/m.

questions.q: Two cells are connected in opposition as shown. Cell \(E_1\) is of 8 V emf and 2 Ω internal resistance; the cell \(E_2\) is of 2 V emf and 4 Ω internal resistance. The terminal potential difference of cell \(E_2\) is ____ V.
questions.sol: In opposition: \(I = \dfrac{8 - 2}{2 + 4} = 1\) A, charging \(E_2\). \(V_2 = 2 + 1\times4 = 6\) V.

questions.q: An electron of hydrogen atom in an excited state is having energy \(E_n = -0.85\) eV. The maximum number of allowed transitions to lower energy level is ____ .
questions.sol: \(-0.85\) eV is \(n = 4\): number of lines \(= \dfrac{4\times3}{2} = 6\).

questions.q: A capacitor of capacitance C and potential V has energy E. It is connected to another capacitor of capacitance 2C and potential 2 V. Then the loss of energy is \(\frac x3E\), where \(x\) is ____ .
questions.sol: Common potential \(= \dfrac{CV + 4CV}{3C} = \dfrac53V\). Initial energy \(= 9E\), final \(= \dfrac{25}{3}E\). Loss \(= \dfrac23E\).

questions.q: The distance between object and its two times magnified real image as produced by a convex lens is 45 cm. The focal length of the lens used is ____ cm.
questions.sol: Real image twice as large: \(u = 15\) cm, \(v = 30\) cm. \(\dfrac1f = \dfrac1{30} + \dfrac1{15} \Rightarrow f = 10\) cm.

questions.q: In a closed organ pipe, the frequency of fundamental note is 30 Hz. A certain amount of water is now poured in the organ pipe so that the fundamental frequency is increased to 110 Hz. If the organ pipe has a cross-sectional area of 2 cm², the amount of water poured in the organ tube is ____ g. (Take speed of sound in air is 330 m/s)

Consider a Disc of mass 5 kg, radius 2 m, rotating with angular velocity of 10 rad/s about an axis perpendicular to the plane of rotation. An identical disc is kept gently over the rotating disc along the same axis. The energy dissipated so that both the discs continue to rotate together without slipping is ____ J.
questions.sol: \(I = \tfrac12\times5\times4 = 10\) kg m². \(KE_i = \tfrac12\times10\times100 = 500\) J. Final \(\omega = 5\) rad/s: \(KE_f = \tfrac12\times20\times25 = 250\) J. Lost 250 J.

questions.q: The displacement and the increase in the velocity of a moving particle in the time interval of \(t\) to \((t + 1)\) s are 125 m and 50 m/s, respectively. The distance travelled by the particle in \((t + 2)^{th}\) s is ____ m.

Each of three blocks P, Q and R shown in figure has a mass of 3 kg. Each of the wires A and B has cross-sectional area 0.005 cm² and Young's modulus \(2\times10^{11}\) N m\(^{-2}\). Neglecting friction, the longitudinal strain on wire B is ____ \(\times10^{-4}\). (Take \(g\) = 10 m/s²)
questions.sol: \(a = \dfrac{30}{9} = \dfrac{10}{3}\) m/s². Wire B pulls P and Q: \(T = 6\times\dfrac{10}{3} = 20\) N. Strain \(= \dfrac{20}{5\times10^{-7}\times2\times10^{11}} = 2\times10^{-4}\).

questions.q: A ceiling fan having 3 blades of length 80 cm each is rotating with an angular velocity of 1200 rpm. The magnetic field of earth in that region is 0.5 G and angle of dip is 30°. The emf induced across the blades is \(N\pi\times10^{-5}\) V. The value of N is ____ .
questions.sol: \(B_V = 0.5\times10^{-4}\sin30^\circ = 0.25\times10^{-4}\) T, \(\omega = 40\pi\). \(\varepsilon = \tfrac12B_V\omega L^2 = \tfrac12\times0.25\times10^{-4}\times40\pi\times0.64 = 32\pi\times10^{-5}\) V.

questions.q: A small liquid drop of radius R is divided into 27 identical liquid drops. If the surface tension is T, then the work done in the process will be:
questions.sol: Small drops have radius \(\dfrac R3\). Extra area \(= 27\times4\pi\dfrac{R^2}{9} - 4\pi R^2 = 8\pi R^2\), so \(W = 8\pi R^2T\).

questions.q: In the given circuit, the current in resistance \(R_3\) is :
questions.sol: \(R_2\,\|\,R_3 = 2\ \Omega\); total \(2 + 2 + 1 = 5\ \Omega\), \(I = 2\) A, split equally: 1 A through \(R_3\).

questions.q: A physical quantity Q is found to depend on quantities a, b, c by the relation \(Q = \frac{a^4b^3}{c^2}\). The percentage error in a, b and c are 3%, 4% and 5% respectively. Then, the percentage error in Q is :
questions.sol: \(4\times3 + 3\times4 + 2\times5 = 34\%\).

questions.q: A stone of mass 900 g is tied to a string and moved in a vertical circle of radius 1 m making 10 rpm. The tension in the string, when the stone is at the lowest point is (if \(\pi^2\) = 9.8 and \(g\) = 9.8 m/s²) :
questions.sol: \(\omega = \dfrac{10\times2\pi}{60} = \dfrac\pi3\). \(T = m(g + \omega^2r) = 0.9\left(9.8 + \dfrac{9.8}{9}\right) = 9.8\) N.

questions.q: The truth table for this given circuit is :
questions.sol: \(Y = AB + \bar AB = B\): the output follows B.

questions.q: A bob of mass 'm' is suspended by a light string of length 'L'. It is imparted a minimum horizontal velocity at the lowest point A such that it just completes half circle reaching the top most position B. The ratio of kinetic energies \(\frac{(K.E)_A}{(K.E)_B}\) is :
questions.sol: Just completing the top: \(v_B^2 = gL\); then \(v_A^2 = 5gL\). Ratio 5 : 1.

questions.q: An electric field is given by \((6\hat i + 5\hat j + 3\hat k)\) N/C. The electric flux through a surface area \(30\hat i\) m² lying in YZ-plane (in SI unit) is :
questions.sol: \(\phi = \vec E\cdot\vec A = 6\times30 = 180\) N m²/C.

questions.q: A planet takes 200 days to complete one revolution around the Sun. If the distance of the planet from Sun is reduced to one fourth of the original distance, how many days will it take to complete one revolution :
questions.sol: \(T \propto r^{3/2}\): \(200\times\left(\dfrac14\right)^{3/2} = 25\) days.

questions.q: A wire of length L and radius r is clamped at one end. If its other end is pulled by a force F, its length increases by \(l\). If the radius of the wire and the applied force both are reduced to half of their original values keeping original length constant, the increase in length will become:
questions.sol: \(\Delta l \propto \dfrac{F}{r^2}\): \(\dfrac{1/2}{1/4} = 2\) times.

questions.q: The temperature of a gas having \(2.0\times10^{25}\) molecules per cubic meter at 1.38 atm (Given, \(k = 1.38\times10^{-23}\) J K\(^{-1}\)) is :
If the distance between object and its two times magnified virtual image produced by a curved mirror is 15 cm, the focal length of the mirror must be:
questions.sol: Virtual and magnified: concave, \(v = -2u\) on the other side. \(u = -5\) cm, \(v = +10\) cm (15 cm apart). \(\dfrac1f = \dfrac1{10} - \dfrac15 \Rightarrow f = -10\) cm.

questions.q: A plane electromagnetic wave of frequency 35 MHz travels in free space along the X-direction. At a particular point (in space and time) \(\vec E = 9.6\hat j\) V/m. The value of magnetic field at this point is :
questions.sol: \(B = \dfrac Ec = 3.2\times10^{-8}\) T; with travel along \(x\) and \(\vec E\) along \(y\), \(\vec B\) is along \(z\).

questions.q: In an a.c. circuit, voltage and current are given by: \(V = 100\sin(100t)\) V and \(I = 100\sin\left(100t + \frac\pi3\right)\) mA respectively. The average power dissipated in one cycle is:
questions.sol: \(P = \tfrac12V_0I_0\cos\phi = \tfrac12\times100\times0.1\times\cos60^\circ = 2.5\) W.

questions.q: A particle is moving in a straight line. The variation of position '\(x\)' as a function of time '\(t\)' is given as \(x = (t^3 - 6t^2 + 20t + 15)\) m. The velocity of the body when its acceleration becomes zero is :

The bob of a pendulum was released from a horizontal position. The length of the pendulum is 10 m. If it dissipates 10% of its initial energy against air resistance, the speed with which the bob arrives at the lowest point is: [Use, \(g\) : 10 m s\(^{-2}\)]
questions.sol: \(\tfrac12v^2 = 0.9\times10\times10 \Rightarrow v^2 = 180\), \(v = 6\sqrt5\) m/s.

questions.q: N moles of a polyatomic gas (\(f = 6\)) must be mixed with two moles of a monoatomic gas so that the mixture behaves as a diatomic gas. The value of N is :
questions.sol: \(C_v\) of the mix \(= \dfrac{3RN + \frac32R\cdot2}{N + 2} = \dfrac52R \Rightarrow 3N + 3 = 2.5N + 5 \Rightarrow N = 4\).

questions.q: In Young's double slit experiment, light from two identical sources are superimposing on a screen. The path difference between the two lights reaching at a point on the screen is \(7\lambda/4\). The ratio of intensity of fringe at this point with respect to the maximum intensity of the fringe is :
questions.sol: Phase \(= \dfrac{7\pi}{2}\); \(\dfrac{I}{I_{max}} = \cos^2\dfrac{7\pi}{4} = \dfrac12\).

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I : Most of the mass of the atom and all its positive charge are concentrated in a tiny nucleus and the electrons revolve around it, is Rutherford's model.
Statement II : An atom is a spherical cloud of positive charges with electrons embedded in it, is a special case of Rutherford's model.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate from the options given below
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both statement I and statement II are false
questions.sol: Statement I describes Rutherford's model correctly; Statement II is Thomson's model, not a case of Rutherford's.

questions.q: Two sources of light emit with a power of 200 W. The ratio of number of photons of visible light emitted by each source having wavelengths 300 nm and 500 nm respectively, will be :
questions.sol: \(N = \dfrac{P\lambda}{hc} \propto \lambda\): 300 : 500 = 3 : 5.

questions.q: Two particles X and Y having equal charges are being accelerated through the same potential difference. Thereafter they enter normally in a region of uniform magnetic field and describe circular paths of radii \(R_1\) and \(R_2\) respectively. The mass ratio of X and Y is :
questions.sol: \(r = \dfrac{\sqrt{2mqV}}{qB} \propto \sqrt m\), so \(\dfrac{m_X}{m_Y} = \left(\dfrac{R_1}{R_2}\right)^2\).

questions.q: In the given circuit, the current flowing through the resistance 20 Ω is 0.3 A, while the ammeter reads 0.9 A. The value of \(R_1\) is ____ Ω.
questions.sol: Voltage \(= 0.3\times20 = 6\) V; the 15 Ω branch takes 0.4 A, leaving 0.2 A for \(R_1\): \(R_1 = 30\ \Omega\).

questions.q: In the given figure, the charge stored in 6 μF capacitor, when points A and B are joined by a connecting wire is ____ μC.
questions.sol: With A and B joined, steady current flows 9 V → 6 Ω → 3 Ω → ground: 1 A, so the junction is at 3 V. The 6 μF capacitor has 6 V: \(Q = 36\ \mu\)C.

questions.q: In a single slit diffraction pattern, a light of wavelength 6000 Å is used. The distance between the first and third minima in the diffraction pattern is found to be 3 mm when the screen in placed 50 cm away from slits. The width of the slit is ____ \(\times10^{-4}\) m.
questions.sol: First to third minimum: \(\dfrac{2\lambda D}{a} = 3\) mm \(\Rightarrow a = \dfrac{2\times6\times10^{-7}\times0.5}{3\times10^{-3}} = 2\times10^{-4}\) m.

questions.q: A body of mass 5 kg moving with a uniform speed \(3\sqrt2\) m s\(^{-1}\) in X − Y plane along the line \(y = x + 4\). The angular momentum of the particle about the origin will be ____ kg m² s\(^{-1}\).
questions.sol: Distance of the line from the origin \(= \dfrac{4}{\sqrt2} = 2\sqrt2\) m. \(L = mvd = 5\times3\sqrt2\times2\sqrt2 = 60\).

questions.q: Hydrogen atom is bombarded with electrons accelerated through a potential difference of V, which causes excitation of hydrogen atoms. If the experiment is being performed at T = 0 K, the minimum potential difference needed to observe any Balmer series lines in the emission spectra will be \(\frac{\alpha}{10}\) V, where \(\alpha\) = ____ .
questions.sol: Balmer lines need excitation to \(n = 3\): \(13.6\left(1 - \dfrac19\right) = 12.09\) eV \(\approx \dfrac{121}{10}\) V.

questions.q: A simple harmonic oscillator has an amplitude A and time period \(6\pi\) second. Assuming the oscillation starts from its mean position, the time required by it to travel from \(x = A\) to \(x = \frac{\sqrt3}{2}A\) will be \(\frac\pi x\) s, where \(x\) = ____ .
questions.sol: \(\omega = \dfrac13\) rad/s. From \(A\) to \(\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}A\) the phase moves by \(\dfrac\pi6\): \(t = \dfrac{\pi/6}{1/3} = \dfrac\pi2\) s.

questions.q: Two metallic wires P and Q have same volume and are made up of same material. If their area of cross sections are in the ratio 4 : 1 and force \(F_1\) is applied to P, an extension of \(\Delta l\) is produced. The force which is required to produce same extension in Q is \(F_2\). The value of \(\frac{F_1}{F_2}\) is ____ .
questions.sol: Same volume: \(L_P : L_Q = 1 : 4\). \(F = \dfrac{YA\Delta l}{L} \propto \dfrac AL\): \(\dfrac{F_1}{F_2} = \dfrac{4/1}{1/4} = 16\).

questions.q: A particle is moving in a circle of radius 50 cm in such a way that at any instant the normal and tangential components of it's acceleration are equal. If its speed at \(t = 0\) is 4 m/s, the time taken to complete the first revolution will be \(\frac1\alpha[1 - e^{-2\pi}]\) s, where \(\alpha\) = ____ .
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{dv}{dt} = \dfrac{v^2}{R}\) gives \(v = v_0e^{s/R}\) along the path. \(t = \int\dfrac{ds}{v} = \dfrac{R}{v_0}\left(1 - e^{-s/R}\right)\); for \(s = 2\pi R\): \(t = \dfrac18\left(1 - e^{-2\pi}\right)\) s.

questions.q: A charge of 4.0 μC is moving with a velocity of \(4.0\times10^6\) m s\(^{-1}\) along the positive y axis under a magnetic field \(\vec B\) of strength \((2\hat k)\) T. The force acting on the charge is \(x\hat i\) N. The value of \(x\) is ____ .
questions.sol: \(\vec F = q\vec v\times\vec B = 4\times10^{-6}\times4\times10^6(\hat j\times2\hat k) = 32\hat i\) N.

questions.q: A horizontal straight wire 5 m long extending from east to west is falling freely at right angle to horizontal component of earths magnetic field \(0.60\times10^{-4}\) Wb m\(^{-2}\). The instantaneous value of emf induced in the wire when its velocity is 10 m s\(^{-1}\) is ____ \(\times10^{-3}\) V.
questions.sol: \(\varepsilon = Bvl = 0.6\times10^{-4}\times10\times5 = 3\times10^{-3}\) V.

questions.q: The resistance \(R = \frac VI\) where \(V = (200 \pm 5)\) V and \(I = (20 \pm 0.2)\) A, the percentage error in the measurement of R is :
The de-Broglie wavelength of an electron is the same as that of a photon. If velocity of electron is 25% of the velocity of light, then the ratio of K.E. of electron and K.E. of photon will be:
questions.sol: Equal wavelengths mean equal momentum \(p\). Electron: \(K = \dfrac{pv}{2}\); photon: \(E = pc\). Ratio \(= \dfrac{v}{2c} = \dfrac{0.25}{2} = \dfrac18\).
