questions.q: A convex mirror of radius of curvature 30 cm forms an image that is half the size of the object. The object distance is :
questions.sol: Convex: \(f = +15\) cm, \(m = \dfrac12 = -\dfrac vu \Rightarrow v = -\dfrac u2\). \(\dfrac1v + \dfrac1u = -\dfrac1u = \dfrac1{15} \Rightarrow u = -15\) cm.

questions.q: The deflection in moving coil galvanometer falls from 25 divisions to 5 divisions when a shunt of 24 Ω is applied. The resistance of galvanometer coil will be :
questions.sol: With the shunt only \(\dfrac15\) of the current passes the coil: \(I_gG = (I - I_g)S \Rightarrow G = 4\times24 = 96\ \Omega\).

questions.q: A capacitor of capacitance 100 μF is charged to a potential of 12 V and connected to a 6.4 mH inductor to produce oscillations. The maximum current in the circuit would be :
questions.sol: \(\tfrac12CV^2 = \tfrac12LI^2 \Rightarrow I = V\sqrt{\dfrac CL} = 12\sqrt{\dfrac{10^{-4}}{6.4\times10^{-3}}} = 1.5\) A.

questions.q: At what distance above and below the surface of the earth a body will have same weight. (take radius of earth as R.)
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{R^2}{(R + h)^2} = 1 - \dfrac hR\). With \(x = \dfrac hR\): \(x(1 - x - x^2) = 0 \Rightarrow x = \dfrac{\sqrt5 - 1}{2}\), so \(h = \dfrac{\sqrt5R - R}{2}\).

questions.q: A galvanometer having coil resistance 10 Ω shows a full scale deflection for a current of 3 mA. For it to measure a current of 8 A, the value of the shunt should be:
questions.sol: \(S = \dfrac{I_gG}{I - I_g} = \dfrac{3\times10^{-3}\times10}{7.997} \approx 3.75\times10^{-3}\ \Omega\).

questions.q: A thermodynamic system is taken from an original state A to an intermediate state B by a linear process as shown in the figure. Its volume is then reduced to the original value from B to C by an isobaric process. The total work done by the gas from A to B and B to C would be :
questions.sol: Pressures in dyne/cm² (1 dyne/cm² = 0.1 Pa): A→B area \(= \dfrac{800 + 400}{2}\times4 = 2400\) J; B→C: \(-400\times4 = -1600\) J. Total 800 J.

questions.q: Two charges of 5Q and −2Q are situated at the points (3a, 0) and (−5a, 0) respectively. The electric flux through a sphere of radius '4a' having center at origin is :
questions.sol: Only \(5Q\) (at 3a) is inside the sphere of radius 4a: \(\phi = \dfrac{5Q}{\epsilon_0}\).

questions.q: A biconvex lens of refractive index 1.5 has a focal length of 20 cm in air. Its focal length when immersed in a liquid of refractive index 1.6 will be:
A block of mass 100 kg slides over a distance of 10 m on a horizontal surface. If the co-efficient of friction between the surfaces is 0.4, then the work done against friction (in J) is :
questions.sol: \(W = \mu mgs = 0.4\times100\times10\times10 = 4000\) J.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I : If a capillary tube is immersed first in cold water and then in hot water, the height of capillary rise will be smaller in hot water.
Statement II : If a capillary tube is immersed first in cold water and then in hot water, the height of capillary rise will be smaller in cold water.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate from the options given below
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol: Surface tension falls as temperature rises, so the rise is smaller in hot water: I true, II false.

questions.q: If the radius of curvature of the path of two particles of same mass are in the ratio 3 : 4, then in order to have constant centripetal force, their velocities will be in the ratio of :
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{mv^2}{r}\) constant \(\Rightarrow v \propto \sqrt r\): \(\sqrt3 : 2\).

questions.q:
Match List I with List II
List-IList-II
(A)\(\oint\vec B\cdot d\vec l = \mu_0i_c + \mu_0\epsilon_0\frac{d\phi_E}{dt}\)(I)Gauss' law for electricity
(B)\(\oint\vec E\cdot d\vec l = \frac{d\phi_B}{dt}\)(II)Gauss' law for magnetism
(C)\(\oint\vec E\cdot d\vec A = \frac{Q}{\epsilon_0}\)(III)Faraday law
(D)\(\oint\vec B\cdot d\vec A = 0\)(IV)Ampere - Maxwell law
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol: A is the Ampere–Maxwell law, B Faraday's law, C Gauss's law for electricity and D Gauss's law for magnetism.

questions.q: Two vessels A and B are of the same size and are at same temperature. A contains 1 g of hydrogen and B contains 1 g of oxygen. \(P_A\) and \(P_B\) are the pressures of the gases in A and B respectively, then \(\frac{P_A}{P_B}\) is:
In the given circuit, the breakdown voltage of the Zener diode is 3.0 V. What is the value of \(I_z\) ?
questions.sol: Series current \(= \dfrac{10 - 3}{1000} = 7\) mA; load current \(= \dfrac{3}{2000} = 1.5\) mA; \(I_z = 5.5\) mA.

questions.q: A body starts moving from rest with constant acceleration covers displacement \(S_1\) in first \((p - 1)\) seconds and \(S_2\) in first \(p\) seconds. The displacement \(S_1 + S_2\) will be made in time :
questions.sol: \(S_1 + S_2 = \tfrac12a[(p - 1)^2 + p^2] = \tfrac12at^2 \Rightarrow t = \sqrt{2p^2 - 2p + 1}\) s.

questions.q: The electric current through a wire varies with time as \(I = I_0 + \beta t\), where \(I_0\) = 20 A and \(\beta\) = 3 A/s. The amount of electric charge crossed through a section of the wire in 20 s is :

The potential energy function (in J) of a particle in a region of space is given as \(U = (2x^2 + 3y^3 + 2z)\). Here x, y and z are in meter. The magnitude of x-component of force (in N) acting on the particle at point P(1, 2, 3) m is :
questions.sol: \(F_x = -\dfrac{\partial U}{\partial x} = -4x = -4\) N at \(x = 1\); magnitude 4 N.

questions.q:
The explosive in a Hydrogen bomb is a mixture of \({}_1\text{H}^2\), \({}_1\text{H}^3\) and \({}_3\text{Li}^6\) in some condensed form. The chain reaction is given by
\({}_3\text{Li}^6 + {}_0n^1 \to {}_2\text{He}^4 + {}_1\text{H}^3\)
\({}_1\text{H}^2 + {}_1\text{H}^3 \to {}_2\text{He}^4 + {}_0n^1\)
During the explosion the energy released is approximately [Given ; M(Li) = 6.01690 amu, M(\({}_1\text{H}^2\)) = 2.01471 amu, M(\({}_2\text{He}^4\)) = 4.00388 amu, and 1 amu = 931.5 MeV]

In a double slit experiment shown in figure, when light of wavelength 400 nm is used, dark fringe is observed at P. If D = 0.2 m, the minimum distance between the slits \(S_1\) and \(S_2\) is ____ mm.
questions.sol: Path difference \(= 2\left(\sqrt{D^2 + d^2} - D\right) \approx \dfrac{d^2}{D} = \dfrac\lambda2\). \(d = \sqrt{\dfrac{400\times10^{-9}\times0.2}{2}} = 2\times10^{-4}\) m = 0.20 mm.

questions.q: A cylinder is rolling down on an inclined plane of inclination 60°. Its acceleration during rolling down will be \(\frac{x}{\sqrt3}\) m/s², where \(x\) = ____ (use \(g\) = 10 m/s²).
questions.sol: Cylinder: \(a = \dfrac{g\sin60^\circ}{1 + 1/2} = \dfrac23\times10\times\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2} = \dfrac{10}{\sqrt3}\) m/s².

questions.q: An electron is moving under the influence of the electric field of a uniformly charged infinite plane sheet S having surface charge density \(+\sigma\). The electron at \(t = 0\) is at a distance of 1 m from S and has a speed of 1 m/s. The maximum value of \(\sigma\) if the electron strikes S at \(t\) = 1 s is \(\alpha\left[\frac{m\epsilon_0}{e}\right]\frac{\text{C}}{\text{m}^2}\), the value of \(\alpha\) is ____ .
questions.sol: The electron is pulled towards the sheet with \(a = \dfrac{e\sigma}{2\epsilon_0m}\). Largest \(\sigma\) when it starts moving away: \(0 = 1 + 1\cdot1 - \dfrac a2 \Rightarrow a = 4\), so \(\sigma = \dfrac{8\epsilon_0m}{e}\).

questions.q: When a hydrogen atom going from n = 2 to n = 1 emits a photon, its recoil speed is \(\frac x5\) m/s. Where \(x\) = ____ . (Use, mass of hydrogen atom = \(1.6\times10^{-27}\) kg)

A square loop of side 10 cm and resistance 0.7 Ω is placed vertically in east-west plane. A uniform magnetic field of 0.20 T is set up across the plane in north east direction. The magnetic field is decreased to zero in 1 s at a steady rate. Then, magnitude of induced emf is \(\sqrt x\times10^{-3}\) V. The value of \(x\) is ____ .
questions.sol: The loop's normal is N–S, at 45° to the field. \(\phi = 0.2\times0.01\times\cos45^\circ = \sqrt2\times10^{-3}\) Wb, removed in 1 s: \(\varepsilon = \sqrt2\times10^{-3}\) V.

questions.q: The magnetic potential due to a magnetic dipole at a point on its axis situated at a distance of 20 cm from its center is \(1.5\times10^{-5}\) T m. The magnetic moment of the dipole is ____ A m². (Given : \(\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi} = 10^{-7}\) T m A\(^{-1}\))
questions.sol: \(V = \dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\dfrac{m}{r^2} \Rightarrow m = \dfrac{1.5\times10^{-5}\times0.04}{10^{-7}} = 6\) A m².

questions.q: A 16 Ω wire is bent to form a square loop. A 9 V battery with internal resistance 1 Ω is connected across one of its sides. If a 4 μF capacitor is connected across one of its diagonals, the energy stored by the capacitor will be \(\frac x2\) μJ, where \(x\) = ____
questions.sol: Each side 4 Ω. Across the battery: 4 Ω ‖ 12 Ω = 3 Ω, \(I = \dfrac{9}{4}\) A, so 6.75 V across that side. Along the 12 Ω path the far corner sits at 2.25 V, so the diagonal has 4.5 V. \(U = \tfrac12\times4\times4.5^2 = 40.5 = \dfrac{81}{2}\ \mu\)J.

questions.q: When the displacement of a simple harmonic oscillator is one third of its amplitude, the ratio of total energy to the kinetic energy is \(\frac x8\), where \(x\) = ____ .
questions.sol: At \(x = \dfrac A3\): \(K = E\left(1 - \dfrac19\right) = \dfrac89E\), so \(\dfrac EK = \dfrac98\).

questions.q: A ball rolls off the top of a stairway with horizontal velocity u. The steps are 0.1 m high and 0.1 m wide. The minimum velocity u with which that ball just hits the step 5 of the stairway will be \(\sqrt x\) m s\(^{-1}\) where \(x\) = ____ [use \(g\) = 10 m/s²].
questions.sol: To land on step 5 it must just clear step 4: falling 0.4 m takes \(t = \sqrt{0.08}\) s while moving 0.4 m. \(u = \dfrac{0.4}{\sqrt{0.08}} = \sqrt2\) m/s.

questions.q: In a test experiment on a model aeroplane in wind tunnel, the flow speeds on the upper and lower surfaces of the wings are 70 m s\(^{-1}\) and 65 m s\(^{-1}\) respectively. If the wing area is 2 m², the lift of the wing is ____ N. (Given density of air = 1.2 kg m\(^{-3}\))

Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : In Vernier calliper if positive zero error exists, then while taking measurements, the reading taken will be more than the actual reading.
Reason (R) : The zero error in Vernier Calliper might have happened due to manufacturing defect or due to rough handling.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
o: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.sol: With a positive zero error the instrument reads more than the true value (A true). Zero errors do arise from manufacture or rough use (R true), but that does not explain A.

questions.q: A ball suspended by a thread swings in a vertical plane so that its magnitude of acceleration in the extreme position and lowest position are equal. The angle (\(\theta\)) of thread deflection in the extreme position will be :
questions.sol: Extreme: \(a = g\sin\theta\). Lowest: \(a = \dfrac{v^2}{l} = 2g(1 - \cos\theta)\). Equal: \(2\sin\frac\theta2\cos\frac\theta2 = 4\sin^2\frac\theta2 \Rightarrow \tan\frac\theta2 = \frac12\).

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : The limiting force of static friction depends on the area of contact and independent of materials.
Statement (II) : The limiting force of kinetic friction is independent of the area of contact and depends on materials.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
o: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.sol: Limiting static friction does not depend on contact area and does depend on the materials (I wrong); kinetic friction too is independent of area and depends on materials (II right).

questions.q: Primary side of a transformer is connected to 230 V, 50 Hz supply. Turns ratio of primary to secondary winding is 10 : 1. Load resistance connected to secondary side is 46 Ω. The power consumed in it is :
questions.sol: Secondary voltage \(= \dfrac{230}{10} = 23\) V. \(P = \dfrac{23^2}{46} = 11.5\) W.

questions.q: A heavy iron bar of weight 12 kg is having its one end on the ground and the other on the shoulder of a man. The rod makes an angle 60° with the horizontal, the normal force applied by the man on bar is :
questions.sol: Torque about the ground end, with the man's force perpendicular to the bar: \(N\cdot L = 12\cdot\dfrac L2\cos60^\circ \Rightarrow N = 3\) kg-wt.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : The angular speed of the moon in its orbit about the earth is more than the angular speed of the earth in its orbit about the sun.
Reason (R) : The moon takes less time to move around the earth than the time taken by the earth to move around the sun.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
o: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.sol: \(\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{T}\); the moon's period (about a month) is far shorter than a year, which is exactly why its angular speed is larger.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : The property of body, by virtue of which it tends to regain its original shape when the external force is removed, is Elasticity.
Reason (R) : The restoring force depends upon the bonded inter atomic and inter molecular force of solid.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.sol: Elasticity is the tendency to regain shape, and the restoring force comes from interatomic and intermolecular bonding: R explains A.

questions.q: The atomic mass of \({}_6\text{C}^{12}\) is 12.000000 u and that of \({}_6\text{C}^{13}\) is 13.003354 u. The required energy to remove a neutron from \({}_6\text{C}^{13}\), if mass of neutron is 1.008665 u, will be :
The threshold frequency of a metal with work function 6.63 eV is :
During an adiabatic process, the pressure of a gas is found to be proportional to the cube of its absolute temperature. The ratio of \(\frac{C_p}{C_v}\) for the gas is :
questions.sol: Adiabatic: \(P \propto T^{\gamma/(\gamma - 1)}\). \(\dfrac{\gamma}{\gamma - 1} = 3 \Rightarrow \gamma = \dfrac32\).

questions.q: A bullet is fired into a fixed target loses one third of its velocity after travelling 4 cm. It penetrates further \(D\times10^{-3}\) m before coming to rest. The value of D is :
questions.sol: \(u^2 - \dfrac49u^2 = 2a(4) \Rightarrow a = \dfrac{5u^2}{72}\). Then \(\dfrac49u^2 = 2ad \Rightarrow d = 3.2\) cm = \(32\times10^{-3}\) m.

questions.q: Three voltmeters, all having different internal resistances are joined as shown in figure. When some potential difference is applied across A and B, their readings are \(V_1\), \(V_2\) and \(V_3\). Choose the correct option.
questions.sol: \(V_1\) and \(V_2\) are in series across A and B, and \(V_3\) is directly across A and B: \(V_1 + V_2 = V_3\).

questions.q: The equation of state of a real gas is given by \(\left(P + \frac{a}{V^2}\right)(V - b) = RT\), where P, V and T are pressure, volume and temperature respectively and R is the universal gas constant. The dimensions of \(\frac{a}{b^2}\) is similar to that of :
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{a}{V^2}\) is a pressure and \(b\) a volume, so \(\dfrac{a}{b^2}\) has the dimensions of pressure.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : Work done by electric field on moving a positive charge on an equipotential surface is always zero.
Reason (R) : Electric lines of forces are always perpendicular to equipotential surfaces.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
o: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.sol: The field is perpendicular to an equipotential surface, so it does no work on a charge moving along that surface: R explains A.

questions.q: When a polaroid sheet is rotated between two crossed polaroids then the transmitted light intensity will be maximum for a rotation of :
questions.sol: \(I = \dfrac{I_0}{8}\sin^22\theta\) is largest at \(\theta = 45^\circ\).

questions.q: An object is placed in a medium of refractive index 3. An electromagnetic wave of intensity \(6\times10^8\) W/m² falls normally on the object and it is absorbed completely. The radiation pressure on the object would be (speed of light in free space = \(3\times10^8\) m/s) :
questions.sol: In the medium the wave travels at \(\dfrac c3 = 10^8\) m/s. For full absorption \(P = \dfrac Iv = \dfrac{6\times10^8}{10^8} = 6\) N/m².

questions.q: The total kinetic energy of 1 mole of oxygen at 27°C is : [Use universal gas constant (R) = 8.31 J/mole K]
questions.sol: Diatomic O\(_2\): \(K = \dfrac52RT = 2.5\times8.31\times300 = 6232.5\) J.

questions.q: The truth table of the given circuit diagram is :
questions.sol: The circuit is \(Y = A\bar B + \bar AB\) (XOR): outputs 0, 1, 1, 0.

questions.q: A current of 200 μA deflects the coil of a moving coil galvanometer through 60°. The current to cause deflection through \(\frac{\pi}{10}\) radian is :
questions.sol: Deflection \(\propto\) current: \(\dfrac{\pi/10}{\pi/3}\times200 = 60\ \mu\)A.

questions.q: Wheatstone bridge principle is used to measure the specific resistance (\(S_1\)) of given wire, having length L, radius r. If X is the resistance of wire, then specific resistance is; \(S_1 = X\left(\frac{\pi r^2}{L}\right)\). If the length of the wire gets doubled then the value of specific resistance will be :
questions.sol: Specific resistance is a property of the material, so it stays \(S_1\).

questions.q: A closed organ pipe 150 cm long gives 7 beats per second with an open organ pipe of length 350 cm, both vibrating in fundamental mode. The velocity of sound is ____ m/s.
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{v}{4\times1.5} - \dfrac{v}{2\times3.5} = 7 \Rightarrow \dfrac{v}{42} = 7 \Rightarrow v = 294\) m/s.

questions.q: A series LCR circuit with \(L = \frac{100}{\pi}\) mH, \(C = \frac{10^{-3}}{\pi}\) F and R = 10 Ω, is connected across an ac source of 220 V, 50 Hz supply. The power factor of the circuit would be ____ .
questions.sol: \(X_L = 2\pi\times50\times\dfrac{0.1}{\pi} = 10\ \Omega\); \(X_C = \dfrac{1}{2\pi\times50\times10^{-3}/\pi} = 10\ \Omega\). Resonance, so the power factor is 1.

questions.q: Two charges of \(-4\ \mu\)C and \(+4\ \mu\)C are placed at the points A(1, 0, 4) m and B(2, −1, 5) m located in an electric field \(\vec E = 0.20\hat i\) V/cm. The magnitude of the torque acting on the dipole is \(8\sqrt\alpha\times10^{-5}\) N m, where \(\alpha\) = ____ .
questions.sol: \(\vec d = (1, -1, 1)\) m, \(\vec E = 20\hat i\) V/m. \(\tau = q|\vec d\times\vec E| = 4\times10^{-6}\times20\times|(0, 1, 1)| = 8\sqrt2\times10^{-5}\) N m.

questions.q: A ring and a solid sphere roll down the same inclined plane without slipping. They start from rest. The radii of both bodies are identical and the ratio of their kinetic energies is \(\frac x7\), where \(x\) is ____ .
questions.sol: Starting from the same height, each body's kinetic energy at the bottom equals \(mgh\); for equal masses the ratio is \(1 = \dfrac77\).

questions.q: A body falling under gravity covers two points A and B separated by 80 m in 2 s. The distance of upper point A from the starting point is ____ m (use \(g\) = 10 m s\(^{-2}\)).
questions.sol: \(80 = 2u + \tfrac12\times10\times4 \Rightarrow u = 30\) m/s at A. Height fallen to A \(= \dfrac{30^2}{20} = 45\) m.

questions.q: The electric potential at the surface of an atomic nucleus (\(z = 50\)) of radius \(9\times10^{-13}\) cm is ____ \(\times10^6\) V.
questions.sol: \(V = \dfrac{kZe}{R} = \dfrac{9\times10^9\times50\times1.6\times10^{-19}}{9\times10^{-15}} = 8\times10^6\) V.

questions.q: The magnetic field at the centre of a wire loop formed by two semicircular wires of radii \(R_1 = 2\pi\) m and \(R_2 = 4\pi\) m, carrying current I = 4 A as per figure given below is \(\alpha\times10^{-7}\) T. The value of \(\alpha\) is ____ . (Centre O is common for all segments)
questions.sol: Each semicircle gives \(\dfrac{\mu_0I}{4R}\): \(2\times10^{-7}\) T (R\(_1\)) and \(1\times10^{-7}\) T (R\(_2\)), in the same direction: \(3\times10^{-7}\) T.

questions.q: A parallel beam of monochromatic light of wavelength 5000 Å is incident normally on a single narrow slit of width 0.001 mm. The light is focused by convex lens on screen, placed on its focal plane. The first minima will be formed for the angle of diffraction of ____ (degree).
questions.sol: \(\sin\theta = \dfrac\lambda a = \dfrac{5\times10^{-7}}{10^{-6}} = 0.5 \Rightarrow \theta = 30^\circ\).

questions.q: The reading of pressure metre attached with a closed pipe is \(4.5\times10^4\) N/m². On opening the valve, water starts flowing and the reading of pressure metre falls to \(2.0\times10^4\) N/m². The velocity of water is found to be \(\sqrt V\) m/s. The value of V is ____ .
questions.sol: \(\tfrac12\rho v^2 = (4.5 - 2.0)\times10^4 \Rightarrow v^2 = 50\).

questions.q: If Rydberg's constant is R, the longest wavelength of radiation in Paschen series will be \(\frac{\alpha}{7R}\), where \(\alpha\) = ____ .
questions.sol: \(\dfrac1\lambda = R\left(\dfrac19 - \dfrac1{16}\right) = \dfrac{7R}{144}\), so \(\lambda = \dfrac{144}{7R}\).

questions.q: Position of an ant (S in metres) moving in Y-Z plane is given by \(S = 2t^2\hat j + 5\hat k\) (where \(t\) is in second). The magnitude and direction of velocity of the ant at \(t\) = 1 s will be :
questions.sol: \(\vec v = \dfrac{d\vec S}{dt} = 4t\hat j\): at \(t = 1\) s, 4 m/s along \(y\).

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : Viscosity of gases is greater than that of liquids.
Statement (II) : Surface tension of a liquid decreases due to the presence of insoluble impurities.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
o: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.sol: Liquids are far more viscous than gases (I wrong). Impurities that do not dissolve lower the surface tension (II right).

questions.q: If the refractive index of the material of a prism is \(\cot\left(\frac A2\right)\), where \(A\) is the angle of prism then the angle of minimum deviation will be
questions.sol: \(\cot\dfrac A2 = \dfrac{\sin\frac{A + \delta}{2}}{\sin\frac A2} \Rightarrow \sin\dfrac{A + \delta}{2} = \cos\dfrac A2 \Rightarrow \dfrac{A + \delta}{2} = \dfrac\pi2 - \dfrac A2 \Rightarrow \delta = \pi - 2A\).

questions.q:
A proton moving with a constant velocity passes through a region of space without any change in its velocity. If \(\vec E\) and \(\vec B\) represent the electric and magnetic fields respectively, then the region of space may have :
(A) E = 0, B = 0
(B) E = 0, B ≠ 0
(C) E ≠ 0, B = 0
(D) E ≠ 0, B ≠ 0
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: Unchanged velocity is possible with no fields, with only B parallel to the velocity, or with crossed E and B balancing. E alone always accelerates a proton.

questions.q: The acceleration due to gravity on the surface of earth is \(g\). If the diameter of earth reduces to half of its original value and mass remains constant, then acceleration due to gravity on the surface of earth would be :
questions.sol: \(g = \dfrac{GM}{R^2}\): halving \(R\) gives \(4g\).

questions.q: A train is moving with a speed of 12 m/s on rails which are 1.5 m apart. To negotiate a curve of radius 400 m, the height by which the outer rail should be raised with respect to the inner rail is (Given, \(g\) = 10 m/s²) :
questions.sol: \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{v^2}{rg} = \dfrac{144}{4000}\); \(h = d\tan\theta = 1.5\times0.036 = 0.054\) m = 5.4 cm.

questions.q: Which of the following circuits is reverse - biased?
questions.sol: In (D) the anode is at +2 V and the cathode at +4 V: the diode is reverse biased. In the others the p-side is at the higher potential.

questions.q: Identify the physical quantity that cannot be measured using spherometer :
o: Radius of curvature of concave surface
Radius of curvature of convex surface
questions.sol: A spherometer measures small thicknesses and radii of curvature; specific rotation needs a polarimeter.

questions.q: Two bodies of mass 4 g and 25 g are moving with equal kinetic energies. The ratio of magnitude of their linear momentum is :
questions.sol: \(p = \sqrt{2mK}\) with equal \(K\): \(\dfrac{p_1}{p_2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{4}{25}} = \dfrac25\).

questions.q: 0.08 kg air is heated at constant volume through 5°C. The specific heat of air at constant volume is 0.17 kcal/kg°C and J = 4.18 joule/cal. The change in its internal energy is approximately.
questions.sol: \(\Delta U = mc_v\Delta T = 0.08\times0.17\times5 = 0.068\) kcal \(= 68\times4.18 \approx 284\) J.

questions.q: The radius of third stationary orbit of electron for Bohr's atom is R. The radius of fourth stationary orbit will be:
A rectangular loop of length 2.5 m and width 2 m is placed at 60° to a magnetic field of 4 T. The loop is removed from the field in 10 s. The average emf induced in the loop during this time is
questions.sol: Flux \(= BA\cos60^\circ = 4\times5\times0.5 = 10\) Wb, falling to zero in 10 s: \(\varepsilon = -\dfrac{\Delta\phi}{\Delta t} = +1\) V.

questions.q: An electric charge \(10^{-6}\ \mu\)C is placed at origin (0, 0) m of X − Y co-ordinate system. Two points P and Q are situated at \((\sqrt3, \sqrt3)\) m and \((\sqrt6, 0)\) m respectively. The potential difference between the points P and Q will be :
questions.sol: Both points are \(\sqrt6\) m from the charge, so they are at the same potential: 0 V.

questions.q: A convex lens of focal length 40 cm forms an image of an extended source of light on a photoelectric cell. A current I is produced. The lens is replaced by another convex lens having the same diameter but focal length 20 cm. The photoelectric current now is :
questions.sol: The same diameter collects the same light power, so the photocurrent stays I.

questions.q: A body of mass 1000 kg is moving horizontally with a velocity 6 m/s. If 200 kg extra mass is added, the final velocity (in m/s) is:
questions.sol: Momentum is conserved: \(6000 = 1200v \Rightarrow v = 5\) m/s.

questions.q: A plane electromagnetic wave propagating in x-direction is described by \(E_y = (200\text{ V m}^{-1})\sin[1.5\times10^7t - 0.05x]\); The intensity of the wave is : (Use \(\epsilon_0 = 8.85\times10^{-12}\) C² N\(^{-1}\) m\(^{-2}\))
questions.sol: \(I = \tfrac12c\epsilon_0E_0^2 = 0.5\times3\times10^8\times8.85\times10^{-12}\times4\times10^4 \approx 53.1\) W/m².

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : Planck's constant and angular momentum have same dimensions.
Statement (II) : Linear momentum and moment of force have same dimensions.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
o: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol: \(h\) and \(L\) are both J s (I true). Momentum is kg m/s, torque is N m (II false).

questions.q: A wire of length 10 cm and radius \(\sqrt7\times10^{-4}\) m is connected across the right gap of a meter bridge. When a resistance of 4.5 Ω is connected on the left gap by using a resistance box, the balance length is found to be at 60 cm from the left end. If the resistivity of the wire is \(R\times10^{-7}\) Ω m, then value of R is :
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{4.5}{X} = \dfrac{60}{40} \Rightarrow X = 3\ \Omega\). \(\rho = \dfrac{XA}{L} = \dfrac{3\times\pi\times7\times10^{-8}}{0.1} = 66\times10^{-7}\ \Omega\) m.

questions.q: A wire of resistance R and length L is cut into 5 equal parts. If these parts are joined parallely, then resultant resistance will be :
questions.sol: Each part is \(\dfrac R5\); five in parallel give \(\dfrac{R}{25}\).

questions.q: The average kinetic energy of a monatomic molecule is 0.414 eV at temperature : (Use \(K_B = 1.38\times10^{-23}\) J/mol − K)
questions.sol: \(\dfrac32kT = 0.414\times1.6\times10^{-19} \Rightarrow T = \dfrac{6.62\times10^{-20}}{2.07\times10^{-23}} \approx 3200\) K.

questions.q: A particle starts from origin at \(t = 0\) with a velocity \(5\hat i\) m/s and moves in \(x - y\) plane under action of a force which produces a constant acceleration of \((3\hat i + 2\hat j)\) m/s². If the \(x\)-coordinate of the particle at that instant is 84 m, then the speed of the particle at this time is \(\sqrt\alpha\) m/s. The value of \(\alpha\) is ____ .

A thin metallic wire having cross sectional area of \(10^{-4}\) m² is used to make a ring of radius 30 cm. A positive charge of \(2\pi\) C is uniformly distributed over the ring, while another positive charge of 30 pC is kept at the centre of the ring. The tension in the ring is ____ N; provided that the ring does not get deformed (neglect the influence of gravity). (given, \(\frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} = 9\times10^9\) SI units)
questions.sol: For a ring of charge \(q\) with \(Q\) at the centre, \(T = \dfrac{kqQ}{2\pi r^2} = \dfrac{9\times10^9\times2\pi\times30\times10^{-12}}{2\pi\times0.09} = 3\) N.

questions.q: Two coils have mutual inductance 0.002 H. The current changes in the first coil according to the relation \(i = i_0\sin\omega t\), where \(i_0\) = 5 A and \(\omega = 50\pi\) rad/s. The maximum value of emf in the second coil is \(\frac\pi\alpha\) V. The value of \(\alpha\) is ____ .
questions.sol: \(\varepsilon_{max} = Mi_0\omega = 0.002\times5\times50\pi = \dfrac\pi2\) V, so \(\alpha = 2\).

questions.q: Two immiscible liquids of refractive indices \(\frac85\) and \(\frac32\) respectively are put in a beaker as shown in the figure. The height of each column is 6 cm. A coin is placed at the bottom of the beaker. For near normal vision, the apparent depth of the coin is \(\frac\alpha4\) cm. The value of \(\alpha\) is ____ .

In a nuclear fission process, a high mass nuclide (\(A \approx 236\)) with binding energy 7.6 MeV/Nucleon dissociated into middle mass nuclides (\(A \approx 118\)), having binding energy of 8.6 MeV/Nucleon. The energy released in the process would be ____ MeV.

Four particles each of mass 1 kg are placed at four corners of a square of side 2 m. Moment of inertia of system about an axis perpendicular to its plane and passing through one of its vertex is ____ kg m².
questions.sol: About one corner the other masses are at 2, 2 and \(2\sqrt2\) m: \(I = 4 + 4 + 8 = 16\) kg m².

questions.q: A particle executes simple harmonic motion with an amplitude of 4 cm. At the mean position, velocity of the particle is 10 cm/s. The distance of the particle from the mean position when its speed becomes 5 cm/s is \(\sqrt\alpha\) cm, where \(\alpha\) = ____ .

Two long, straight wires carry equal currents in opposite directions as shown in figure. The separation between the wires is 5.0 cm. The magnitude of the magnetic field at a point P midway between the wires is ____ μT (Given : \(\mu_0 = 4\pi\times10^{-7}\) T m A\(^{-1}\))
questions.sol: At P the fields of opposite currents add: \(B = 2\times\dfrac{\mu_0I}{2\pi(0.025)} = 2\times\dfrac{2\times10^{-7}\times10}{0.025} = 160\ \mu\)T.

questions.q: The charge accumulated on the capacitor connected in the following circuit is ____ μC (Given C = 150 μF)
questions.sol: \(V_A = 10\times\dfrac{2}{1 + 2} = 6.67\) V and \(V_B = 10\times\dfrac{4}{6 + 4} = 4\) V above the bottom. \(Q = 150\ \mu\text{F}\times\dfrac83\text{ V} = 400\ \mu\)C.

questions.q: If average depth of an ocean is 4000 m and the bulk modulus of water is \(2\times10^9\) N m\(^{-2}\), then fractional compression \(\frac{\Delta V}{V}\) of water at the bottom of ocean is \(\alpha\times10^{-2}\). The value of \(\alpha\) is ____ (Given, \(g\) = 10 m s\(^{-2}\), \(\rho\) = 1000 kg m\(^{-3}\))
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{\Delta V}{V} = \dfrac{\rho gh}{B} = \dfrac{1000\times10\times4000}{2\times10^9} = 2\times10^{-2}\).
